input_text: 后汉以给边将，和帝时，万人将军得用之。 魏晋以来，二十八解不复具存，用者有《黄鹄》、《陇头》、《出关》、《入关》、《出塞》、《入塞》、《折杨柳》、《黄覃子》、《赤之杨》、《望行人》十曲。 案魏晋之世，有孙氏善弘旧曲，宋识善击节唱和，陈左善清歌，列和善吹笛，郝索善弹筝，硃生善琵琶，尤发新声。 故傅玄著书曰： 人若钦所闻而忽所见，不亦惑乎？ 设此六人生于上世，越今古而无俪，何但夔牙同契哉！ 案此说，则自兹以后，皆孙硃等之遗则也。 相和，汉旧歌也，丝竹更相和，执节者歌。 本一部，魏明帝分为二，更递夜宿。 本十七曲，硃生、宋职、列和等复合之为十三曲。 但歌，四曲，出自汉世。 无弦节，作伎最先唱，一人唱，三人和。 魏武帝尤好之。
target_text: Drum and horn horizontal blowing music is discussed, with the drum used to promote military affairs and the horn to ward off enemies. The music evolved from Hu music, with Zhang Bowang transmitting playing skills to Xijing. During the Wei and Jin Dynasties, only ten songs were used, such as "Huang Hu" and "Longtou." The Song of Harmony is an old song from the Mo Dynasty, with silk and bamboo overlapping to harmonize. Originally one part, Emperor Wei Ming divided it into two parts. There are four Danges from the Han Dynasty, with no string accompaniment, and the lead singer sings first. Since the Jin Dynasty, this music has been extinct.

input_text: 《长史变》者，司徒左长史王廞临败所制。 凡此诸曲，始皆徒歌，即而被之管弦。 又有因丝竹金石，造歌以被之，魏世三调歌辞之类是也。 《杯柈舞》，案太康中天下为《晋世宁舞》，务手以接杯柈反覆之。 此则汉世惟有柈舞，而晋加之以杯，反覆之也。 《公莫舞》，今之《巾舞》也。 相传云项庄剑舞，项伯以袖隔之，使不得害汉高祖，且语项庄云 公莫 ！ 古人相呼曰公，言公莫害汉王也。 今之用巾盖像项伯衣袖之遗式。 然案《琴操》有《公莫渡河曲》，然则其声所从来已久，俗云项伯，非也。 《白纟宁舞》，案舞辞有巾袍之言。 纟宁本吴地所出，宜是吴舞也。 晋《俳歌》又云： 皎皎白绪，节节为双。 吴音呼绪为纟宁，疑白纟宁即白绪也。《铎舞歌》一篇，《幡舞歌》一篇，《鼓舞伎》六曲，并陈于元会。 后汉正旦，天子临德阳殿受朝贺，舍利从西方来，戏于殿前，激水化成比目鱼，跳跃嗽水，作雾翳日。 毕，又化成龙，长八九丈，出水游戏，炫耀日光。 以两大丝绳系两柱头，相去数丈，两倡女对舞，行于绳上，相逢切肩而不倾。 魏晋讫江左，犹有《夏育扛鼎》、《巨象行乳》、《神龟抃舞》、《背负灵岳》、《桂树白雪》、《画地成川》之乐。 成帝咸康七年，尚书蔡谟奏： 八年正会仪注，惟作鼓吹钟鼓，其余伎乐尽不作。 侍中张澄、给事黄门侍郎陈逵驳，以为 王者观时设教，至于吉凶殊断，不易之道也。
target_text: Wu songs and miscellaneous songs come from south of the Yangtze River, with songs like "Midnight Song," "Phoenix General's Young Song," and "Qianxi Song" composed by various individuals. Cup Loop Dance and "Gong Mo Wu" are also described, with the latter associated with Xiang Zhuang and Xiang Bo. Bai Yu Wu and other dances are mentioned, with lyrics and performances presented at New Year's Day gatherings. In the seventh year of Emperor Cheng's reign, Shangshu Cai Mo wrote about the use of music, with debates on whether to play bells and drums. Eventually, some acrobatic music was abolished, but later restored.

input_text: 《传》曰： 听之不聪，是谓不谋，厥咎急，厥罚恆寒，厥极贫。 时则有鼓妖，时则有鱼孽，时则有豕祸，时则有耳痾，时则有黑眚黑祥。 惟火沴水。 听之不聪，是谓不谋，言上偏听不聪，下情隔塞，则谋虑利害，失在严急，故其咎急也。 盛冬日短，寒以杀物，政促迫，故其罚常寒也。 寒则不生百谷，上下俱贫，故其极贫也。 君严猛而闭下，臣战栗而塞耳，则妄闻之气发于音声，故有鼓妖。 寒气动，故有鱼孽。 而龟能为孽，龟能陆处，非极阴也，鱼去水而死，极阴之薛也。 于《易》，《坎》为水，为豕，豕大耳而不聪察，听气毁，故有豕祸也。 一曰，寒岁豕多死及为怪，亦是也。 及人，则多病耳者，故有耳痾。 水色黑，故有黑眚黑祥。 凡听伤者，病水敢；水气病，则火沴之。 其极贫者，顺之，其福曰富。 刘歆《听传》曰有介虫之孽也。
target_text: Various calamities and portents, linking them to failures in the five behaviors of a ruler: appearance, speech, sight, hearing, and thought. A failure in hearing, described as "hearing but not hearing," is called "not planning." This occurs when a superior's will is blocked from subordinates, leading to impatience. The punishment for this is continuous cold, which prevents grain growth and results in poverty. Associated portents include drum monsters, fish evils, pig troubles, ear diseases, and black disasters. The text explains that cold air causes fish evils, and pigs, associated with water in the "Yi," suffer when the spirit of hearing is damaged. The color of water is black, hence black disasters. This condition is described as fire overcoming water.

input_text: 案刘向说，近水沴水，听之不聪之罚也。 京房《易传》曰： 君淫于色，贤人潜，国家危，厥异水流赤。 穆帝升平三年二月，凉州城东池中有火。 四年四月，姑臧泽水中又有火。 此火沴水之妖也。 明年，张天锡杀中护军张邕。 邕，执政之人也。 安帝元兴二年十月，钱唐临平湖水赤，桓玄讽吴郡使言开除以为己瑞，俄而桓玄败。 《传》曰： 思心之不容，是谓不圣，厥咎，厥罚恆风，厥极凶短折。 时则有脂夜之妖，时则有华孽，时则有牛祸，时则有心腹之痾，时则有黄眚黄祥，时则有金木水火沴土。 思心不容，是谓不圣。 思心者，心思虑也。 容，宽也。孔子曰： 居上不宽，吾何以观之哉！ 言上不宽大包容，臣下则不能居圣位。 貌言视听，以心为主，四进皆失，则区无识，故其咎也。 雨旱寒燠，亦以风为本，四气皆乱，故其罚恆风也。
target_text: A failure in thought, described as "the mind and heart not allowing," is called "unholiness." This means a ruler is not tolerant, preventing subordinates from holding virtuous positions. The disaster is dark weather, and the punishment is continuous wind, which harms all things and leads to early death. Associated portents include the demon of fat night, flower evils, cow troubles, strange illnesses among close friends, and yellow disasters. The text notes that cows have large hearts but cannot think, so they suffer when heart energy is damaged. The color of earth is yellow, hence yellow disasters. This condition is described as metal, wood, water, and fire overcoming earth.

input_text: 《传》曰： 皇之不极，是谓不建，厥咎眊，厥罚恆阴，厥极弱。 时则有射妖，时则有龙蛇之孽，时则有马祸，时则有下人伐上之痾，时则有日月乱行，星辰逆行。 皇之不极，是谓不建。 皇，君；极，中；建，立也。 人君貌言视听思心五事皆失，不得其中，不能立万事，失在眊悖，故其咎眊也。 王者自下承天理物。 云起于山，而弥于天；天气乱，故其罚恆阴，一曰： 上失中，则下强盛而蔽君明也。 《易》曰： 亢龙有悔，贵而亡位，高而亡民，贤人在下位而亡辅。 如此，则君有南面之尊，而亡一人之助，故其极弱也。 盛阳动进轻疾。 礼，春而大射，以顺阳气。 上微弱则下奋惊动，故有射妖。
target_text: A failure in speech and action, described as "words and deeds being inappropriate," is called "being unable to achieve success." The punishment is a long period of cloudy weather, and in the extreme, the country becomes weak. Associated portents include shooting demons, monsters like dragons and snakes, horse troubles, and the disadvantage of subordinates attacking superiors. The text explains that if the upper level is weak, the lower level will be alarmed, causing shooting demons. Yin Qi moving causes dragon and snake evils. The horse, associated with the king in the "Yi," suffers when the monarch's spirit is damaged. The text states that when the ruler's way is damaged, the sun and moon move out of order and stars go retrograde.

input_text: 庶征之恆寒，刘歆以为大雨雪，及未当雨雪而雨雪，及大雨雹，陨霜杀菽草，皆恆寒之罚也。 京房《易传》曰： 有德遭险兹谓逆命，厥异寒。 诛罚过深，当燠而寒，尽六日，亦为雹。 害正不诛兹谓养贼，寒七十二日，杀飞禽。 道人始去兹谓伤，其寒，物无霜而死，涌水而出。 战不量敌帮兹谓辱命，其寒，虽雨物不茂。 闻善不予，厥咎聋。 吴孙权嘉禾三年九月朔，陨霜伤谷。 案刘向说，诛罚不由君出，在臣下之象也 。 是时，校事吕壹专作威福，与汉元帝时石显用事陨霜同应。 班固书九月二日，陈寿言朔，皆明未可以伤谷也。 壹后亦伏诛。 京房《易传》曰： 兴兵妄诛兹谓亡法，厥灾霜，夏杀五谷，冬杀麦。 诛不原情兹谓不仁，其霜，夏先大雷风，冬先雨，乃陨霜，有芒角。 贤圣遭害，其霜附木不下地。 佞人依刑兹谓私贼，其霜在草根土隟间。 不教而诛兹谓虐，其霜反在草下。
target_text: The text provides numerous historical examples of these portents. For continuous cold, it cites heavy snow, unseasonable frost, and hail, linking them to harsh punishments, framing of loyal officials, and unjust killings. Examples include frost damaging grains in the third year of Jiahe of Wu Sun Quan, and heavy snow in the fourth year of Chiwu. For continuous wind, it records strong winds overturning houses and breaking trees, linking them to ignorant and arbitrary rule, as during the reign of King Zhengshi of Wei Qi. Earthquakes are extensively documented, attributed to the power of subordinates and the disorder of yin and yang, with examples from the reigns of Sun Quan, Emperor Wu of Jin, and Emperor Hui.

input_text: 鱼孽魏齐王嘉平四年五月，有二鱼集于武库屋上，此鱼孽也。 王肃曰： 鱼生于水，而亢于屋，介鳞之物，失其所也。 边将其殆有弃甲之变乎！ 后果有东关之败。 干宝又以为高贵乡公兵祸之应。 二说皆与班固旨同。 武帝太康中，有鲤鱼二见武库屋上。 干宝以为： 武库兵府，鱼有鳞甲，亦兵类也。 鱼既极阴，屋上太阳，鱼见屋上，象至阴以兵革之祸干太阳也。 至惠帝初，诛杨骏，废太后，矢交馆阁。 元康末，贾后谤杀太子，寻亦诛废。 十年之间，母后之难再兴，是其应也，自是祸乱构矣。 京房《易传》曰： 鱼去水，飞入道路，兵且作。 蝗虫《春秋》，螽。 刘歆从介虫之孽，与鱼同占。 魏文帝黄初三年七月，冀州大蝗，人饥。 案蔡邕说， 蝗者，在上贪苛之所致也 。
target_text: The text also records instances of fish falling on arsenal roofs, interpreted as a sign of war, and locust plagues, linked to the lord's greed and harshness. Pig disasters, such as wild boars entering military camps, are seen as portents of failure and emptiness. Black and yellow mists are recorded as signs of impending doom or usurpation. Landslides and ground collapses are interpreted as signs of the emperor's way collapsing and the people losing favor. The appearance of dragons in wells is considered a bad omen, indicating that the ruler's virtue is at odds with fate. Finally, the text records numerous human anomalies, such as women turning into men, the dead coming back to life, and births of monstrous children, all interpreted as signs of social and political disorder, with subordinates overtaking superiors.

input_text: 夫性灵之表，不知所以发于咏歌；感动之端，不知所以关于手足。 生于心者谓之道，成于形者谓之用。 譬诸天地，其犹影响，百兽率舞，而况于人乎！美其和平而哀其丧乱，以兹援律，乃播其声焉。 农瑟羲琴，倕钟和磬，达灵成性，象物昭功，由此言之，其来自远。 殷氏不纲，遗风馀孽，淫奏既兴，雅章奔散，《英》《茎》之制，盖已微矣。 孔子曰： 人能弘道，非道弘人。 周始二《南》，《风》兼六代。 昔黄帝作《云门》，尧作《咸池》，舜作《大韶》，禹作《大夏》，殷作《大濩》，周作《大武》，所谓因前王之礼，设俯仰之容，和顺积中，英华发外。 《书》称命夔典乐，教胄子，则《周官》所谓奏大吕，歌黄钟。 天贶来下，人祗动色，抑扬周监，以弘雅音。
target_text: The history of music and ritual in China from ancient times to the Jin Dynasty, emphasizing their spiritual and emotional significance. Spirituality and emotion are expressed through chanting and physical movement, with the heart's essence called Tao and its reflection in images called Yong. Music is used to spread sound, praise peace, and mourn chaos. Ancient sages like Shennong and Fuxi created instruments such as harps, bells, and chimes to express the soul and imitate nature. The Yin Shang Dynasty saw a decline in elegant music due to obscene influences, leading to the loss of works like "Five Heroes" and "Six Stems." Confucius remarked that people can promote Tao, but Tao cannot promote people.

input_text: 及褒艳兴灾，平王逢乱，礼废亲疏，乐沈河海。 是以延陵季子闻歌《小雅》曰： 其周德之衰乎！犹有先王之遗风焉。 而列壤称孤，各兴吟咏。 魏文侯聆古乐而恐卧，晋平公听新声而忘食，先王之道，渐以陵夷。 八方殊风，九州异则。 秦氏并吞，遂专刑宪，至于弦歌《诗》《颂》，干戚旄羽，投诸烟火，扫地无遗。 汉祖提剑寰中，削平天下，文匪躬于德化，武有心于制作。 太后摈儒家之道，大臣排贾氏之言，搢绅先生所以长叹，而子政、仲舒犹不能已也。 炎汉中兴，明皇帝即位，表圭景而陈《清庙》，树槐阴而疏璧流；祀光武于明堂，以配上帝；召桓荣于太学，袒而割牲；济济焉，皇皇焉，有足观者。
target_text: From the Zhou Dynasty onward, various rulers composed music, including the Yellow Emperor's "Yunmen," Yao's "Xianchi," and others. The text describes how music and ritual were used to educate and govern, with the "Shang Shu" and "Zhou Guan" referencing the teaching of music to noble children. However, during the reign of King Ping, etiquette was destroyed, and elegant music was lost. Yanling Jizi noted that the Zhou Dynasty's decline still retained the legacy of previous kings. As nations rose, they created their own music, leading to a gradual decline in the way of kings. The Qin Dynasty unified the world but destroyed all musical works and instruments. The Han Dynasty revived music and ritual under Emperors Gaozu, Wen, and Wu, though Confucianism was abandoned. Emperor Ming of the Han Dynasty further promoted rituals and music, establishing a pagoda market and performing ceremonies in the Mingtang.

input_text: 汉自东京大乱，绝无金石之乐，乐章亡缺，不可复知。 及魏武平荆州，获汉雅乐郎河南杜夔，能识旧法，以为军谋祭酒，使创定雅乐。 时又有散骑侍郎邓静、尹商善训雅乐，歌师尹胡能歌宗庙郊祀之曲，舞师冯肃、服养晓知先代诸舞，夔悉总领之。 远详经籍，近采故事，考会古乐，始设轩悬钟磬。 而黄初中柴玉、左延年之徒，复以新声被宠，改其声韵。 及武帝受命之初，百度草创。 泰始二年，诏郊祀明堂礼乐权用魏仪，遵周室肇称殷礼之义，但改乐章而已，使傅玄为之词云。 祀天地五郊夕牲歌 天命有晋，穆穆明明。 我其夙夜，祗事上灵。 常于时假，迄用其成。 于荐玄牡，进夕其牲。
target_text: The text details various types of music, including great music for the world, sacrificial music for ancestral temples, and ceremonial music for different occasions. It explains the five tones (palace, shang, jiao, zheng, yu) and their associations with virtues and emotions, as well as the eight sounds (stone, leather, bamboo, wood, silk, earth, metal) and their corresponding winds. The twelve pitches (six yang and six yin) are linked to the twelve months and their characteristics. After the Han Dynasty's chaos, music was scattered. Emperor Wu of Wei appointed Du Kui to create Yale, but new music later changed its charm. Emperor Wu of Jin initially based rituals on the Wei Dynasty, with Fu Xuan composing lyrics for various sacrifices, including songs for heaven and earth, the five suburbs, and ancestral temples.

input_text: 及太和中，左延年改夔《驺虞》、《伐檀》、《文王》三曲，更自作声节，其名虽存，而声实异。 唯因夔《鹿鸣》，全不改易。 每正旦大会，太尉奉璧，群后行礼，东厢雅乐常作者是也。 后又改三篇之行礼诗。 第一日《于赫篇》，咏武帝，声节与古《鹿鸣》同。 第二曰《巍巍篇》，咏文帝，用延年所改《驺虞》声。 第三日《洋洋篇》，咏明帝，用延年所改《文王》声。 第四曰复用《鹿鸣》。 《鹿鸣》之声重用，而除古《伐檀》。 及晋初，食举亦用《鹿鸣》。 至泰始五年，尚书奏，使太仆傅玄、中书监荀勖、黄门侍郎张华各造正旦行礼及王公上寿酒、食举乐歌诗。 荀勖云： 魏氏行礼、食举，再取周诗《鹿鸣》以为乐章。 又《鹿鸣》以宴嘉宾，无取于朝，考之旧闻，未知所应。 勖乃除《鹿鸣》旧歌更作行礼诗四篇，先陈三朝朝宗之义。 又为正旦大会、王公上寿歌诗并食举乐歌诗，合十三篇。 又以魏氏歌诗或二言，或三言，或四言，或五言，与古诗不类，以问司律中郎将陈颀。 颀曰： 被之金石，未必皆当。 故勖造晋歌，皆为四言，唯王公上寿酒一篇为三言五言焉。 张华以为 魏上寿、食举诗及汉氏所施用，其文句长短不齐，未皆合古。 盖以依咏弦节，本有因循，而识乐知音，足以制声度曲，法用率非凡近之所能改。 二代三京，袭而不变，虽诗章辞异，兴废随时，至其韵逗留曲折，皆系于旧，有由然也。
target_text: The text includes numerous songs and poems used in rituals, such as those for the first day of the first lunar month, sacrifices to heaven and earth, and ancestral temple ceremonies. It describes the evolution of music under different rulers, including the adaptation of old melodies by Zuo Yannian and the creation of new songs by Xun Xu and Zhang Hua. Xun Xu developed new rhythmic flutes and adjusted the pitch, though Ruan Xian criticized the high tone as sorrowful. The text concludes with the history of the "Bayu Dance," which originated from the Banshun people and was adapted by Wang Can during the Wei Dynasty. In the Jin Dynasty, it was renamed "Xuanwu Dance" and later replaced by "Zhengde" and "Dayu" dances.

input_text: 史臣曰：昔者乘云效驾，卷领垂衣，则黄帝皁衣纁裳，放勋彤车白马，叶三微之序，舍寅丑之建，玄戈玉刃，作会相晖。 若乃参旗分景，帝车含曜，又所以营卫南宫，增华北极。 《月令》季夏之月， 命妇官染彩 ，赪丹班次，各有品章矣。 高旗有日月之象，式视有威仪之选，衣兼鞙珮，衡载鸣和，是以闲邪屏弃，不可入也。 若乃正名百物，补缉四维，疏怀山之水，静倾天之害，功尤彰者饰弥焕，德愈盛者服弥尊，莫不质良，用成其美。 《书》曰： 明试以功，车服以庸。 《礼记》曰： 鸾车，有虞氏之路也。 钩车，夏后氏之路也。 大路，殷路也。 乘路，周路也。
target_text: A detailed historical account of chariots, clothing, and ceremonial regalia from ancient times through the Jin Dynasty, emphasizing their symbolic and functional roles in governance, ritual, and social hierarchy. Since antiquity, gods and ancestors used specific vehicles and attire, such as the Yellow Emperor’s black top and light red lower clothes, and Fang Xun’s vermilion chariot with white horses, aligning with calendrical systems. The "Moon Order" describes women dyeing satin in regulated shades, while flags bearing sun and moon images and jade-adorned garments were meant to inspire awe and suppress evil. The text cites classical texts like "Shangshu" and "Book of Rites" to justify rewarding merit with chariots and clothing, and notes that saints derived designs from nature, such as birds and plants, for garments and wheels.

input_text: 若乃豪杰不经，庶人干典，彯鹬冠于郑伯之门，蹑珠履于春申之第。 及秦皇并国，揽其余轨，丰貂东至，獬豸南来，又有玄旗皁旒之制，旄头罕车之饰，写九王之廷于咸阳北坂，车舆之彩，各树其文，所谓秦人大备，而陈战国之后车者也。 及凝脂布网，经书咸烬，削灭三代，以金根为帝轸，除弃六冕，以袀玄为祭服。 高祖入关，既因秦制。 世宗挺英雄之略，总文景之资，扬霓拂翳，皮轩记鼓，横汾河而祠后土，登甘泉而祭昊天，奉常献仪，谓之大驾，车千乘而骑万匹。 至于成帝，以幸姬赵飞燕置属车间豹尾中，又杨雄所谓彏天狼之威弧，张曜日之灵旄，骈罗列布，雾集云合者也。 于后王氏擅朝，武车常轫，赤眉之乱，文物无遗。 建武十三年，吴汉平蜀，始送葆车舆辇，充庭之饰，渐以周备。 明帝采《周官》、《礼记》，更服衮章，天子冠通天而佩玉玺。 魏明以黼黻之美，有疑于僭，于是随章傧略，而捐者半焉。 高堂隆奏曰： 改正朔、殊徽号者，帝王所以神明其政，变民耳目也。 帝从其议，改青龙五年为景初元年，服色尚黄，从地正也。 世祖武皇帝接天人之贶，开典午之基，受终之礼，皆如唐虞故事。 晋氏金行，而服色尚赤，岂有司失其传欤！
target_text: The narrative traces the evolution of these systems through dynasties. During the Zhou and Yin periods, creative designs emerged, but later, as ritual order declined, princes violated norms, leading to confusion like purple garments in Qi and long tassels in Zou. Confucius advocated for clothing matching status. The Qin Dynasty unified practices, collecting furs and decorating chariots, but burned texts and simplified regalia. Emperor Gaozu followed Qin systems, while Emperor Shizong expanded ceremonies with grand processions. However, later rulers like Emperor Sheng favored concubines, and the Wang family’s dominance led to war and destruction of artifacts. After the Chimei Rebellion, Emperor Ming restored costumes based on "Zhou Guan" and "Book of Rites," and Emperor Wei Ming reduced lavish furs. Gao Tanglong advised changing Zhengshuo to align with gods, leading to yellow as the dominant color in the Jingchu era.

input_text: 史臣曰：昔者乘云效驾，卷领垂衣，则黄帝皁衣纁裳，放勋彤车白马，叶三微之序，舍寅丑之建，玄戈玉刃，作会相晖。 若乃参旗分景，帝车含曜，又所以营卫南宫，增华北极。 《月令》季夏之月， 命妇官染彩 ，赪丹班次，各有品章矣。 高旗有日月之象，式视有威仪之选，衣兼鞙珮，衡载鸣和，是以闲邪屏弃，不可入也。 若乃正名百物，补缉四维，疏怀山之水，静倾天之害，功尤彰者饰弥焕，德愈盛者服弥尊，莫不质良，用成其美。 《书》曰： 明试以功，车服以庸。 《礼记》曰： 鸾车，有虞氏之路也。 钩车，夏后氏之路也。 大路，殷路也。 乘路，周路也。
target_text: The text details specific chariot types, such as the "five chariots" (jade, gold, elephant, leather, wood), each with distinct decorations and uses. The jade chariot, most noble, featured a Taichang flag with twelve strands for sky worship. The golden chariot had nine strands for guests, the elephant chariot was plain red for court, the leather chariot was for military campaigns, and the wood chariot for hunting. Chariots were drawn by horses with elaborate trappings, including gold ornaments, bells, and jade fittings. The emperor’s ceremonial procession included various vehicles like the Sinan chariot (a compass guide), drum cart (measuring distance), and sheep cart, each with specific functions. The text also describes the Five Oxen Flag, plowing cart, and hunting cart, noting changes in color and flags under different rulers, such as Wei Jingchu’s shift to yellow and white.

input_text: 若乃豪杰不经，庶人干典，彯鹬冠于郑伯之门，蹑珠履于春申之第。 及秦皇并国，揽其余轨，丰貂东至，獬豸南来，又有玄旗皁旒之制，旄头罕车之饰，写九王之廷于咸阳北坂，车舆之彩，各树其文，所谓秦人大备，而陈战国之后车者也。 及凝脂布网，经书咸烬，削灭三代，以金根为帝轸，除弃六冕，以袀玄为祭服。 高祖入关，既因秦制。 世宗挺英雄之略，总文景之资，扬霓拂翳，皮轩记鼓，横汾河而祠后土，登甘泉而祭昊天，奉常献仪，谓之大驾，车千乘而骑万匹。 至于成帝，以幸姬赵飞燕置属车间豹尾中，又杨雄所谓彏天狼之威弧，张曜日之灵旄，骈罗列布，雾集云合者也。 于后王氏擅朝，武车常轫，赤眉之乱，文物无遗。 建武十三年，吴汉平蜀，始送葆车舆辇，充庭之饰，渐以周备。 明帝采《周官》、《礼记》，更服衮章，天子冠通天而佩玉玺。 魏明以黼黻之美，有疑于僭，于是随章傧略，而捐者半焉。 高堂隆奏曰： 改正朔、殊徽号者，帝王所以神明其政，变民耳目也。 帝从其议，改青龙五年为景初元年，服色尚黄，从地正也。 世祖武皇帝接天人之贶，开典午之基，受终之礼，皆如唐虞故事。 晋氏金行，而服色尚赤，岂有司失其传欤！
target_text: The account continues with the emperor’s travel sequence, listing dozens of vehicles and officials in a strict order, from the elephant chariot and drummers to the golden root chariot and imperial guards. This procession included multiple ranks of officials, cavalry, and ceremonial items like flags, halberds, and drums. The text notes that after the Liao Dynasty, many old regulations were lost, and by the Yuantong era, only a few chariots remained, with temporary decorations for sacrifices. The compass and other chariots were rediscovered later, such as Liu Yu finding the Sinan chariot in the 13th year of Yixi. The crown prince’s chariot and the empress dowager’s golden root chariot are also described, with specific rules for women’s vehicles, such as the queen’s mica chariot for silkworm worship.

input_text: 魏武以天下凶荒，资财乏匮，拟古皮弁，裁缣帛以为，合乎简易随时之义，以色别其贵贱，本施军饰，非为国容也。 徐爰曰： 俗说本未有岐，荀文若巾之行，触树枝成岐，谓之为善，因而弗改。 今通以为庆吊服。 巾，以葛为之，形如而横著之，古尊卑共服也。 故汉末妖贼以黄为巾，世谓黄巾贼。 帽名犹冠也，义取于蒙覆其首，其本纚也。 古者冠无帻，冠下有纚，以缯为之。 后世施帻于冠，因或裁缨为帽。 自乘舆宴居，下至庶人无爵者皆服之。 成帝咸和九年，制听尚书八座丞郎、门下三省侍官乘车，白低帏，出入掖门。 又，二宫直官著乌纱。 然则往往士人宴居皆著矣。 而江左时野人已著帽，人士亦往往而然，但其顶圆耳，后乃高其屋云。 汉制，自天子至于百官，无不佩剑，其后惟朝带剑。 晋世始代之以木，贵者犹用玉首，贱者亦用蚌、金银、玳瑁为雕饰。
target_text: The second half focuses on clothing and headwear. The emperor’s ceremonial attire included a black frame crown with white jade beads, twelve tassels, and a robe with twelve chapters (e.g., sun, moon, dragons). Different occasions required specific garments, such as a soap-colored robe for ancestral sacrifices or a crimson robe for court. Crowns varied by rank: the Tongtian Crown for the emperor, Pingmian for princes, and Jinxian Crown for scholars, with beams indicating status (e.g., three beams for princes, one beam for low officials). Other crowns like the Wu Guan (martial), Alpine Crown (for envoys), and Dharma Crown (for law officials) had distinct shapes and origins, often linked to historical figures or legends. The text also describes caps, scarves, and hats, noting that the clam (a type of headgear) evolved from ancient practices and was used by all classes.

input_text: 自非公会则不得乘轺车，止乘漆布辎軿，铜五采而已。 王妃、特进夫人、封郡君，安车，驾三，皁交路。 封县乡君油軿车，驾两马，右騑。 自过江之后，旧章多缺。 元帝践极，始造大路、戎路各一，皆即古金根之制也，无复充庭之仪。 至于郊祀大事，则权饰余车以周用。 六师亲征则用戎路，去其盖而乘之，属车但五乘而已。 加绿油幢，硃丝路，饰青交路，黄金涂五采，其轮毂犹素，两箱无金锦之饰。 其一车又是轺车，旧仪，天子所乘驾六，是时无复六马之乘，五路皆驾四而已，同用黑，是为玄牡。 无复五时车，有事则权以马车代之，建旗其上。 其后但以五色木牛象五时车，竖旗于牛背，行则使人舆之。 牛之义，盖取其负重致远安而稳也。 旗常缠而不舒旆，所谓德车结旌者也。
target_text: The text concludes with accessories and women’s attire. Swords were once universal but later limited to court, with wooden swords replacing metal. The emperor’s six seals, including the legendary Imperial Seal, were passed down, though the sword of the white snake was lost. Belts, pouches, and wats (tablets) were used for official duties, with specific colors and materials for ranks. Women’s clothing, such as the queen’s soap-colored top for temple visits or cyan for weddings, included elaborate headdresses with golden flowers, jade ornaments, and step decorations. Noble ladies and concubines had graded seals, ribbons, and jade, with specific attire for silkworm ceremonies. The text emphasizes that these systems were meant to reflect virtue and status, but many were lost or simplified over time, especially after the Eastern Jin Dynasty.

input_text: 昔者元胎无象，太素流形，对越在天，以为元首，则《记》所谓冬居营窟，夏居橧巢，饮血茹毛，未有麻丝者也。 及燧人钻火，庖牺出震，风宗下武，炎胤昌基，画野无闻，其归一揆。 黄帝则东海南江，登空蹑岱，至于昆峰振辔，崆山防道，存诸汗竹，不可厚诬。 高阳任地依神，帝喾顺天行义。 东逾蟠木，西济流沙，北至幽陵，南抚交址，日月所经，舟车所至，莫匪王臣，不逾兹域。 帝尧时，禹平水土，以为九州。
target_text: It then traces the development of civilization through legendary figures: Suirenshi who drilled wood for fire, Paoxishi who created the eight trigrams, Nüwa who repaired the heavens, and Shennong who developed agriculture and divided territories. The Yellow Emperor traveled extensively, reaching the eastern seaside, the Yangtze River in the south, and Mount Daiyue. Zhuanxu ensured everyone's needs were met, while the Gaoxin family followed heavenly ways. Emperor Yao's reign saw Dayu control floods and divide the land into nine provinces. Yu Shun formulated calendars, divided star districts, and established provinces including Bingzhou, Youzhou, and Yingzhou.

input_text: 虞舜登庸，厥功弥劭，表提类而分区宇，判山河而考疆域，冀北创并部之名，燕齐起幽营之号，则《书》所谓肇十有二州，封十有二山者也。 夏功在于唐尧，殷因无所损益。 周武克商，自丰徂镐。 至成王时，改作《禹贡》，徐梁入于青雍，冀野析于幽并。 职方掌天下之土，以周厥利；保章辩九州之野，皆有分星。 东南曰扬州，正南曰荆州，河南曰豫州，正东曰青州，河东曰兗州，正西曰雍州，东北曰幽州，河内曰冀州，正北曰并州。 始皇初并天下，惩战国，削罢列侯，分天下为三十六郡。
target_text: The text details the evolution of administrative divisions through successive dynasties. During the Xia and Shang dynasties, territorial systems were established and maintained. King Wu of Zhou moved the capital from Feng to Haojing. Under King Cheng of Zhou, the "Yu Gong" was revised, merging some provinces and dividing others. Officials were appointed to manage lands and observe astronomy, distinguishing the nine provinces with their corresponding star regions. The southeast was Yangzhou, due south was Jingzhou, Henan was Yuzhou, due east was Qingzhou, east of Hedong was Yanzhou, due west was Yongzhou, northeast was Youzhou, north of the Yellow River was Jizhou, and due north was Bingzhou.

input_text: 三川、河东、南阳、南郡、九江、鄣郡、会稽、颍川、砀郡、泗水、薛郡、东郡、琅邪、齐郡、上谷、渔阳、右北平、辽西、辽东、代郡、钜鹿、邯郸、上党、太原、云中、九原、雁门、上郡、陇西、北地、汉中、巴郡、蜀郡、黔中、长沙、凡三十五郡，与内史为三十六郡也。 于是兴师逾江，平取百越，又置闽中、南海、桂林、象郡，凡四十郡，郡一守焉。 其他则西临洮而北沙漠，东萦西带，皆临大海。 汉祖龙兴，革秦之弊，分内史为三部，更置郡国二十有三，桂阳、江夏、豫章、河内、魏郡、东海、楚国、平原、梁国、定襄、泰山、汝南、淮阳、千乘、东莱、燕国、清河、信都、常山、中山、渤海、广汉、涿郡，合二十三也。 三内史者，河上、渭南、中地也。 《地理志》曰：高祖增二十六，武帝改河上、渭南、中地以为京兆、冯翊、扶风是为三辅也。 文增厥九，广平、城阳、淄川、济南、胶西、胶东、河间、庐江、衡山、武帝改衡山曰六安。 景加其四。 济北、济阴、山阳、北海也。 宣改济北曰东平。 武帝开越攘胡，初置十七，南海、苍梧、郁林、合浦、交耻、九真、日南、珠崖、儋耳九郡，平西南夷置牂柯、越嵩、沈黎、汶山、犍为、益州六郡，西置武都郡，又分立零陵郡，合十七郡。 拓土分疆，又增十四。 弘农、临淮、西河、朔方、酒泉、陈留、安定、天水、玄菟、乐浪、广陵、敦煌、武威、张掖。 昭帝少事，又增其一。 金城也。 至平帝元始二年，凡新置郡国七十有一，与秦四十，合一百一十有一。
target_text: When Qin Shihuang unified the world, he abolished the feudal princes and divided the empire into thirty-six counties, including Sanchuan, Hedong, Nanyang, Nanjun, Jiujiang, and others. The Qin territory extended to Dianfeng in the west, the desert in the north, and the sea in the east. After the Qin dynasty fell, the Han dynasty established new administrative systems. Emperor Gaozu of Han added twenty-three counties, while Emperor Wu established seventeen counties after conquering Vietnam and the Hu lands, and six more after pacifying the southwestern barbarians. By the second year of Emperor Ping's Yuanshi period, there were 111 counties total, divided into thirteen divisions including Liang, Yi, Jing, Yang, Qing, Yu, Yan, Xu, You, Bing, Ji, Jiaozhi, and Shuofang.

input_text: 省前汉八，分置五，改旧名七，因旧九十六，少前汉三也。 桓灵颇增于前，复置六郡。 桓，高阳、高凉、博陵；灵，南安、鄱阳、庐陵。 魏武定霸，三方鼎立，生宁版荡，关洛荒芜，所置者十二，新兴、乐平、西平、新平、略阳、阴平、带方、谯、乐陵、章武、南乡、襄阳。 所省者七，上郡、朔方、五原、云中、定襄、渔阳、庐江。 而文帝置七，朝歌、阳平、弋阳、魏兴、新城、义阳、安丰。 得汉郡者十有一焉。吴主大皇帝初置郡五，临贺、武昌、珠崖、新安、庐陵南部。 少帝、景帝各四，少，临川、临海、衡阳、湘东。 景，天门、建安、建平、合浦北部。 归命侯亦置十有二郡，始安、始兴、邵陵、安成、新昌、武平、九德、吴兴、东阳、桂林、荥阳、宜都。 得汉郡者十有八焉。 晋武帝太康元年，既平孙氏，凡增置郡国二十有三，荥阳、上洛、顿丘、临淮、东莞、襄城、汝阴、长广、广宁、昌黎、新野、随郡、阴平、义阳、毗陵、宣城、南康、晋安、宁浦、始平、咯阳、乐平、南平。 省司隶置司州，别立梁、秦、宁、平四州，仍吴之广州，凡十九州，司、冀、兗、豫、荆、徐、扬、青、幽、平、并、雍、凉、秦、梁、益、宁、交、广州。 郡国一百七十三，仍吴所置二十五，仍蜀新置十一，仍魏所置二十一，仍汉旧九十三，置二十三。 以为冠带之国，尽有殷周之土。 若乃敦庞于天地之始，昭晰于牺农之世，用长黎元，未争疆埸。 而玉环楛矢，夷裘风驾，南翚表贶，东风入律，光乎上德，奚远弗臻。
target_text: The text describes how later dynasties continued to modify territorial divisions. During the Later Han, Emperor Guangwu merged eight counties due to population decline. Subsequent emperors added or changed various counties. During the Three Kingdoms period, Wei, Shu, and Wu each established new counties. By the first year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, after pacifying the Wu state, twenty-three additional counties were established, bringing the total to 173 counties across nineteen provinces. The text notes that this represented a great civilized country owning all territories of Yin and Zhou.

input_text: 天有七星，地有七表；天有四维，地有四渎。 八纮之外，名为八极。 地不足东南，天不足西北。 八极之广，东西二亿三万一千三百里，南北二亿三万一千三百里。 自地至天，半八极之数，自下亦如之。 昔黄帝令竖亥步自东极，至于西极，五亿十万九千八百八步。 史臣案，凡周天积百七万九百一十三里，径三十五万六千九百七十里。 所谓南北为经，东西为纬。 天有十二次，日月之所躔；地有十二辰，王侯之所国也。 或因生得姓，因功命土，祁、酉、燕、齐，在乎兹域。 昔黄帝旁行天下，方制万里，得百里之国万区，则《周易》所谓 首出庶物，万国咸宁 者也。 昔在帝尧，叶和万邦，制八家为邻，三邻为朋，三朋为里，五里为邑，十邑为都，十都为师，州十有二师焉。
target_text: The document provides extensive detail on the geographical measurements and cosmological understanding of the ancient world. It describes the eight poles (Baji) as being 203,1300 miles from east to west and the same from north to south. The distance from earth to heaven was half the width of the eight poles. The text explains that there are seven stars in the Big Dipper and seven layers of earth, with four corners in the sky and four great rivers flowing eastward into the sea. The terrain becomes lower in the southeast while the sky tilts toward the northwest.

input_text: 一同百里，提封万井，除山川、坑岸、城池、邑居、园囿、街路三千六百井，定出赋六千四百井，戎马四百匹，兵车百乘，此卿大夫采地之大者也，是谓百乘之家。 一封三百六十六里，提封十万井，定出赋六万四千井，戎马四千匹，兵车千乘，此谓诸侯之大者也，谓之千乘之国。 天子畿内方千里，提封百万井，定出赋六十四万井，戎马四万匹，兵车万乘，戎卒七十二万人，故天子称万乘之主焉。 秦始皇既得志于天下，访周之败，以为处士横议，诸侯寻戈，四夷交侵，以弱见夺，于是削去五等焉。 汉兴，创艾亡秦孤立而败，于是割裂封疆，立爵二等，功臣侯者百有余邑。 于时民罹秦项，户口凋弊，大侯不过万家，小者五六百户，而尊王子弟，大启九国。 古者有分土而无分民，若乃大者跨州连郡，小则十有余城，以户口为差降，略封疆之远近，所谓分民自汉始也。
target_text: The text extensively describes the feudal system established by various dynasties. Under the Xia dynasty, the territory was divided into five service zones (five fu) extending 5000 miles in radius. The system included Dianfu (imperial domain), Houfu (marquis domain), Suifu (submission domain), Yaofu (essential domain), and Huangfu (wilderness domain), each with specific tax and service requirements. The Zhou dynasty established five ranks of nobility—Duke, Marquis, Earl, Viscount, and Baron—with specific land allocations. The emperor's field was 1000 li in circumference, while dukes received 100 li, earls 70 li, and viscounts 50 li. The text notes that during the Zhou dynasty's peak, there were 13,714,933 people and no crimes were committed.

input_text: 五伯迭兴，总其盟会。 陵夷至于战国，遂有七王，韩、魏、赵、燕、齐、秦、楚。 又有宋、卫、中山，不断如线，如三晋篡夺，亦称孤也。 《司马法》广陈三代，曰：古者六尺为步，步百为亩，亩百为夫，夫三为屋，屋三为井。 井方一里，是为九夫，八家共之。 一夫一妇受私田百亩，公田十亩，是为八百八十亩，余二十亩为庐舍，出入相友，守望相助，疾病相救。 民受田，上田夫百亩，中田夫二百亩，下田夫三百亩，岁受耕之，爰自其处。 其家众男为余夫，亦以口受田如此。 士工商家受田，五口乃当农夫一口。 有赋有税，税谓公田什一及工商衡虞之入也，赋供车马甲兵士从之役。 民年二十受田，六十归田。
target_text: The document traces the decline of the Zhou royal family and the rise of the Spring and Autumn period, when 36 monarchs were killed and 52 countries perished over 242 years. It lists 139 known countries including Lu, Zhu, Zheng, Song, Ji, Wei, and others, plus 31 countries that disappeared. The five hegemons emerged, followed by the seven warring states of Han, Wei, Zhao, Yan, Qi, Qin, and Chu. The text describes the well-field system in detail, where land was divided into nine squares of 100 mu each, with eight families jointly cultivating the central public field.

input_text: 自文景与民休息，至平帝元始二年，民户千二百二十三万三千六十二，口五千九百五十九万四千九百七十八，其地东西九千三百二里，南北万三千三百六十八里。 大率十里一亭，亭有长。 十亭一乡，乡有三老，有秩啬夫、游徼各一人。 县大率方百里，民稠则减，稀则旷，乡、亭亦如之。 皆秦制也。 光武中兴，不逾前制，东海王疆以去就有礼，故优以大封，兼食鲁郡二十九县，其余称为宠锡者，兼一郡而已。 至桓帝永寿三年，户千六十七万七千九百六十，口五千六百四十八万六千八百五十六，斯亦户口之滋殖者也。 献帝建安元年拜曹操为镇东将军，封费亭侯。 魏文帝黄初三年，初制封王之庶子为乡公，嗣王之庶子为亭侯，公侯之庶子为亭伯。 刘备章武元年，亦以郡国封建诸王，或遥采嘉名，不由检土地所出。 其户二十万九十万。 孙叔赤乌五年，亦取中州嘉号封建诸王。
target_text: The text concludes by describing the administrative systems of the Qin and Han dynasties. After Qin Shihuang abolished the five-rank nobility system, the Han dynasty established second-class titles, granting fiefs to meritorious officials. By Emperor Ping's reign, there were 12,233,062 households and 59,594,978 people, with territory extending 9,302 miles east to west and 13,368 miles north to south. The document details the system of pavilions every ten miles, townships every ten pavilions, and the roles of village elders and other officials. It notes that by the third year of a later reign, there were 10,677,960 households with 56,486,856 people, representing an era of increasing population.

input_text: 《易》曰： 有天地然后有万物，有万物然后有男女，有男女然后有夫妇。 夫妇之义尚矣哉！周礼，王者立后六宫，三夫人、九嫔、二十七世妇、八十一御妻，以听天下之内治。 故《昏义》云： 天子之与后，犹日之与月，阴之与阳，相须而成者也。 汉初因秦称号，帝母称皇太后，后称皇后，而加以美人、良人、八子、七子之属。 至孝武制婕妤之徒凡十四等。 降及魏、晋，母后之号，皆因汉法；自夫人以下，世有增损焉。 高祖拨乱反正，深鉴奢逸，恶衣菲食，务先节俭。 配德早终，长秋旷位，嫔嫱之数，无所改作。 太祖献皇后张氏，讳尚柔，范阳方城人也。 祖次惠，宋濮阳太守。
target_text: It describes the Zhou etiquette system, where the emperor maintained a hierarchy of concubines—three wives, nine concubines, twenty-seven wives, and eighty-one royal wives—to govern women's education. The "Huanyi" compares the emperor and empress to the sun and moon, complementing each other like yin and yang. During the early Yi Dynasty, Qin titles were adopted, with the emperor's mother called empress dowager and his wife called empress, while other women received titles like beauty, beloved, eighth son, and seventh son. By the time of the ridge stem, there were fourteen titles including Jieyu. From the Wei and Zhi dynasties onward, queen mother titles followed Mo Dynasty rules, while wife titles varied by generation.

input_text: 后母萧氏，即文帝从姑。 后，宋元嘉中嫔于文帝，生长沙宣武王懿、永阳昭王敷，次生高祖。 初，后尝于室内，忽见庭前昌蒲生花，光彩照灼，非世中所有。 后惊视，谓侍者曰： 汝见不？ 对曰： 不见。 后曰： 尝闻见者当富贵。 因遽取吞之。 是月产高祖。 将产之夜，后见庭内若有衣冠陪列焉。 次生衡阳宣王畅、义兴昭长公主令。 宋泰始七年，殂于秣陵县同夏里舍，葬武进县东城里山。 天监元年五月甲辰，追上尊号为皇后。谥曰献。 父穆之，字思静，晋司空华六世孙。 曾祖舆坐华诛，徙兴古，未至召还。 及过江，为丞相掾，太子舍人。 穆之少方雅，有识鉴。 宋元嘉中，为员外散骑侍郎。
target_text: Emperor Gaozu, learning from past extravagance that led to ruin, practiced frugality, ate simple food, and wore plain clothes. His first wife died early, leaving the queen position vacant, and concubine numbers remained stable. Taizong and Shidan, heirs from outside the country, had concubines who died before them, so no new boudoirs were built. The text then details the lineage of a queen, whose grandfather was a salt magistrate. Her mother, Mrs. Xiao, was Saitong's cousin. The queen became Saitong's concubine during Sai Chengtai's reign, bearing King Lu Deng of Xuanwu in Changsha, Lu Ti of King Zhao of Yongyang, and Zhidan. Early in her household, she saw Changpu flowers glowing in the hall, swallowed them, and conceived Gaozu. Before giving birth, she saw many people in the hall. She later gave birth to Xiao Chang, King Xuan of Hengyang, and a daughter. She died in the seventh year of Taishi in the Song Dynasty and was buried in Dongcheng Mountain. In the first year of Tianjian, she was posthumously honored as queen with the title Mi.

input_text: 与吏部尚书江湛、太子左率袁淑善，淑荐之于始兴王浚，浚深引纳焉。 穆之鉴其祸萌，思违其难，言于湛求外出。 湛将用为东县，固乞远郡，久之，得为宁远将军、交址太守。 治有异绩。 会刺史死，交土大乱，穆之威怀循拊，境内以宁。 宋文帝闻之嘉焉，将以为交州刺史，会病卒。 子弘籍，字真艺，齐初为镇西参军，卒于官。 高祖践阼，追赠穆之光禄大夫，加金章。 又诏曰： 亡舅齐镇西参军，素风雅猷，夙肩名辈，降年不永，早世潜辉。 朕少离苦辛，情地弥切，虽宅相克成，辂车靡赠，兴言永往，触目恸心。 可追赠廷尉卿。 弘籍无子，从父弟弘策以第三子缵为嗣，别有传。 高祖德皇后郗氏，讳徽，高平金乡人也。 祖绍，国子祭酒，领东海王师。 父烨，太子舍人，早卒。
target_text: Her father, Mu Zhi, was a sixth-generation grandson of Zhang Hua, a Jin Dynasty Sikong. After Zhang Hua's punishment, Mu Zhi's great-grandfather was transferred but recalled. Mu Zhi served as a member of the Communist Party of China during the Song, Yuan, and Jia years, befriending Jiang Zhan and Yuan Shu. Foreseeing disaster, he sought an outside post, becoming General Ningyuan and Governor of Jiaosha, where he governed well. After the governor's death, he calmed the territory. Emperor Severn praised him but he died before being appointed governor of Manye. His son Hongji died in office. Gaozu posthumously gave Mu Zhi the title of Guanglu Doctor and a gold medal, later adding Ting Wei Qing. Hongzhan had no sons, so his nephew Hongce's son Zhang Lan became his heir.

input_text: 初，后母寻阳公主方娠，梦当生贵子。 及生后，有赤光照于室内，器物尽明，家人皆怪之。 巫言此女光采异常，将有所妨，乃于水滨祓除之。 后幼而明慧，善隶书，读史传。 女工之事，无不闲习。 宋后废帝将纳为后；齐初，安陆王缅又欲婚：郗氏并辞以女疾，乃止。 建元未，高祖始娉焉。 生永兴公主玉姚，永世公主玉婉，永康公主玉嬛。 建武五年，高祖为雍州刺史，先之镇，后乃迎后。 至州未几，永元元年八月殂于襄阳官舍，时年三十二。 其年归葬南徐州南东海武进县东城里山。 中兴二年，齐朝进高祖位相国，封十郡，梁公，诏赠后为梁公妃。 高祖践阼，追崇为皇后。
target_text: Empress Xiao Yan, Emperor Wu of Liang, was from Jinxiang, Gaoping. Her grandfather Xi Shao was a teacher to King Shu Hai, and her father Xi Ye was a crown prince who died early. Her mother, Princess Xunyang, dreamed of having a son before her birth. At birth, a red light shone, alarming the family. A wizard performed an exorcism. The queen was intelligent, skilled in calligraphy, and loved history. She refused marriage proposals from the Song deposed emperor and Anlu King Xiao Mian. At the end of Jianyuan, Gaozu became engaged to her. They had three daughters. In the first year of Chengtai, she served as governor of Zong Maggot, then died in Xiangyang in the first year of Yongyuan at age thirty-two. She was buried in Dongchengshan. In the second year of Zhongxing, she was granted the title of Liang Gong Concubine, and later queen. Her posthumous title was Empress De, and her tomb was Xiuling. Her father Xi Ye was posthumously named Doctor Jin Ziguanglu.

input_text: 有司议谥，吏部尚书兼右仆射臣约议曰： 表号垂名，义昭不朽。 先皇后应祥月德，比载坤灵，柔范阴化，仪形自远。 伣天作合，义先造舟，而神猷夙掩，所隔升运。宜式遵景行，用昭大典。 谨按《谥法》，忠和纯备曰德，贵而好礼曰德。 宜崇曰德皇后。 诏从之。 陵曰修陵。 后父烨，诏赠金紫光禄大夫。 烨尚宋文帝女寻阳公主，齐初降封松滋县君。 烨子泛，中军临川王记室参军。 太宗简皇后王氏，讳灵宾，琅邪临沂人也。 祖俭，太尉、南昌文宪公。 后幼而柔明淑德，叔父暕见之曰： 吾家女师也。 天监十一年，拜晋安王妃。 生哀太子大器，南郡王大连，长山公主妙纮。 中大通三年十月，拜皇太子妃。
target_text: Taizong's Queen Jian, named Wang, was from Linyi, Langxie. Her grandfather Wang Jian was a Taiwei and Duke Wenxian. She was gentle and wise, becoming Princess Jin'an in the eleventh year of Tianjian. She bore Prince Ai, Prince Zuolian of Nanjun, and Princess Chengshan. She became crown princess in the third year of Zhongdatong and died in the third year of Li Zha at age forty-five. Taizong posthumously titled her empress with Mi Jian, and she was buried in Zhuangling. An imperial decree mandated frugality for her funeral, citing historical precedents. Her father Wang Qian, originally named Si Ji, changed his name to avoid conflict with Emperor Qi Gao. He served as a foreign minister, Prince Xima, and prefect of Yixing, later becoming a hussar councilor and Huangmenlang. He was calm and did not seek advancement. At the end of Yongyuan, he refused promotion to Shizhong. Under Gaozu, he served as Grand Sima consultant and later Shizhong. After the abdication, he was granted the title of Marquis of Nanchang County. He died in the third year of his life at age forty-nine, posthumously granted Shizhong and Jin Ziguanglu Doctor.

input_text: 在郡卧疾不视事。 征还，复为度支尚书，加给事中，领射声校尉。 以母忧去职。 普通三年十月卒，时年四十九。 诏赠侍中、金紫光禄大夫，谥曰安。 子规袭爵，别有传。 高祖丁贵嫔，讳令光，谯国人也，世居襄阳。 贵嫔生于樊城，有神光之异，紫烟满室，故以 光 为名。 相者云： 此女当大贵。 高祖临州，丁氏因人以闻。 贵嫔时年十四，高祖纳焉。 初，贵嫔生而有赤痣在左臂，治之不灭，至是无何忽失所在。 事德皇后小心祗敬，尝于供养经案之侧，仿佛若见神人，心独异之。 高祖义师起，昭明太子始诞育，贵嫔与太子留在州城。 京邑平，乃还京都。
target_text: Emperor Gaozu's concubine Ding, named Lingguang, was from Qiao State, living in Xiangyang. Born in Fancheng with a divine light and purple smoke, she was named "Light." A fortune teller predicted her wealth. At fourteen, Gaozu married her. She had a red mole on her left arm that disappeared when she was sent away. She served Empress De carefully and once saw divine figures. During Gaozu's rebellion, Crown Prince Zhaoming was born. In the first year of Tianjian, she was made a noble concubine, living in Xianyang Hall. A minister argued that her status should be respected due to her son, citing historical precedents. She was kind, frugal, and avoided luxury. She promoted Buddhism, refused meat, and ate only vegetables. On her ordination day, sweet dew fell. She was proficient in the Pure Name Sutra. She died in the seventh year of her life at age forty-two. A condolence poem praised her virtues. She was posthumously titled Mu. After Taizong ascended, she was honored as Empress Dowager Mu. Her father was a governor.

input_text: 齐始安王遥光纳焉。 遥光败，入东昏宫。 建康城平，高祖纳为彩女。 天监七年八月，生世祖。 寻拜为修容，常随世祖出蕃。 大同六年六月，薨于江州内寝，时年六十七。 其年十一月，归葬江宁县通望山。 谥曰宣。 世祖即位，有司奏追崇为文宣太后。 承圣二年，追赠太后父齐故奉朝请灵宝散骑常侍、左卫将军，封武康县侯，邑五百户；母陈氏，武康侯夫人。 世祖徐妃，讳昭佩，东海郯人也。 祖孝嗣，太尉、枝江文忠公。 父绲，侍中、信武将军。 天监十六年十二月，拜湘东王妃。 生世子方等、益昌公主含贞。 太清三年五月，被谴死，葬江陵瓦官寺。 史臣曰：后妃道赞皇风，化行天下，盖取《葛覃》、《关雎》之义焉。
target_text: Emperor Gaozu's doctor, Zhao Yao, originally surnamed Hu, was from Hejikung Yao. King Zha Shi'an took her as a concubine. After Dong Guang's defeat, she was brought into the palace by Donghun Hou. After Jianchenyuan was pacified, Zhidan accepted her as a palace maid. In the seventh year of Yue, she gave birth to Shidan and was granted the title of Xiurong. She died in the sixth year of Zuo Hui at age sixty-seven and was buried in Tongwang Mountain. After Shidan became emperor, she was honored as Empress Dowager Wenxuan. Her father was posthumously granted titles, and her mother was made a marquis's wife.

input_text: 齐始安王遥光纳焉。 遥光败，入东昏宫。 建康城平，高祖纳为彩女。 天监七年八月，生世祖。 寻拜为修容，常随世祖出蕃。 大同六年六月，薨于江州内寝，时年六十七。 其年十一月，归葬江宁县通望山。 谥曰宣。 世祖即位，有司奏追崇为文宣太后。 承圣二年，追赠太后父齐故奉朝请灵宝散骑常侍、左卫将军，封武康县侯，邑五百户；母陈氏，武康侯夫人。 世祖徐妃，讳昭佩，东海郯人也。 祖孝嗣，太尉、枝江文忠公。 父绲，侍中、信武将军。 天监十六年十二月，拜湘东王妃。 生世子方等、益昌公主含贞。 太清三年五月，被谴死，葬江陵瓦官寺。 史臣曰：后妃道赞皇风，化行天下，盖取《葛覃》、《关雎》之义焉。
target_text: Shizu's concubine Xu, named Zhaopei, was from Tan in the East China Sea. Her grandfather was a Taiwei and Duke Wenzhong, and her father was a general. In the 16th year of Tianjian, she was named Princess Xiangshu. She bore Fang Deng and Princess Hanzhen. In the third year of Taiqing, she was ordered to commit suicide and buried in Waguan Temple. The text concludes that the empress supported royal customs, while Mu Guifei's glory was displayed through her son, but the ancestor's concubine Xu lacked virtue and brought about her own destruction.

input_text: 裴子野，字几原，河东闻喜人，晋太子左率康八世孙。 兄黎，弟楷、绰，并有盛名，所谓 四裴 也。 曾祖松之，宋太中大夫。 祖骃，南中郎外兵参军。 父昭明，通直散骑常侍。 子野生而偏孤，为祖母所养，年九岁，祖母亡，泣血哀恸，家人异之。 少好学，善属文。 起家齐武陵王国左常侍，右军江夏王参军，遭父忧去职。 居丧尽礼，每之墓所，哭泣处草为之枯，有白兔驯扰其侧。 天监初，尚书仆射范云嘉其行，将表奏之，会云卒，不果。 乐安任昉有盛名，为后进所慕，游其门者，昉必相荐达。 子野于昉为从中表，独不至，昉亦恨焉。 久之，除右军安成王参军，俄迁兼廷尉正。
target_text: Pei Ziye, courtesy name Jiyuan, was from Wenxi, Hedong, and a descendant of Jin Dynasty royalty. He was raised by his grandmother after his mother died at his birth, and showed deep filial piety when she passed when he was nine. Known for his studiousness and literary skill, he began his official career as Zuo Changshi of the Wuling Kingdom of Qi. His mourning period for his father was so exemplary that withered grass and a white rabbit appeared at his father's tomb. Fan Yun praised his conduct but died before reporting it to the emperor. Ren Fang, a famous scholar, resented Ziye for not visiting him, despite being a cousin. Ziye later served as a military advisor but was dismissed when a document was signed in his absence without his knowledge. He refused to litigate to clear his name, accepting the dismissal without resentment.

input_text: 时三官通署狱牒，子野尝不在，同僚辄署其名，奏有不允，子野从坐免职。 或劝言诸有司，可得无咎。 子野笑而答曰： 虽惭柳季之道，岂因讼以受服。 自此免黜久之，终无恨意。 二年，吴平侯萧景为南兗州刺史，引为冠军录事，府迁职解。 时中书范缜与子野未遇，闻其行业而善焉。 会迁国子博士，乃上表让之曰： 伏见前冠军府录事参军河东裴子野，年四十，字几原，幼禀至人之行，长厉国士之风。居丧有礼，毁瘠几灭，免忧之外，蔬水不进。 栖迟下位，身贱名微，而性不憛憛，情无汲汲，是以有识嗟推，州闾叹服。 且家传素业，世习儒史，苑囿经籍，游息文艺。 著《宋略》二十卷，弥纶首尾，勒成一代，属辞比事，有足观者。 且章句洽悉，训故可传。脱置之胶庠，以弘奖后进，庶一夔之辩可寻，三豕之疑无谬矣。
target_text: Fan Zhen later recommended Ziye, praising his moral integrity, filial piety, and scholarly achievements, including his twenty-volume "Song Lue." Despite some officials objecting to his qualifications, Ziye was appointed as Minister Bibu Lang and later as a county magistrate, where he resolved disputes through reasoning, eliminating lawsuits. He completed his great-grandfather's unfinished history, earning praise from Shen Yue and others. He was then appointed as a historian and editor, known for his broad knowledge, such as identifying the origins of envoys from the Baiti and Hua kingdoms. He compiled the "Picture of Envoys from Fang Kingdom" and was admired by contemporaries like Liu Xian and Liu Zhilin. In the seventh year of the ordinary year, he drafted an edict against Wei quickly, impressing Emperor Gaozu with his heroic writing. Ziye's style imitated the ancients, and he wrote quickly, saying he wrote with his heart. He served in the palace for over a decade, living frugally, giving his salary to poor relatives, and supporting his family on borrowed land. He was a devout Buddhist vegetarian in his later years. He died at sixty-two, and the emperor mourned him, granting posthumous honors and a burial. His works include "Collection of Mourning Clothes," "Continued Biography of the Pei Family," and others.

input_text: 太尉临川王闻其名，召掌书记，仍侍西豊侯正德读。 正德为巴西、梓潼郡，协除所部安都令。未至县，遭母忧。 服阕，出补西阳郡丞。 还除北中郎行参军，复兼廷尉正。 久之，出为庐陵郡丞，未拜。会西豊侯正德为吴郡，除中军参军，领郡五官，迁轻车湘东王参军事，兼记室。 普通六年，正德受诏北讨，引为府录事参军，掌书记。 军还，会有诏举士，湘东王表荐协曰： 臣闻贡玉之士，归之润山；论珠之人，出于枯岸。 是以刍荛之言，择于廊庙者也。 臣府兼记室参军吴郡顾协，行称乡闾，学兼文武，服膺道素，雅量邃远，安贫守静，奉公抗直，傍阙知己，志不自营，年方六十，室无妻子。 臣欲言于官人，申其屈滞，协必苦执贞退，立志难夺，可谓东南之遗宝矣。 伏惟陛下未明求衣，思贤如渴，爰发明诏，各举所知。 臣识非许、郭，虽无知人之鉴，若守固无言，惧贻蔽贤之咎。 昔孔愉表韩绩之才，庾亮荐翟汤之德，臣虽未齿二臣，协实无惭两士。 即召拜通直散骑侍郎，兼中书通事舍人。累迁步兵校尉，守鸿胪卿，员外散骑常侍，卿、舍人并如故。
target_text: Gu Xie, courtesy name Zhengli, from Wu County, lost his father young and was raised by his grandfather. As a child, he expressed a desire for seclusion, impressing his maternal grandfather. He was studious and praised for his concentration. He began his career as a historian in Yangzhou and later as a Taixue doctor. Minister Shen Yue praised his policy essay as unmatched since the Eastern Jin. He served in various roles, including as a magistrate and military advisor. At sixty, he was recommended for his conduct and knowledge, though he remained indifferent to fame. He was appointed as a minister and died at seventy-three. The emperor mourned him, noting his honesty and lack of close relatives. Gu Xie was known for his integrity, refusing gifts and living frugally. He married his uncle's daughter in his sixties, having no children. He was well-read and compiled works like "Yi Xing Yuan" and "Suo Yu."

input_text: 少时将娉舅息女，未成婚而协母亡，免丧后不复娶。 至六十余，此女犹未他适，协义而迎之。 晚虽判合，卒无胤嗣。 协博极群书，于文字及禽兽草木尤称精详。 撰《异姓苑》五卷，《琐语》十卷，并行于世。 徐摛，字士秀，东海郯人也。 祖凭道，宋海陵太守。 父超之，天监初仕至员外散骑常侍。 摛幼而好学，及长，遍览经史。 属文好为新变，不拘旧体。 起家太学博士，迁左卫司马。 会晋安王纲出戍石头，高祖谓周舍曰： 为我求一人，文学俱长兼有行者，欲令与晋安游处。 舍曰： 臣外弟徐摛，形质陋小，若不胜衣，而堪此选。 高祖曰： 必有仲宣之才，亦不简其容貌。 以摛为侍读。 后王出镇江州，仍补云麾府记室参军，又转平西府中记室。
target_text: Xu Zhai, courtesy name Shixiu, from Donghai, was studious and known for his innovative writing. He served as a Taixue doctor and was recommended by Zhou She to accompany Prince Jin'an, despite his plain appearance. He held various posts, including as a magistrate and military advisor. His writing style, known as "gong style," was imitated in the palace, initially angering Emperor Gaozu but later earning his favor. Zhu Yi, feeling threatened, had Xu Zhai appointed as prefect of Xin'an, where he governed fairly and improved customs. He later served as a general and advisor on marriage rituals, advising the emperor on proper etiquette. During Hou Jing's rebellion, Xu Zhai stood firm, impressing Hou Jing with his fierceness. He died at seventy-eight after refusing a general title. His eldest son, Xu Ling, was famous.

input_text: 僧辩既入，乃背泉而坐，曰： 鲍郎有罪，令旨使我锁卿，卿勿以故意见期。 因出令示泉，锁之床下。 泉曰： 稽缓王师，甘罪是分，但恐后人更思鲍泉之愦愦耳。 乃为启谢淹迟之罪。 世祖寻复其任，令与僧辩等率舟师东逼邵陵王于郢州。 郢州平，元帝以长子方诸为刺史，泉为长史，行府州事。 侯景密遣将宋子仙、任约率精骑袭之。方诸与泉不恤军政，唯蒲酒自乐，贼骑至，百姓奔告，方诸与泉方双陆，不信，曰： 徐文盛大军在东，贼何由得至？ 既而传告者众，始令阖门。贼纵火焚之，莫有抗者，贼骑遂入，城乃陷。 执方诸及泉送之景所。 后景攻王僧辩于巴陵，不克，败还，乃杀泉于江夏，沉其尸于黄鹄矶。 初，泉之为南讨都督也，其友人梦泉得罪于世祖，觉而告之。 后未旬，果见囚执。 顷之，又梦泉著硃衣而行水上，又告泉曰： 君勿忧，寻得免矣。 因说其梦，泉密记之，俄而复见任，皆如其梦。 泉于《仪礼》尤明，撰《新仪》四十卷，行于世。
target_text: Bao Quan, courtesy name Runyue, from Donghai, was well-read and skilled in writing. He served Emperor Yuan and was appointed governor of Xinzhou. He defeated Xiao Yu but was later accused of delaying the king's army and imprisoned by Wang Sengbian. He was forgiven and later served as chief historian in Yingzhou. The city fell due to neglect by Fang Zhu and Bao Quan, who were captured by Hou Jing. Bao Quan was killed in Jiangxia. He had prophetic dreams about his fate. He was an expert on "Ritual" and compiled forty volumes of "Xinyi."

input_text: 陈吏部尚书姚察曰：阮孝绪常言，仲尼论四科，始乎德行，终乎文学。 有行者多尚质朴，有文者少蹈规矩，故卫、石靡余论可传，屈、贾无立德之誉。 若夫宪章游、夏，祖述回、骞，体兼文行，于裴几原见之矣。
target_text: Yao Cha noted that Ruan Xiaoxu observed that virtue and literature rarely coexist, but Pei Ziye exemplified both, combining the qualities of Ziyou, Zixia, Yan Hui, and Ziqian.

input_text: 袁昂子君正袁昂，字千里，陈郡阳夏人。 祖询，宋征虏将军、吴郡太守，父抃，冠军将军、雍州刺史，泰始初，举兵奉晋安王子勋，事败诛死。 昂时年五岁，乳媪携抱匿于庐山，会赦得出，犹徙晋安。至元徽中听还，时年十五。 初，抃败，传首京师，藏于武库，至是始还之。 昂号恸呕血，绝而复苏，从兄彖尝抚视抑譬，昂更制服，庐于墓次。 后与彖同见从叔司徒粲，粲谓彖曰： 其幼孤而能至此，故知名器自有所在。 齐初，起家冠军安成王行参军，迁征虏主簿，太子舍人，王俭镇军府功曹史。 俭时为京尹，经于后堂独引见昂，指北堂谓昂曰： 卿必居此。 累迁秘书丞，黄门侍郎。 昂本名千里，齐永明中，武帝谓之曰： 昂昂千里之驹，在卿有之，今改卿名为昂。即千里为字。 出为安南鄱阳王长史、寻阳公相。 还为太孙中庶子、卫军武陵王长史。
target_text: Yuan Ang, courtesy name Qianli, was from Yangxia, Chen County. His grandfather and father were military officials in the Song Dynasty; his father was killed after supporting Prince Xun of Jin'an. At age five, Yuan Ang was hidden in Lushan by his wet nurse, returning home at fifteen after a pardon. He mourned his father deeply, vomiting blood and building a hut by the grave. Raised by his brother Yuan Yuzeng, he later served in various official posts under the Qi Dynasty, including Secretary Cheng and Huangmen Shilang. Emperor Wu of Qi renamed him Yuan Ang, using his courtesy name Qianli.

input_text: 虽礼无明据，乃事有先例，率迷而至，必欲行之。 君问礼所归，谨以谘白。 临纸号哽，言不识次。 服阕，除右军邵陵王长史，俄迁御史中丞。 时尚书令王晏弟诩为广州，多纳赇货，昂依事劾奏，不惮权豪，当时号为正直。 出为豫章内史，丁所生母忧去职。以丧还，江路风浪暴骇，昂乃缚衣著柩，誓同沉溺。 及风止，余船皆没，唯昂所乘船获全，咸谓精诚所致。 葬讫，起为建武将军、吴兴太守。 永元末，义师至京师，州牧郡守皆望风降款，昂独拒境不受命。 高祖手书喻曰： 夫祸福无门，兴亡有数，天之所弃，人孰能匡？ 机来不再，图之宜早。
target_text: During the Liang Dynasty, Yuan Ang held numerous high-ranking positions, such as Censor Zhongcheng, Prefect of Wuxing, and Minister of the Ministry of Personnel. He was known for his integrity, once impeaching a corrupt official despite the latter's powerful connections. When his mother died, he tied himself to her coffin during a storm, vowing to sink with it; the storm ceased, and his boat alone survived.

input_text: 册谥曰穆正公。 子君正，美风仪，善自居处，以贵公子得当世名誉。 顷之，兼吏部郎，以母忧去职。 服阕，为邵陵王友、北中郎长史、东阳太守。 寻征还都，郡民征士徐天祐等三百人诣阙乞留一年，诏不许，仍除豫章内史，寻转吴郡太守。 侯景乱，率数百人随邵陵王赴援，及京城陷，还郡。 君正当官莅事有名称，而蓄聚财产，服玩靡丽。 贼遣于子悦攻之，新城戍主戴僧易劝令拒守；吴陆映公等惧贼脱胜，略其资产，乃曰： 贼军甚锐，其锋不可当；今若拒之，恐民心不从也。 君正性怯懦，乃送米及牛酒，郊迎子悦。子悦既至，掠夺其财物子女，因是感疾卒。 史臣曰：夫天尊地卑，以定君臣之位；松筠等质，无革岁寒之心。 袁千里命属崩离，身逢厄季，虽独夫丧德，臣志不移；及抗疏高祖，无亏忠节，斯亦存夷、叔之风矣。 终为梁室台鼎，何其美焉。
target_text: At the end of the Yongyuan period, when the righteous army arrived, Yuan Ang initially resisted but later surrendered after Emperor Gaozu wrote him a letter. He was pardoned and continued to serve, eventually becoming Sikong, Shizhong, and Shangshuling. He died at age eighty, posthumously titled Muzheng Gong. In his final words, he refused posthumous honors, citing his humble origins and gratitude for imperial grace. His son, Zijun, also served in official posts but died of illness after Hou Jing's rebellion.

input_text: 册谥曰穆正公。 子君正，美风仪，善自居处，以贵公子得当世名誉。 顷之，兼吏部郎，以母忧去职。 服阕，为邵陵王友、北中郎长史、东阳太守。 寻征还都，郡民征士徐天祐等三百人诣阙乞留一年，诏不许，仍除豫章内史，寻转吴郡太守。 侯景乱，率数百人随邵陵王赴援，及京城陷，还郡。 君正当官莅事有名称，而蓄聚财产，服玩靡丽。 贼遣于子悦攻之，新城戍主戴僧易劝令拒守；吴陆映公等惧贼脱胜，略其资产，乃曰： 贼军甚锐，其锋不可当；今若拒之，恐民心不从也。 君正性怯懦，乃送米及牛酒，郊迎子悦。子悦既至，掠夺其财物子女，因是感疾卒。 史臣曰：夫天尊地卑，以定君臣之位；松筠等质，无革岁寒之心。 袁千里命属崩离，身逢厄季，虽独夫丧德，臣志不移；及抗疏高祖，无亏忠节，斯亦存夷、叔之风矣。 终为梁室台鼎，何其美焉。
target_text: The historical commentary praises Yuan Ang for his unwavering loyalty and integrity, comparing him to the virtuous Boyi and Shuqi, and noting his role in supporting the Liang dynasty.

input_text: 谢举，字言扬，中书令览之弟也。 幼好学，能清言，与览齐名。 举年十四，尝赠沈约五言诗，为约称赏。 世人为之语曰： 王有养、炬，谢有览、举。 养、炬，王筠、王泰小字也。 起家秘书郎，迁太子舍人，轻车功曹史，秘书丞，司空从事中郎，太子庶子，家令，掌东宫管记，深为昭明太子赏接。 秘书监任昉出为新安郡，别举诗云： 讵念耋嗟人，方深老夫托。 其属意如此。 尝侍宴华林园，高祖访举于览，览对曰： 识艺过臣甚远，惟饮酒不及于臣。 高祖大悦。 转太子中庶子，犹掌管记。 天监十一年，迁侍中。 十四年，出为宁远将军、豫章内史，为政和理，甚得民心。 十八年，复入为侍中，领步兵校尉。 普通元年，出为贞毅将军、太尉临川王长史。
target_text: Xie Ju, courtesy name Yan Yang, was the younger brother of Xie Lan. He was an eager learner from a young age, skilled in discussing mystical principles, and shared fame with Xie Li. He began his career as Secretary Lang and later held various positions, including Prince Sheren and Cao Shi of Qingchao Gong. He was deeply appreciated by Prince Zhaoming. Emperor Gaozu once asked Xie Ju for advice, and Xie Ju humbly replied that his knowledge was far superior but he was not as good in drinking, which pleased the emperor. He served as General Ningyuan and Internal History of Yuzhang, where his tolerant administration won the people's hearts. He later held several high-ranking positions, including Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and Shizhong. Xie Ju was well-read, especially in Laozi, Zhuangzi, and Buddhist philosophy. He once corrected Lu Guang's errors during a lecture, earning Lu's respect. He died in the besieged capital during Hou Jing's invasion. His works were lost in the war.

input_text: 是岁，侯景寇京师，举卒于围内。 诏赠侍中、中卫将军、开府仪同三司，侍中、尚书令如故。 文集乱中并亡逸。 二子禧，嘏，并少知名。 嘏，太清中，历太子中庶子，出为建安太守。 何敬容，字国礼，庐江人也。 祖攸之，宋太常卿；父昌珝，齐吏部尚书；并有名前代。 敬容以名家子，弱冠选尚齐武帝女长城公主，拜驸马都尉。 天监初，为秘书郎，历太子舍人，尚书殿中郎，太子洗马，中书舍人，秘书丞，迁扬州治中。 出为建安内史，清公有美绩，民吏称之。 还除黄门郎，累迁太子中庶子，散骑常侍，侍中，司徒左长史。 普通二年，复为侍中，领羽林监，俄又领本州大中正。 顷之，守吏部尚书，铨序明审，号为称职。 四年，出为招远将军、吴郡太守，为政勤恤民隐，辨讼如神，视事四年，治为天下第一。
target_text: He Jinrong, courtesy name Guoli, was born in Lujiang. He married Princess Changcheng and was awarded the title of Prince Consort. He served as Secretary Lang and later as Internal History of Jian'an, where he was praised for his honest and effective governance. He was known for his solemn demeanor and meticulous selection of officials. He served as Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and later as Shangshu Ling. He was diligent in government affairs, working day and night, but was despised by the world for his focus on administrative tasks rather than literary pursuits. He was convicted of deceiving the emperor for personal gain and was dismissed from office. He later died in the besieged capital during Hou Jing's rebellion. He Jinrong had a premonition of Hou Jing's rebellion, which came true. He was posthumously awarded General Renwei.

input_text: 王僧孺，字僧孺，东海郯人，魏卫将军肃八世孙。 曾祖雅，晋左光禄大夫、仪同三司。 祖准，宋司徒左长史。 僧孺年五岁，读《孝经》，问授者此书所载述，曰： 论忠孝二事。 僧孺曰： 若尔，常愿读之。 六岁能属文，既长好学。 家贫，常佣书以养母，所写既毕，讽诵亦通。 仕齐，起家王国左常侍、太学博士。 尚书仆射王晏深相赏好。 晏为丹阳尹，召补郡功曹，使僧孺撰《东宫新记》。 迁大司马豫章王行参军，又兼太学博士。 司徒竟陵王子良开西邸招文学，僧孺亦游焉。 文惠太子闻其名，召入东宫，直崇明殿。 欲拟为宫僚，文惠薨，不果。 时王晏子德元出为晋安郡，以僧孺补郡丞，除候官令。 建武初，有诏举士，扬州刺史始安王遥光表荐秘书丞王暕及僧孺曰： 前候官令东海王僧孺，年三十五，理尚栖约，思致悟敏，既笔耕为养，亦佣书成学。 至乃照萤映雪，编蒲缉柳，先言往行，人物雅俗，甘泉遗仪，南宫故事，画地成图，抵掌可述；岂直鼮鼠有必对之辩，竹书无落简之谬，访对不休，质疑斯在。 除尚书仪曹郎，迁治书侍御史，出为钱唐令。 初，僧孺与乐安任昉遇竟陵王西邸，以文学友会，及是将之县，昉赠诗，其略曰： 惟子见知，惟余知子。
target_text: Wang Sengru, courtesy name Sengru, was a native of Tan, Donghai, and the eighth-generation grandson of Wang Su, a general of the Wei Dynasty. His great-grandfather Wang Ya served as Dr. Zuo Guanglu and Yi Tong in the Jin Dynasty, while his grandfather Wang Zhun served as Situ Zuo Changshi in the Song Dynasty. At age five, Sengru read the "Book of Filial Piety" and asked his teacher about its contents. Told it discussed loyalty and filial piety, he expressed a desire to read it often. By six, he could write articles and grew up eager to learn. His family was poor, so he often copied books for others to support his mother, memorizing them afterward. He served as an official in the Qi Dynasty, recruited as the Kingdom's Zuo Changshi and Doctor of Taixue. Wang Yan, the minister of public affairs, admired him and appointed him to compile "New Records of the East Palace." He later held various posts, including Grand Sima Yuzhang and Wang Xing joined the army, and Doctor of Imperial College. Prince Wenhui summoned him to Shu Palace, but his planned appointment as a vassal of the crown prince was not implemented due to the prince's death. In the early years of the founding, an edict recommended talents, and Wang Luoguang praised Sengru's intelligence and familiarity with sages' words and deeds. He was awarded titles such as Cao Lang, Minister Yi, and later Chief Secretary, Censor, and Ling of Qian and Tang Dynasties.

input_text: 既至，拜中书郎、领著作，复直文德省，撰《中表簿》及《起居注》。 迁尚书左丞，领著作如故。 俄除游击将军，兼御史中丞。 僧孺幼贫，其母鬻纱布以自业，尝携僧孺至市，道遇中丞卤簿，驱迫沟中。 及是拜日，引驺清道，悲感不自胜。 寻以公事降为云骑将军，兼职如故，顷之即真。 是时高祖制《春景明志诗》五百字，敕在朝之人沈约已下同作，高祖以僧孺诗为工。 迁少府卿，出监吴郡。 还除尚书吏部郎，参大选，请谒不行。 出为仁威南康王长史，行府、州、国事。 王典签汤道愍昵于王，用事府内，僧孺每裁抑之，道愍遂谤讼僧孺，逮诣南司。 奉笺辞府曰： 下官不能避溺山隅，而正冠李下，既贻疵辱，方致徽绳，解箓收簪，且归初服。 窃以董生伟器，止相骄王；贾子上才，爰傅卑土。 下官生年有值，谬仰清尘，假翼西雍，窃步东阁，多惭袨服，取乱长裾，高榻相望，直居坐右，长阶如画，独在僚端。 借其从容之词，假以宽和之色，恩礼远过申、白，荣望多厕应、徐。
target_text: Sengru was highly regarded by his friends, including Ren Zuo, who wrote a poem praising his conduct and speech. In the early years of Tianjian, he served as governor of Nanhai, where he refused to exploit foreign merchants for profit, unlike previous officials. After one month, he was ordered to return to the capital, but six hundred people requested his retention, which the court denied. He then became Zhongshulang, compiled "Zhongbiaobu" and "Daily Notes," and later served as Minister Zuocheng and guerrilla general. When his mother, who had sold gauze for a living, died, he grieved deeply. He was demoted to General Yunqi due to official duties but soon returned to full-time work. Emperor Gaozu praised his poem "Poetry on Spring Scenery and Mingzhi" as the most exquisite among those composed by officials. He later served as Shaofu Qing and Shangshu Libulang, participating in official selections. As chief historian of King Renwei of Nankang, he suppressed the domineering Wang Dian, who slandered him, leading to his arrest and imprisonment. In a farewell letter to the king, Sengru expressed regret for his imprisonment and lamented his inability to repay the king's kindness. He was dismissed from office and not promoted for a long time.

input_text: 岂复得与二三士友，抱接膝之欢，履足差肩，摛绮縠之清文，谈希微之道德。 唯吴冯之遇夏馥，范彧之值孔嵩，愍其留赁，怜此行乞耳。 傥不以垢累，时存寸札，则虽先犬马，犹松乔焉。 去矣何生，高树芳烈。 裁书代面，笔泪俱下。 久之，起为安西安成王参军，累迁镇右始兴王中记室，北中郎南康王谘议参军，入直西省，知撰谱事。 普通三年，卒，时年五十八。 僧孺好坟籍，聚书至万余卷，率多异本，与沈约、任昉家书相埒。 少笃志精力，于书无所不睹。 其文丽逸，多用新事，人所未见者，世重其富。 僧孺集《十八州谱》七百一十卷，《百家谱集》十五卷，《东南谱集抄》十卷，文集三十卷，《两台弹事》不入集内为五卷，及《东宫新记》，并行于世。
target_text: Sengru wrote to his friend He Jiong, expressing his sorrow and describing his suffering. He lamented his lack of talent and the misfortunes that had befallen him, including illness and humiliation. He reflected on his low status and the envy of others, noting that his family was poor and he had no gifts to offer friends. He felt isolated and slandered, leading to his deposition. He described the sadness of autumn and his loneliness, living among birds and beasts. He hoped to meet intellectual friends again but feared he would die in obscurity. After a long time, he was appointed by King Cheng of Anxi to join the army and later served in various posts, including Wang Zhongji of Youduo County. He died three years later at age fifty-eight. Sengru loved ancient classics and collected over 10,000 volumes of books, many rare. His articles were elegant and recorded new things. His works included "Eighteen Prefecture Genealogy" (710 volumes), "Collection of Hundred Family Genealogy" (15 volumes), "Collection of Southeastern Genealogy" (10 volumes), and "Collection of Essays" (30 volumes), among others.

input_text: 张率，字士简，吴郡吴人。 祖永，宋右光禄大夫。 父瑰，齐世显贵，归老乡邑，天监初，授右光禄，加给事中。 率年十二，能属文，常日限为诗一篇，稍进作赋颂，至年十六，向二千许首。 齐始安王萧遥光为扬州，召迎主簿，不就。 起家著作佐郎。 建武三年，举秀才，除太子舍人。 与同郡陆倕幼相友狎，常同载诣左卫将军沈约，适值任昉在焉，约乃谓昉曰： 此二子后进才秀，皆南金也，卿可与定交。 由此与昉友善。 迁尚书殿中郎。 出为西中郎南康王功曹史，以疾不就。 久之，除太子洗马。 高祖霸府建，引为相国主簿。 天监初，临川王已下并置友、学。 以率为鄱阳王友，迁司徒谢朏掾，直文德待诏省。敕使抄乙部书，又使撰妇人事二十余条，勒成百卷。使工书人琅邪王深、吴郡范怀约、褚洵等缮写，以给后宫。 率又为《待诏赋》奏之，甚见称赏。手敕答曰： 省赋殊佳。 相如工而不敏，枚皋速而不工，卿可谓兼二子于金马矣。 又侍宴赋诗，高祖乃别赐率诗曰： 东南有才子，故能服官政。
target_text: Zhang Shu, courtesy name Shi Jian, was from Wu County. His grandfather Zhang Yong served as Doctor Youguanglu in the Song Dynasty, and his father Zhang Quan held high status in the Qi Dynasty. At twelve, Zhang Shu could write articles, limiting himself to one poem daily. By sixteen, he had written over two thousand poems. In the Qi Dynasty, he was summoned as chief secretary by Xiao Yaoguang but did not take the post. He started as Zuo Lang and later became Prince Sheren. He was friendly with Lu Chui, and they visited Shen Yue together, who praised them as outstanding talents. Zhang Shu was moved to various posts, including Zhonglang of Shangshu Palace and Xizhonglang. He served as prince to wash horses and later as chief minister of the state. In the early years of Tianjian, he was appointed as a plastic orbit friend. He was moved to Situ Xie Naotun and ordered to copy books and write articles on women's affairs. He wrote "Wai Shao Fu," praised by Emperor Gaozu, who compared him to Sima Xiangru and Mei Gao. He was moved to Secretary Cheng and treated with great honor. In March of the fourth year, a banquet was held in Huaguang Hall, where he wrote a poem about a dancing horse. He later served in various posts, including Zhongquan Jian'an Wang Zhongji's Office and Yunhui Zhongji Office. He stayed in the palace for ten years, receiving great favor. After returning to the capital, he served as a servant of the prince and later as General Zhaoyuan. He was moved to Huangmen Shilang and later became prefect of Xin'an. He died before the mourning period for his mother was over at age fifty-three. Prince Zhaoming sent an envoy to present funeral property. Zhang Shu liked drinking, was tolerant, and did not mind housework. He wrote fifteen volumes of "Wenheng" and thirty volumes of collected works.

input_text: 其人才笔弘雅，亦足嗟惜。 随弟府朝，东西日久，尤当伤怀也。 比人物零落，特可潸慨，属有今信，乃复及之。 率嗜酒，事事宽恕，于家务尤忘怀。 在新安，遣家僮载米三千石还吴宅，既至，遂秏太半。 率问其故，答曰： 雀鼠秏也。 率笑而言曰： 壮哉雀鼠。 竟不研问。 少好属文，而《七略》及《艺文志》所载诗赋，今亡其文者，并补作之。 所著《文衡》十五卷，文集三十卷，行于世。 子长公嗣。 刘孝绰，字孝绰，彭城人，本名冉。 祖勔，宋司空忠昭公。 父绘，齐大司马霸府从事中郎。 孝绰幼聪敏，七岁能属文。 舅齐中书郎王融深赏异之，常与同载适亲友，号曰神童。 融每言曰： 天下文章，若无我当归阿士。 阿士，孝绰小字也。 绘，齐世掌诏诰。 孝绰年未志学，绘常使代草之。 父党沈约、任昉、范云等闻其名，并命驾先造焉，昉尤相赏好。 范云年长绘十余岁，其子孝才与孝绰年并十四五，及云遇孝绰，便申伯季，乃命孝才拜之。 天监初，起家著作佐郎，为《归沐诗》以赠任昉，昉报章曰： 彼美洛阳子，投我怀秋作。 讵慰耋嗟人，徒深老夫托。
target_text: Liu Xiaochuo, courtesy name Xiaochuo, was from Pengcheng. His grandfather Liu Meng was Duke Zhongzhao of Sikong in the Song Dynasty, and his father Ming Hui served as a lieutenant. Xiaochuo could write articles at seven and was admired by his uncle Wang Rong as a child prodigy. He drafted for his father during the Qi Dynasty. Shen Yue, Ren Fang, and Fan Yun visited him, with Ren Fang particularly appreciative. In the early years of Tianjian, he started as Zuo Lang and wrote "Poem of Returning to Mu." He was moved to Prince Sheren and later served as an official and minister of the Ministry of Water. Emperor Gaozu praised his articles and appointed him to various posts, including Secretary Cheng. He served as a consultant to King Ansheng and later as Minister of the Taifu and Prince's Servant. Prince Zhaoming treated him as a distinguished guest and had his portrait painted in Lexian Hall. Xiaochuo compiled the prince's collection and wrote the preface. He was moved to Sanqi Changshi and later served as Tingweiqing. He was dismissed after being impeached for bringing his concubine into the government while his mother lived elsewhere. He wrote letters criticizing Dao Qia, which were burned by Prince Zhaoming. He later served as Xizhong Lang to consult with the king of Xiangdong. He thanked the emperor and crown prince for their favor. He later served as a servant of the prince and died at age fifty-nine. Xiaochuo was famous but willful and scornful of others. His articles were highly valued and widely circulated. His three younger sisters were married to talented men, and his wife was particularly elegant.

input_text: 悱，仆射徐勉子，为晋安郡，卒，丧还京师，妻为祭文，辞甚忄妻怆。 勉本欲为哀文，既睹此文，于是阁笔。 孝绰子谅，字求信。 少好学，有文才，尤博悉晋代故事，时人号曰 皮里晋书 。 历官著作佐郎，太子舍人，王府主簿，功曹史，中城王记室参军。 王筠，字元礼，一字德柔，琅邪临沂人。 祖僧虔，齐司空简穆公。 父楫，太中大夫。 筠幼警寤，七岁能属文。 年十六，为《芍药赋》，甚美。 及长，清静好学，与从兄泰齐名。 陈郡谢览，览弟举，亦有重誉，时人为之语曰： 谢有览举，王有养炬。 炬是泰，养即筠，并小字也。 起家中军临川王行参军，迁太子舍人，除尚书殿中郎。 王氏过江以来，未有居郎署者，或劝逡巡不就，筠曰： 陆平原东南之秀，王文度独步江东，吾得比踪昔人，何所多恨。
target_text: Wang Jun, also named Yuanli and Derou, was from Linyi, Langxie. His grandfather Jianglu served as Duke of Kong Gelong, and his father Dan served as Taizhong doctor. Wang Jun could write articles at seven and wrote "Ode to Peony Root" at sixteen. He was as famous as his cousin Wang Tai. He started his career joining the army as King Xing of Linchuan and later served as Prince Sheren. He was appointed Zhonglang of the Shangshu Palace, a rare position for the Wang family. Shen Yue praised his articles, saying he was unmatched. Wang Jun wrote poems with uncommon rhymes and was highly regarded by Prince Zhaoming. He served as Danyang Yin Cheng and later as Zhongshu Lang. He compiled "Zhongshu Biaozuo" and other works. He was appointed Shangshu Libulang and later served as Prince's concubine. After Prince Zhaoming's death, he wrote a mourning poem. He served as General Zhenwei and Prefect of Linhai but was sued. He later served as Yunzhang Wang Changshi and moved to secretary supervisor. He died at age sixty-nine after falling into a well during a thief attack. Wang Jun was generous and loyal, famous for his talents. He wrote extensively, copying many classics himself. His collection included one hundred volumes of articles.

input_text: 元法僧，魏氏之支属也。 其始祖道武帝。 父钟葵，江阳王。 法僧仕魏，历光禄大夫，后为使持节、都督徐州诸军事、徐州刺史，镇彭城。 普通五年，魏室大乱，法僧遂据镇称帝，诛锄异己，立诸子为王，部署将帅，欲议匡复。 既而魏乱稍定，将讨法僧。法僧惧，乃遣使归款，请为附庸，高祖许焉，授侍中、司空，封始安郡公，邑五千户。 及魏军既逼，法僧请还朝，高祖遣中书舍人硃异迎之。 既至，甚加优宠。 时方事招携，抚悦降附，赐法僧甲第女乐及金帛，前后不可胜数。 法僧以在魏之日，久处疆埸之任，每因寇掠，杀戮甚多，求兵自卫，诏给甲仗百人，出入禁闼。 大通二年，加冠军将军。
target_text: The lives of several individuals from the Northern Wei Dynasty who later served the Liang Dynasty, focusing on their careers, military actions, and fates.

input_text: 出为持节、都督广、越等十三州诸军事、宣惠将军、平越中郎将、广州刺史。 大同中，征侍中、左卫将军。 兄景隆后为广州刺史。 侯景作乱，以景仲元氏之族，遣信诱之，许奉为主。 景仲乃举兵，将下应景。 会西江督护陈霸先与成州刺史王怀明等起兵攻之，霸先徇其众曰： 朝廷以元景仲与贼连从，谋危社稷，今使曲江公勃为刺史，镇抚此州。 众闻之，皆弃甲而散，景仲乃自缢而死。 元树，字君立，亦魏之近属也。 祖献文帝。 父僖，咸阳王。 树仕魏为宗正卿，属尔硃荣乱，以天监八年归国，封为鄴王，邑二千户，拜散骑常侍。 普通六年，应接元法僧还朝，迁使持节、督郢、司、霍三州诸军事、云麾将军、郢州刺史，增封并前为三千户。 讨南蛮贼，平之，加散骑常侍、安西将军，又增邑五百户。
target_text: Yuan Faseng, a relative of the Northern Wei imperial family, served as an official and later declared himself emperor during a period of chaos. He submitted to the Liang Dynasty and was granted high titles. He died at age 83, and his sons, Jinglong and Jingzhong, also served the Liang. Jingzhong later rebelled with Hou Jing but was defeated and hanged himself.

input_text: 中大通二年，征侍中、镇右将军。 四年，为使持节，镇北将军，都督北讨诸军事，加鼓吹一部以伐魏，攻魏谯城，拔之。 会魏将独孤如愿来援，遂围树，城陷被执，发愤卒于魏，时年四十八。 子贞，大同中，求随魏使崔长谦至鄴葬父，还拜太子舍人。 太清初，侯景降，请元氏戚属，愿奉为主，诏封贞为咸阳王，以天子之礼遣还北，会景败而返。 元愿达，亦魏之支庶也。 祖明元帝。 父乐平王。 愿达仕魏为中书令、郢州刺史。 普通中，大军北伐，攻义阳，愿达举州献款，诏封乐平公，邑千户，赐甲第女乐。 仍出为使持节、散骑常侍、都督湘州诸军事、平南将军、湘州刺史。 中大通二年，征侍中、太中大夫、翊左将军。 大同三年，卒，时年五十七。 王神念，太原祁人也。 少好儒术，尤明内典。 仕魏起家州主簿，稍迁颍川太守，遂据郡归款。 魏军至，与家属渡江，封南城县侯，邑五百户。 顷之，除安成内史，又历武阳、宣城内史，皆著治绩。 还除太仆卿。 出为持节、都督青、冀二州诸军事、信武将军、青、冀二州刺史。 神念性刚正，所更州郡必禁止淫祠。 时青、冀州东北有石鹿山临海，先有神庙，妖巫欺惑百姓，远近祈祷，糜费极多。及神念至，便令毁撤，风俗遂改。
target_text: Yuanshu, another Northern Wei relative, served as an official and later defected to the Liang. He was appointed to military and civil posts, captured a city, but was eventually captured and died in the Northern Wei at age 48.

input_text: 中大通二年，征侍中、镇右将军。 四年，为使持节，镇北将军，都督北讨诸军事，加鼓吹一部以伐魏，攻魏谯城，拔之。 会魏将独孤如愿来援，遂围树，城陷被执，发愤卒于魏，时年四十八。 子贞，大同中，求随魏使崔长谦至鄴葬父，还拜太子舍人。 太清初，侯景降，请元氏戚属，愿奉为主，诏封贞为咸阳王，以天子之礼遣还北，会景败而返。 元愿达，亦魏之支庶也。 祖明元帝。 父乐平王。 愿达仕魏为中书令、郢州刺史。 普通中，大军北伐，攻义阳，愿达举州献款，诏封乐平公，邑千户，赐甲第女乐。 仍出为使持节、散骑常侍、都督湘州诸军事、平南将军、湘州刺史。 中大通二年，征侍中、太中大夫、翊左将军。 大同三年，卒，时年五十七。 王神念，太原祁人也。 少好儒术，尤明内典。 仕魏起家州主簿，稍迁颍川太守，遂据郡归款。 魏军至，与家属渡江，封南城县侯，邑五百户。 顷之，除安成内史，又历武阳、宣城内史，皆著治绩。 还除太仆卿。 出为持节、都督青、冀二州诸军事、信武将军、青、冀二州刺史。 神念性刚正，所更州郡必禁止淫祠。 时青、冀州东北有石鹿山临海，先有神庙，妖巫欺惑百姓，远近祈祷，糜费极多。及神念至，便令毁撤，风俗遂改。
target_text: Yuan Yuanda, a branch of the Wei family, served in the Northern Wei and later submitted to the Liang, receiving titles and positions. He died at age 57.

target_text: Wang Shennian, from Qi, was a Confucian scholar who served as a prefect in the Northern Wei and later defected to the Liang. He was known for his uprightness, destroying a fraudulent temple. He died at age 75, and his son also served as an official.

input_text: 普通中，大举北伐，征为右卫将军。 六年，迁使持节、散骑常侍、爪牙将军，右卫如故。 遘疾卒，时年七十五。 诏赠本官、衡州刺史，兼给鼓吹一部。 谥曰壮。 神念少善骑射，既老不衰，尝于高祖前手执二刀楯，左右交度，驰马往来，冠绝群伍。 时复有杨华者，能作惊军骑，并一时妙捷，高祖深叹赏之。 子尊业，仕至太仆卿。 卒，赠信威将军、青、冀二州刺史，鼓吹一部。 次子僧辩，别有传。 杨华，武都仇池人也。 父大眼，为魏名将。 华少有勇力，容貌雄伟，魏胡太后逼通之，华惧及祸，乃率其部曲来降。 胡太后追思之不能已，为作《杨白华歌辞》，使宫人昼夜连臂蹋足歌之，辞甚忄妻惋焉。 华后累征伐，有战功，历官太仆卿，太子左卫率，封益阳县侯。
target_text: Yang Hua, from Qiuchi, was a brave general forced into adultery by Empress Dowager Hu. He defected to the Liang, served in expeditions, and later surrendered to Hou Jing, dying in the rebel territory.

input_text: 太清中，侯景乱，华欲立志节，妻子为贼所擒，遂降之，卒于贼。 羊侃，字祖忻，泰山梁甫人，汉南阳太守续之裔也。 祖规，宋武帝之临徐州，辟祭酒从事、大中正。 会薛安都举彭城降北，规由是陷魏，魏授卫将军、营州刺史。 父祉，魏侍中，金紫光禄大夫。 侃少而瑰伟，身长七尺八寸，雅爱文史，博涉书记，尤好《左氏春秋》及《孙吴兵法》。 弱冠随父在梁州立功。 魏正光中，稍为别将。 时秦州羌有莫遮念生者，据州反，称帝，仍遣其弟天生率众攻陷岐州，遂寇雍州。 侃为偏将，隶萧宝夤往讨之，潜身巡緌，伺射天生，应弦即倒，其众遂溃。 以功迁使持节、征东大将军、东道行台，领泰山太守，进爵钜平侯。 初，其父每有南归之志，常谓诸子曰： 人生安可久淹异域，汝等可归奉东朝。 侃至是将举河济以成先志。 兗州刺史羊敦，侃从兄也，密知之，据州拒侃。
target_text: Yang Kan, from Tai Shan, was a tall and learned man who followed his father in military service. He shot a rebel leader, was promoted, and later defected to the Liang with his family. He was besieged by Wei forces but broke out, arriving in the Liang capital. He served in various military posts, advised against attacking Hou Jing prematurely, and defended the capital during Hou Jing's rebellion. He refused bribes, used tactics to counter siege engines, and remained loyal despite his son being captured. He died of illness at age 54, known for his bravery, strength, and luxurious lifestyle.

input_text: 破郭元建于东关，迁使持节、信武将军、东晋州刺史。 承圣三年，西魏围江陵，鹍赴援不及，从王僧愔征萧勃于岭表。闻大尉僧辩败，乃还，为侯瑱所破，于豫章遇害，时年二十八。 羊鸦仁，字孝穆，太山钜平人也。 少骁果有胆力，仕郡为主簿。 普通中，率兄弟自魏归国，封广晋县侯。 征伐青、齐间，累有功绩，稍迁员外散骑常侍、历阳太守。 中大通四年，为持节、都督谯州诸军事、信威将军、谯州刺史。 大同七年，除太子左卫率，出为持节、都督南、北司、豫、楚四州诸军事、轻车将军、北司州刺史。 侯景降，诏鸦仁督士州刺史桓和之、仁州刺史湛海珍等精兵三万，趋悬瓠应接景，仍为都督豫、司、淮、冀、殷、应、西豫等七州诸军事、司、豫二州刺史，镇悬瓠。 会侯景败于涡阳，魏军渐逼，鸦仁恐粮运不继，遂还北司，上表陈谢。高祖大怒，责之，鸦仁惧，又顿军于淮上。 及侯景反，鸦仁率所部入援。 太清二年，景既背盟，鸦仁乃与赵伯超及南康王会理共攻贼于东府城，反为贼所败。 台城陷，鸦仁见景，为景所留，以为五兵尚书。 鸦仁常思奋发，谓所亲曰： 吾以凡流，受宠朝廷，竟无报效，以答重恩。
target_text: Yang Yaren, also from Tai Shan, was brave and served as an official. He defected to the Liang, was granted a marquisate, and held military commands. He was sent to pick up Hou Jing but later feared punishment. During Hou Jing's rebellion, he aided the court but was defeated. After the capital fell, he served Hou Jing but planned to flee, eventually being killed.

input_text: 社稷倾危，身不能死，偷生苟免，以至于今。 若以此终，没有余愤。 因遂泣下，见者伤焉。 三年，出奔江西，其故部曲数百人迎之，将赴江陵，至东莞，为故北徐州刺史荀伯道诸子所害。 史臣曰：高祖革命受终，光期宝运，威德所渐，莫不怀来，其皆殉难投身，前后相属。 元法僧之徒入国，并降恩遇，位重任隆，击钟鼎食，美矣。 而羊侃、鸦仁值太清之难，并竭忠奉国。 侃则临危不挠，鸦仁守义殒命，可谓志等松筠，心均铁石，古之殉节，斯其谓乎！
target_text: The text concludes with a commentary praising the loyalty of Yang Kan and Yang Yaren during the Taiqing period, comparing their steadfastness to ancient martyrs.

input_text: 陈庆之兰钦陈庆之，字子云，义兴国山人也。 幼而随从高祖。高祖性好棋，每从夜达旦不辍，等辈皆倦寐，惟庆之不寝，闻呼即至，甚见亲赏。 从高祖东下平建鄴，稍为主书，散财聚士，常思效用。 除奉朝请。 普通中，魏徐州刺史元法僧于彭城求入内附，以庆之为武威将军，与胡龙牙、成景俊率诸军应接。 还，除宣猛将军、文德主帅，仍率军二千，送豫章王综入镇徐州。 魏遣安豊王元延明、临淮王元彧率众二万来拒，屯据陟□。 延明先遣其别将丘大千筑垒浔梁，观兵近境。 庆之进薄其垒，一鼓便溃。 后豫章王弃军奔魏，众皆溃散，诸将莫能制止。庆之乃斩关夜退，军士得全。 普通七年，安西将军元树出征寿春，除庆之假节、总知军事。 魏豫州刺史李宪遣其子长钧别筑两城相拒。庆之攻之，宪力屈遂降，庆之入据其城。 转东宫直阁，赐爵关中侯。 大通元年，隶领军曹仲宗伐涡阳。 魏遣征南将军常山王元昭等率马步十五万来援，前军至驼涧，去涡阳四十里。
target_text: Chen Qingzhi, courtesy name Ziyun, from Yixingguoshan, served Emperor Gaozu from youth. Gaozu loved chess, playing tirelessly; while others tired and slept, Qingzhi remained alert and responsive, earning high regard. He followed Gaozu to pacify Jianye, served as chief secretary, and recruited soldiers with dispersed funds. He was granted an imperial invitation. In the ordinary years, Wei's Xuzhou governor Yuan Faseng sought attachment to Pengcheng. Qingzhi, as a powerful general, led Hu Longya and Cheng Jingjun to escort him. After returning, he became General Xuanmeng and Commander Wende, leading 2,000 troops to guard Xuzhou with Xiao Zong. Wei sent Prince Yanming of Anfeng and Prince Yuan of Linhuai with 20,000 troops to resist at Zhikou. Yanming's general Qiu Dagan built a fort at Xunliang; Qingzhi defeated him in a single battle. Later, King Yuzhang fled to Wei, causing a rout. Qingzhi cut bolts, breached the city, and retreated at night, saving his sergeants.

target_text: In the seventh ordinary year, General Yuan Shu of Anxi went to Shouchun. Wei's Yuzhou governor Li Xian sent his son to build forts; Qingzhi attacked, Li Xian surrendered, and Qingzhi occupied the city. He was transferred to Donggong Zhihe and titled Marquis of Guanzhong. In Datong's first year, a subordinate leader fortified and conquered Yan. General Changshan Wang Yuanzhao led 150,000 cavalry and infantry to rescue, reaching Tuojian, 40 miles from Guoyang. Qingzhi wanted to fight, but Tong Zhen advised caution. Qingzhi argued the Wei were tired and unsuspecting; he led 200 cavalry to defeat their front army. The Wei were horrified. Qingzhi then returned, and the generals attacked together, occupying Woyang City. From spring to winter, hundreds of battles ensued. The army grew exhausted, and Wei reinforcements threatened. Zhongzong and others planned retreat, but Qingzhi insisted on fighting, capturing four of thirteen Wei fortifications. Wang Wei of Woyang surrendered. Qingzhi displayed captured ears, beat drums, and attacked, causing the enemy to collapse. Over 30,000 men and women were captured. West Xuzhou was established on Guoyang's land. Emperor Gaozu praised Qingzhi in a personal letter.

input_text: 魏将丘大千有众七万，分筑九城以相拒。 庆之攻之，自旦至申，陷其三垒，大千乃降。 时魏征东将军济阴王元晖业率羽林庶子二万人来救梁、宋，进屯考城，城四面萦水，守备严固。 庆之命浮水筑垒，攻陷其城，生擒晖业，获租车七千八百辆。 仍趋大梁，望旗归款。 颢进庆之卫将军、徐州刺史、武都公。 仍率众而西。 魏左仆射杨昱、西阿王元庆、抚军将军元显恭率御仗羽林宗子庶子众凡七万，据荥阳拒颢。 兵既精强，城又险固，庆之攻未能拔。 魏将元天穆大军复将至，先遣其骠骑将军尔硃吐没儿领胡骑五千，骑将鲁安领夏州步骑九千，援杨昱；又遣右仆射尔硃世隆、西荆州刺史王罴骑一万，据虎牢。 天穆、吐没儿前后继至，旗鼓相望。 时荥阳未拔，士众皆恐，庆之乃解鞍秣马，宣喻众曰： 吾至此以来，屠城略地，实为不少；君等杀人父兄，略人子女，又为无算。 天穆之众，并是仇雠。 我等才有七千，虏众三十余万，今日之事，义不图存。 吾以虏骑不可争力平原，及未尽至前，须平其城垒，诸君无假狐疑，自贻屠脍。 一鼓悉使登城，壮士东阳宋景休、义兴鱼天愍逾堞而入，遂克之。 俄而魏阵外合，庆之率骑三千背城逆战，大破之，鲁安于阵乞降，元天穆、尔硃吐没儿单骑获免。
target_text: In early Datong, Wei's Wang Yuanhao surrendered due to internal chaos, seeking to become lord of Wei. Emperor Gaozu appointed Qingzhi as Jiejie and Biaoyong General, sending Yuan Hao north. Yuan Hao declared himself Emperor of Wei at Huanshui. Qingzhi, as Chijie and commander, advanced from Liao County to Suiyang. Wei general Qiu Dagan had 70,000 troops in nine forts; Qingzhi captured three by afternoon, and Daqian surrendered. Wei's Jiyin Wang Yuanhuiye led 20,000 troops to rescue; Qingzhi built a fortress on water, captured the city, and seized 7,800 tax vehicles. Heading to Dafun, enemies surrendered at the sight of his flag. Qingzhi became General of the Guard and Governor of Lansu. He led forces west. Wei's Yang Yu, Xi'a Wang Yuanqing, and Yuan Xianggong led 70,000 troops to hold Rongyang. Qingzhi failed to capture it. Wei general Yuan Tianmu's army approached; Qingzhi, with only 7,000 troops against 300,000 captives, rallied his men, conquered Rongyang, and defeated Tianmu's army. He entered Hulao, and Zhu Shichen fled. Yuan Ziyou fled, and Yuan Hao entered Luoyang Palace, ascending the throne. Qingzhi was appointed servant and general, with increased households. Wei generals led 40,000 troops to capture Daliang; Qingzhi's white-robed subordinates were invincible. A Luoyang nursery rhyme warned: "Thousands of troops should avoid white robes." From Zhixian to Luoyang, in 140 days, Qingzhi leveled 32 fortresses and fought 47 battles, unstoppable.

input_text: 荣将退，时有刘助者，善天文，乃谓荣曰： 不出十日，河南大定。 荣乃缚木为筏，济自硖石，与颢战于河桥，颢大败，走至临颍，遇贼被擒，洛阳陷。 庆之马步数千，结阵东反，荣亲自来追，值蒿高山水洪溢，军人死散。 庆之乃落须发为沙门，间行至豫州，豫州人程道雍等潜送出汝阴。 至都，仍以功除右卫将军，封永兴县侯，邑一千五百户。 出为持节、都督缘淮诸军事、奋武将军、北兗州刺史。 会有妖贼沙门僧强自称为帝，土豪蔡伯龙起兵应之。僧强颇知幻术，更相扇惑，众至三万，攻陷北徐州，济阴太守杨起文弃城走，钟离太守单希宝见害，使庆之讨焉。 车驾幸白下，临饯谓庆之曰： 江、淮兵劲，其锋难当，卿可以策制之，不宜决战。 庆之受命而行。 曾未浃辰，斩伯龙、僧强，传其首。 中大通二年，除都督南、北司、西豫、豫四州诸军事、南、北司二州刺史，余并如故。 庆之至镇，遂围悬瓠。 破魏颍州刺史娄起、扬州刺史是云宝于溱水，又破行台孙腾、大都督侯进、豫州刺史尧雄、梁州刺史司马恭于楚城。 罢义阳镇兵，停水陆转运，江湖诸州并得休息。 开田六千顷，二年之后，仓廪充实。 高祖每嘉劳之。 又表省南司州，复安陆郡，置上明郡。 大同二年，魏遣将侯景率众七万寇楚州，刺史桓和陷没，景仍进军淮上，贻庆之书使降。 敕遣湘潭侯退、右卫夏侯夔等赴援，军至黎浆，庆之已击破景。 时大寒雪，景弃辎重走，庆之收之以归。
target_text: Yuan Hao indulged in wine and sex, plotting against Qingzhi. Qingzhi planned secretly but was alienated. Yuan Hao refused to send more troops. Qingzhi's deputy warned of danger, suggesting killing Yuan Hao, but Qingzhi refused. Yuan Hao appointed Qingzhi governor of Xuzhou but feared him and didn't send him. Wei's Ji Zhufu and others, claiming millions, attacked Yuan Hao. Qingzhi crossed the Yellow River to defend Beizhonglang City, fighting eleven times in three days. Ji Zhurong nearly retreated but was advised to stay. He crossed the river, defeated Yuan Hao, and Luoyang fell. Qingzhi, with thousands, formed a formation and returned east. Ji Zhurong pursued; Songgao Mountain flooded, scattering his soldiers. Qingzhi shaved his head, became a monk, and traveled to Yuzhou. He was secretly sent to the capital, awarded General Youwei and Yongxing County Fortress. Later, as Chijie and governor of Northern Yanzhou, he defeated the demon thief monk Tan Qiang, killing him in twelve days. In Zhongdatong's second year, he became military governor of four states. He opened 6,000 hectares of land, filling warehouses. In Datong's second year, Wei's Hou Jing invaded Chuzhou; Qingzhi defeated him in snowy conditions. He was promoted to General Renwei. During a famine in Yuzhou, he opened warehouses for relief. He died at fifty-six, posthumously honored. Qingzhi was cautious, wore no silk, disliked music, and comforted his soldiers well.
