target_text: After Li Guangli attacked Dayuan, Western Region countries sent envoys to Chang'an. The Han Dynasty built pavilions and barriers from Dunhuang to Yanze, stationed field soldiers in Luntai and Quli, and set up envoys and captains to supervise farming. During Emperor Xuan's reign, Wei Sima oversaw several countries west of Shanshan. After defeating Gu Shi, the Han Dynasty divided it into the former and latter kings of Cheshi and the six kingdoms of Shanbei, initially supervising only the southern route. Later, King Rizhu betrayed Chanyu and surrendered to the Han Dynasty. Zheng Ji, the envoy protecting Shanshan, met King Rizhu, and both were granted marquis titles. The Han Dynasty established the Protectorate, beginning with Zheng Ji, who protected the North Road. The Xiongnu's child servant captain was dismissed, weakening the Xiongnu. The Han Dynasty moved people to farm in Beixu Tar, dividing Shache's land. The Protectorate monitored Wusun, Kangju, and other foreign countries, stationed in Wulei City, 2,738 miles from Yangguan, due to its fertile land and central location.

input_text: 其弟尉屠耆降汉，具言状。 元凤四年，大将军霍光白遣平乐监傅介子往刺其王。 介子轻将勇敢士，赍金币，扬言以赐外国为名。 既至楼兰，诈其王欲赐之，王喜，与介子饮，醉，将其王屏语，壮士二人从后刺杀之，贵人左右皆散走。 介子告谕以： 王负汉罪，天子遣我诛王，当更立王弟尉屠耆在汉者。 汉兵方至，毋敢动，自令灭国矣！ 介子遂斩王尝归首，驰传诣阙，悬首北阙下。 封介子为义阳侯。 乃立尉屠耆为王，更名其国为鄯善，为刻印章，赐以宫女为夫人，备车骑辎重，丞相将军率百官送至横门外，祖而遣之。 王自请天子曰： 身在汉久，今归，单弱，而前王有子在，恐为所杀。 国中有伊循城，其地肥美，愿汉遣一将屯田积谷，令臣得依其威重。 于是汉遣司马一人、吏士四十人，田伊循以填抚之。 其后更置都尉。 伊循官置始此矣。 鄯善当汉道冲，西通且末七百二十里。 自且末以往皆种五谷，土地草木，畜产作兵，略与汉同，有异乃记云。
target_text: During Emperor Yuan's reign, Wuji Xiaowei was appointed to man fields. Wang Zilizhi of Baotui Dongpu surrendered with over 1,700 people, and the Protectorate allocated land for them. Since the Xuancha and Wutong period, Li Sculpture Chanyu Xianghui became a vassal, and details of land, mountains, rivers, and distances were recorded. Starting from the nearest west of Yangguan, the Laoqiang Kingdom had 450 households, 1,750 people, and 500 troops, living with livestock and not farming. The Shanshan Kingdom (formerly Loulan) had 1,570 households, 14,100 people, and 2,912 troops, with officials including Fu Guohou and translators. It produced jade, reeds, and willow, and its people lived with livestock. Initially, Emperor Wu was moved by Zhang Qian's words and sent many envoys to Dawan. Loulan and Gushi, on the main road, attacked Han envoys and acted as Xiongnu spies. Emperor Wu sent Zhao Ponu and Wang Hui to attack Gushi and capture the King of Loulan, leading to the construction of pavilions west to Yumen Pass. Loulan surrendered but later sent hostages to both the Han and Xiongnu. After King Loulan died, the Han Dynasty could not send back a castrated hostage, leading to a new king who declined to visit the Han emperor. Later, Wei Tuqi, the king's brother, surrendered to the Han Dynasty. In the fourth year of Yuanfeng, Fu Jiezi assassinated King Loulan, established Wei Tuqi as king, and renamed the country Shanshan. The Han Dynasty sent a Sima and forty officials to garrison Yixun, marking the beginning of official establishment there. Shanshan was a strategic point on the road to the Western Regions, with various countries like Qiemo, Xiaowan, Jingjue, Ronglu, Shanmi, Qule, Khotan, Pishan, Wushuo, Xiye, Puli, Yinai, Wulei, Nandou, and Jibin, each with specific populations, troops, and distances from Chang'an. Jibin, a large country not under the Western Region Protector, had a mild climate, produced various crops and metals, and had a market with gold and silver coins. The Han Dynasty's communication with Jibin began under Emperor Wu, but later conflicts arose, including the killing of Han envoys. Du Qin advised against further engagement due to the dangers and costs, and the Han Dynasty eventually limited contact. Wuyi Mountain, another large country, had similar customs to Jibin, with a hot climate and lush vegetation. Anxi Kingdom, a very large country with hundreds of cities, used silver coins and had a written language. Emperor Wu sent envoys to Parthia, who were greeted by a general with 20,000 cavalry. Dayuezhi, originally a nomadic country, was defeated by the Xiongnu and moved west to Daxia, establishing their capital. Daxia was divided into five tribes, each with its own marquis, all belonging to Dayuezhi. Kangju, with 120,000 households and 600,000 people, had customs similar to Dayuezhi and was restrained by the Xiongnu. During Emperor Xuan's reign, the Han Dynasty killed Zhizhi Chanyu. Under Emperor Cheng, King Kangju was arrogant, and the Protectorate recommended cutting ties, but the court maintained relations. Yancai, northwest of Kangju, had over 100,000 warriors and customs similar to Kangju. Dayuan, with 60,000 households and 300,000 people, produced good horses and used grapes for wine. Emperor Wu sent Li Guangli to attack Dayuan, resulting in the dedication of two Pegasus horses annually. From Dawan to Parthia, residents had different languages but similar customs, with deep-set eyes and long beards. They were skilled in business and obtained gold and silver from the Han Dynasty. After Huhanxie Chanyu submitted to the Han Dynasty, these countries respected the Han. Various other kingdoms like Taohua, Xiuxun, Zhendu, Shache, Shule, and Weitou had specific populations, troops, and distances, with some farming and raising livestock.

input_text: 乌孙国，大昆弥治赤谷城，去长安八千九百里。 户十二万，口六十三万，胜兵十八万八千八百人。 相，大禄，左右大将二人，侯三人，大将、都尉各一人，大监二人，大吏一人，舍中大吏二人，骑君一人。 东至都护治所千七百二十一里，西至康居蕃内地五千里。 地莽平。多雨，寒。 山多松樠。 不田作种树，随畜逐水草，与匈奴同俗。 国多马，富人至四五千匹。 民刚恶，贪狼无信，多寇盗，最为强国。 故服匈奴，后盛大，取羁属，不肯往朝会。 东与匈奴、西北与康居、西与大宛、南与城郭诸国相接。 本塞地也，大月氏西破走塞王，塞王南越县度。大月氏居其地。 后乌孙昆莫击破大月氏，大月氏徙西臣大夏，而乌孙昆莫居之，故乌孙民有塞种、大月氏种云。
target_text: The Wusun Kingdom, governed by Da Kunmi from Chigu City, was located 8,900 miles from Chang'an. It had 120,000 households, a population of 630,000, and an army of 188,800. The kingdom had a structured government with officials including a prime minister, generals, marquises, and eunuchs. The land was grassy, rainy, and cold, with residents practicing nomadic herding like the Xiongnu. The country was rich in horses, with wealthy individuals owning up to 4,000-5,000. The people were strong-willed but greedy and unfaithful. Wusun originally submitted to the Xiongnu but later became powerful and resisted them. It bordered the Xiongnu, Kangju, Dawan, and various Chengguo Kingdoms. The region was originally inhabited by the Sai people, then conquered by the Dayuezhi, and later by Wusun Kunmo, who incorporated both Sai and Dayuezhi populations.

input_text: 骞既致赐，谕指曰： 乌孙能东居故地，则汉遣公主为夫人，结为昆弟，共距匈奴，不足破也。 乌孙远汉，未知其大小，又近匈奴，服属日久，其大臣皆不欲徙。 昆莫年老国分，不能专制，乃发使送骞，因献马数十匹报谢。 其使见汉人众富厚，归其国，其国后乃益重汉。 匈奴闻其与汉通，怒欲击之。 又汉使乌孙，乃出其南，抵大宛、月氏，相属不绝。 乌孙于是恐，使使献马，愿得尚汉公主，为昆弟。 天子问群臣，议许，曰： 必先内聘，然后遣女。 乌孙以马千匹聘。 汉元封中，遣江都王建女细君为公主，以妻焉。赐乘舆服御物，为备官属宦官侍御数百人，赠送甚盛。 乌孙昆莫以为右夫人。 匈奴亦遣女妻昆莫，昆莫以为左夫人。 公主至其国，自治宫室居，岁时一再与昆莫会，置酒饮食，以币、帛赐王左右贵人。 昆莫年老，言语不通，公主悲愁，自为作歌曰： 吾家嫁我兮天一方，远托异国兮乌孙王。
target_text: Zhang Qian, sent by Emperor Wu of Han, attempted to persuade Wusun to return to their homeland and ally with Han against the Xiongnu. Kunmo initially treated Zhang Qian with Xiongnu-like arrogance but eventually showed respect. Wusun was divided among Kunmo's sons, with internal conflicts over succession. Despite Zhang Qian's efforts, Wusun was reluctant to move east due to distance and longstanding ties with the Xiongnu. However, after envoys saw Han's wealth, Wusun grew more respectful. The Xiongnu, angered by Wusun's contact with Han, threatened attack, leading Wusun to propose marriage to a Han princess. The Han agreed, and during the Yuanfeng period, Princess Xijun was sent to marry Kunmo. The Xiongnu also sent a bride, and Kunmo took both as wives. The princess, homesick and unable to communicate with the elderly Kunmo, composed a sorrowful song. Emperor Wu, pitying her, sent gifts regularly.

input_text: 广利责电兹曰： 外国皆臣属于汉，龟兹何以得受杅弥质？ 即将赖丹入至京师。 昭帝乃用桑弘羊前议，以杅弥太子赖丹为校尉，将军田轮台，轮台与渠犁地皆相连也。 龟兹贵人姑翼谓其王曰： 赖丹本臣属吾国，今佩汉印绶来，迫吾国而田，必为害。 王即杀赖丹，而上书谢汉，汉未能征。 宣帝时，长罗侯常惠使乌孙还，便宜发诸国兵，合五万人攻龟兹，责以前杀校尉赖丹。 龟兹王谢曰： 乃我先王时为贵人姑翼所误，我无罪。 执姑翼诣惠，惠斩之。 时乌孙公主遣女来至京师学鼓琴，汉遣侍郎乐奉送主女，过龟兹。 龟兹前遣人至乌孙求公主女，未还。 会女过龟兹，龟兹王留不遣，复使使报公主，主许之。 后公主上书，愿令女比宗室入朝，而龟兹王绛宾亦受其夫人，上书言得尚汉外孙为昆弟，愿与公主女俱入朝。 元康元年，遂来朝贺。王及夫人皆赐印绶。 夫人号称公主，赐以车骑旗鼓，歌吹数十人，绮绣杂缯琦珍凡数千万。 留且一年，厚赠送之。 后数来朝贺，乐汉衣服制度，归其国，治宫室，作檄道周卫，出入传呼，撞钟鼓，如汉家仪。外国胡人皆曰： 驴非驴，马非马，若龟兹王，所谓骡也。 绛宾死，其子丞德自谓汉外孙，成、哀帝时往来尤数，汉遇之亦甚亲密。
target_text: After Kunmo's death, his grandson Cen Zuo married the princess per Wusun custom, as Emperor Wu approved to maintain the alliance. Cen Zuo became king, and the princess bore a daughter. Upon her death, Princess Jieyou, granddaughter of a Han king, was sent to marry Cen Zuo. Cen Zuo's son by his Xiongnu wife was young, so the throne passed to his uncle's son, Weng Guimi, who married Jieyou and had three sons and two daughters. During Emperor Zhao's reign, Princess Jieyou sought Han aid against Xiongnu attacks. Emperor Xuan later sent a large force, including 150,000 Han cavalry and 50,000 Wusun troops, defeating the Xiongnu and capturing many people and livestock. Wusun took the spoils. Emperor Xuan rewarded Chang Hui, who had led the Wusun forces.

input_text: 汉遣惠持金币赐乌孙贵人有功者。 元康二年，乌孙昆弥因惠上书： 愿以汉外孙元贵靡为嗣，得令复尚汉公主，结婚重亲，畔绝匈奴，原聘马、骡各千匹。 诏下公卿议，大鸿胪萧望之以为： 乌孙绝域，变故难保，不可许。 上美乌孙新立大功，又重绝故业，遣使者至乌孙，先迎取聘。 昆弥及太子、左右大将、都尉皆遣使，凡三百余人，入汉迎取少主。 上乃以乌孙主解忧弟子相夫为公主，置官属侍御百余人，舍上林中，学乌孙言。 天子自临平乐观，会匈奴使者、外国君长大角抵，设乐而遣之。使长罗侯光禄大夫惠为副，凡持节者四人，送少主至郭煌。 未出塞，闻乌孙昆弥翁归靡死，乌孙贵人共从本约，立岑陬子泥靡代为昆靡，号狂王。 惠上书： 愿留少主郭煌，惠驰至乌孙责让不立元贵靡为昆靡，还迎少主。 事下公卿，望之复以为： 乌孙持两端，难约结。 前公主在乌孙四十余年，恩爱不亲密，边竟未得安，此已事已验也。 令少主以元贵靡不立而还，信无负于夷狄，中国之福也。 少主不止，徭役将兴，其原起此。 天子从之，征还少主。
target_text: Wusun Kunmi proposed making his Han-descended grandson Yuan Guimi heir, with a double marriage to sever ties with the Xiongnu. Emperor Xuan agreed but faced opposition from officials like Xiao Wangzhi, who doubted Wusun's reliability. Despite this, the emperor proceeded, sending a young princess to Wusun. However, Weng Guimi died before her arrival, and the throne passed to Nimi, Cen Zuo's son. Chang Hui advised keeping the princess in Dunhuang, and after debate, Emperor Xuan recalled her. Princess Jieyou remained in Wusun for over 40 years, and the mad king, who succeeded, was cruel and unpopular. A plot to kill him failed, leading to conflict. The Han intervened, executing those involved. Later, Wujiutu, a son of Weng Guimi, killed the mad king and declared himself Kunmi. The Han sent forces but ultimately negotiated, dividing Wusun into two Kunmi with separate households. Princess Jieyou, now elderly, was allowed to return to Chang'an, where she died two years later.

input_text: 校尉开门击鼓收吏士，良等随人，遂杀校尉刀护及子男四人、诸昆弟子男，独遗妇女小儿。 止留戊己校尉城，遣人与匈奴南将军相闻，南将军以二千骑迎良等。良等尽胁略戊己校尉吏士男女二千余人入匈奴。 单于以良、带为乌贲都尉。 后三岁，单于死，弟乌累单于咸立，复与莽和亲。 莽遣使者多赍金币赂单于，购求陈良、终带等。 单于尽收四人及手杀刀护者芝音妻子以下二十七人，皆械槛车付使者。 到长安，莽皆烧杀之。 其后莽复欺诈单于，和亲遂绝。 匈奴大击北边，而西域瓦解。 焉耆国近匈奴，先叛，杀都护但钦，莽不能讨。 天凤三年，乃遣五威将王骏、西域都护李崇将戊己校尉出西域，诸国皆郊迎，送兵谷，焉耆诈降而聚兵自备。 骏等将莎车、龟慈兵七千余人，分为数部入焉耆，焉耆伏兵要遮骏。及姑墨、尉犁、危须国兵为反间，还共袭击骏等，皆杀之。 唯戊己校尉郭钦别将兵，后至焉耆。 焉耆兵未还，钦击杀其老弱，引兵还。 莽封钦为剼胡子。 李崇收余士，还保龟兹。 数年莽死，崇遂没，西域因绝。
target_text: The text also details various other kingdoms in the Western Regions, including Gumo, Wensu, Qiuci, and others, with their distances from Chang'an, populations, armies, and administrative structures. It describes the Han Dynasty's efforts to establish agricultural colonies, such as in Luntai, and the challenges of maintaining control over distant territories. Emperor Wu's later years saw a shift away from expansion, with a focus on domestic recovery and reduced military campaigns. The narrative covers conflicts with the Xiongnu, internal rebellions, and the eventual decline of Han influence in the region, culminating in the collapse of the Western Regions Protectorate during Wang Mang's reign. The summary concludes with a reflection on the costs and benefits of Han's Western Regions policy, noting that while the region offered exotic goods, it also drained resources and led to instability.

input_text: 谷永字子云，长安人也。 父吉，为卫司马，使送郅支单于侍子，为郅支所杀，语在《陈汤传》。 永少为长安小史，后博学经书。 建昭中，御史大夫繁延寿闻其有茂材，除补属，举为太常丞，数上疏言得失。 建始三年冬，日食、地震同日俱发，诏举方正直言极谏之士，太常阳城侯刘庆忌举永待诏公车。 对曰： 陛下秉至圣之纯德，惧天地之戒异，饬身修政，纳问公卿，又下明诏，帅举直言，燕见绎，以求咎愆，使臣等得造明朝，承圣问。 臣材朽学浅，不通政事。
target_text: Gu Yong, styled Ziyun, was from Chang'an. His father, Gu Ji, served as a Sima of the Wei Dynasty and was killed by Shanyu Zhizhi while on a diplomatic mission. Gu Yong wrote a short history of Chang'an in his youth and later extensively studied the classics. During Emperor Jianzhao's reign, Fan Yanshou, the imperial censor, recognized his talents and appointed him as a subordinate, later recommending him as Taichang Cheng. Gu Yong wrote many memorials discussing political gains and losses.

input_text: 谷永字子云，长安人也。 父吉，为卫司马，使送郅支单于侍子，为郅支所杀，语在《陈汤传》。 永少为长安小史，后博学经书。 建昭中，御史大夫繁延寿闻其有茂材，除补属，举为太常丞，数上疏言得失。 建始三年冬，日食、地震同日俱发，诏举方正直言极谏之士，太常阳城侯刘庆忌举永待诏公车。 对曰： 陛下秉至圣之纯德，惧天地之戒异，饬身修政，纳问公卿，又下明诏，帅举直言，燕见绎，以求咎愆，使臣等得造明朝，承圣问。 臣材朽学浅，不通政事。
target_text: In the winter of the third year of Jianshi's reign, a solar eclipse and earthquake occurred on the same day. The emperor ordered the selection of upright scholars who dared to speak out. Tai Chang Yangcheng Marquis Liu Qingji recommended Gu Yong to await the imperial edict. Gu Yong replied that the emperor, with his pure moral character, was worried about the strange phenomena and sought advice. He stated that when a sage emperor ascends the throne, he must correct his appearance, speech, sight, hearing, and thinking, and establish imperial rules to obey the will of the Emperor of Heaven. If the king indulges in the harem, pleasure, and hunting, disasters will appear. The solar eclipse and earthquake were signs of faults, and the emperor should look for reasons within himself, possibly due to excessive attention to women, lack of political concern, or improper behavior.

input_text: 窃闻明王即位，正五事，建大中，以承天心，则庶征序于下，日月理于上；如人君淫溺后宫，船乐游田，五事失于躬，大中之道不立，则咎征降而六极至。 凡灾异之发，各象过失，以类告人。 乃十二月朔戊申，日食婺女之分，地震萧墙之内，二者同日俱发，以丁宁陛下，厥咎不远，宜厚求诸身。 意岂陛下志在闺门，未恤政事，不慎举错，娄失中与？ 内宠大盛，女不遵道，嫉妨专上，妨继嗣与？ 古之王者废五事之中，失夫妇之纪，妻妾得意，谒行于内，势行于外，至覆倾国家，或乱阴阳。 昔褒姒用国，宗周以丧；阎妻骄扇，日以不臧。 此其效也。
target_text: Gu Yong cited historical examples: Guo Si caused Zong Zhou's downfall, and Yan's wife's arrogance led to a solar eclipse. He emphasized that the relationship between husband and wife is crucial for national safety. He advised regulating the harem, clarifying superiority and inferiority, and preventing jealousy and arrogance. He urged the emperor to correct himself, reduce private banquets, stop excessive pleasures, and follow etiquette and law. He also stressed the importance of selecting virtuous officials, assessing their merits, and avoiding favoritism. He warned that disasters are warnings from heaven, and if ignored, punishments will increase.

input_text: 其夏，皆令诸方正对策，语在《杜钦传》。 永对毕，因曰： 臣前幸得条对灾异之效，祸乱所极，言关于圣聪。 书陈于前，陛下委弃不纳，而更使方正对策，背可惧之大异，问不急之常论，废承天之至言，角无用之虚文，欲末杀灾异，满谰诬天，是故皇天勃然发怒，甲己之间暴风三溱，拔树折木，此天至明不可欺之效也。 上特复问永，永对曰： 日食、地震，皇后、贵妾专宠所致。 语在《五行志》。 是时，上初即位，谦让委政元舅大将军王凤，议者多归咎焉。 永知凤方见柄用，阴欲自托，乃复曰： 方今四夷宾服，皆为臣妾，北无薰粥冒顿之患，南无赵佗、吕嘉之难，三垂晏然，靡有兵革之警。 诸侯大者乃食数县，汉吏制其权柄，不得有为，亡吴、楚、燕、梁之势。 百官盘互，亲疏相错，骨肉大臣有申伯之忠，洞洞属属，小心畏忌，无重合、安阳、博陆之乱。
target_text: The emperor was surprised by Gu Yong's countermeasures and summoned him. Gu Yong continued, stating that the solar eclipse and earthquake were caused by the exclusive favor of the queen's concubine. He knew that General Wang Feng had just gained power and secretly wanted to rely on him. He argued that the borders were stable, the princes had limited power, and officials were loyal, so the disasters could not be blamed on the uncles. He advised the emperor to understand the warnings, change past mistakes, eliminate biased favor, and ensure all concubines served in turn to secure descendants and end disasters.

input_text: 时，对者数十人，永与杜钦为上第焉。 上皆以其书示后宫。 后上尝赐许皇后书，采永言以责之，语在《外戚传》。 永既阴为大将军凤说矣，能实最高，由是擢为光禄大夫。 永奏书谢凤曰： 永斗筲之材，质薄学朽，无一日之雅，左右之介，将军说其狂言，擢之皂衣之吏，厕之争臣之末，不听浸润之谮，不食肤受之诉，虽齐桓、晋文用士笃密，察父哲兄覆育子弟，诚无以加！ 昔豫子吞炭坏形以奉见异，齐客陨首公门以报恩施，知氏、孟尝犹有死士，何况将军之门！ 凤遂厚之。 数年，出为安定太守。 时，上诸舅皆修经书，任政事。 平阿侯谭年次当继大将军凤辅政，尤与永善。 阳朔中，凤薨。 凤病困，荐从弟御史大夫音以自代。 上从之，以音为大司马车骑将军，领尚书事，而平阿侯谭位特进，领城门兵。 永闻之，与谭书曰： 君侯躬周、召之德，执管、晏之操，敬贤下士，乐善不倦，宜在上将久矣，以大将军在，故抑郁于家，不得舒愤。
target_text: Gu Yong was promoted to Doctor Guanglu. He wrote to thank Wang Feng, praising his support. Later, when Wang Feng died, Wang Yin succeeded him. Gu Yong advised Wang Tan to resign from leading the city gate soldiers, which Wang Tan did, causing a rift with Wang Yin. Gu Yong then advised Wang Yin to work diligently, punish evildoers, and promote virtuous people. He warned about celestial signs like Taibai and Yinghuo, urging Wang Yin to change his ways to comply with God's will.

input_text: 时，对者数十人，永与杜钦为上第焉。 上皆以其书示后宫。 后上尝赐许皇后书，采永言以责之，语在《外戚传》。 永既阴为大将军凤说矣，能实最高，由是擢为光禄大夫。 永奏书谢凤曰： 永斗筲之材，质薄学朽，无一日之雅，左右之介，将军说其狂言，擢之皂衣之吏，厕之争臣之末，不听浸润之谮，不食肤受之诉，虽齐桓、晋文用士笃密，察父哲兄覆育子弟，诚无以加！ 昔豫子吞炭坏形以奉见异，齐客陨首公门以报恩施，知氏、孟尝犹有死士，何况将军之门！ 凤遂厚之。 数年，出为安定太守。 时，上诸舅皆修经书，任政事。 平阿侯谭年次当继大将军凤辅政，尤与永善。 阳朔中，凤薨。 凤病困，荐从弟御史大夫音以自代。 上从之，以音为大司马车骑将军，领尚书事，而平阿侯谭位特进，领城门兵。 永闻之，与谭书曰： 君侯躬周、召之德，执管、晏之操，敬贤下士，乐善不倦，宜在上将久矣，以大将军在，故抑郁于家，不得舒愤。
target_text: When a black dragon appeared, Gu Yong explained it as a sign of the same surname, possibly indicating a threat from a relative or a cruel successor. He warned about the dangers of women and evil people in power, citing historical examples. He criticized the emperor for indulging in private pleasures, neglecting duties, and causing disasters. He urged the emperor to reform, reduce taxes, stop excessive construction, and care for the people. The emperor was moved but did not fully trust Gu Yong.

input_text: 对奏，天子甚感其言。 永于经书，泛为疏达，与杜钦、杜邺略等，不能洽浃如刘向父子及扬雄也。 其于天官、《京氏易》最密，故善言灾异，前后所上四十余事，略相反复，专攻上身与后宫而已。 党于王氏，上亦知之，不甚亲信也。 永所居任职，为北地太守岁余，卫将军商薨，曲阳侯根为票骑将军，荐永，征入为大司农。 岁余，永病，三月，有司奏请免。 故事，公卿病，辄赐告，至永独即时免。 数月，卒于家。 本名并，以尉氏樊并反，更名永云。 杜邺字子夏，本魏郡繁阳人也。 祖父及父积功劳皆至郡守，武帝时徙茂陵。 邺少孤，其母张敞女。 邺。邺壮，从敞子吉学问，得其家书。 以孝廉以郎。 与车骑将军王音善。 平阿侯谭不受城门职，后薨，上闵悔之，乃复令谭弟成都侯商位特进，领城门兵，得举吏如将军府。
target_text: Gu Yong served as governor of the North and later died at home. He was proficient in Tianguan and "Jingshi Yi," and his memorials focused on the lord and the harem. Du Ye, styled Zixia, was from Fanyang and studied with Zhang Ji. He was friendly with Wang Yin and advised him to cooperate with Wang Shang. Du Ye later served as governor of Liangzhou but was dismissed due to illness. During Emperor Ai's reign, he criticized the influence of the Fu and Ding families, warning about solar eclipses and earthquakes as signs of imbalance. He urged the emperor to follow ancient laws and satisfy the people's wishes. Du Ye died without an official title.

input_text: 其正文字过于邺、竦，故世言小学者由杜公。 赞曰：孝成之世，委政外家，诸舅持权，重于丁、傅在孝哀时。 故杜邺敢讥丁、傅，而钦、永不敢言王氏，其势然也。 及钦欲挹损凤权，而邺附会音、商。 永陈三七之戒，斯为忠焉，至其引申伯以阿凤，隙平阿于车骑，指金、火以求合，可谓谅不足而谈有余者。 孔子称 友多闻 ，三人近之矣。
target_text: The commentary notes that during Emperor Xiaocheng's era, power was with relatives, while during Emperor Xiaoai's era, the Fu and Ding families held power. Du Ye dared to accuse the Ding and Fu families, but Gu Yong avoided criticizing the Wang family due to circumstances. Gu Yong's loyalty was shown in his warnings, but he also flattered Wang Feng and alienated others, lacking integrity but excelling in rhetoric.

input_text: 昔先王之制，自天子、公、侯、卿、大夫、士至于皂隶、抱关、击者，其爵禄、奉养、宫室、车服、棺椁、祭祀、死生之制各有差品，小不得僣大，贱不得逾贵。 夫然，故上下序而民志定。 于是辩其土地、川泽、丘陵、衍沃、原隰之宜，教民种树畜养；五谷六畜及至鱼鳖、鸟兽、雚蒲、材干、器械之资，所以养生送终之具，靡不皆育。 然后四民因其土宜，各任智力，夙兴夜寐，以治其业，相与通功易事，交利而俱赡，非有征发期会，而远近咸足。 故《易》曰 后以财成辅相天地之宜，以左右民 ， 备物致用，立成器以为天下利，莫大乎圣人 。
target_text: The ancient system of kings established hierarchical distinctions from emperor to slave, with graded official titles, salaries, and life-and-death rites, ensuring that the lowly did not surpass the noble, thus stabilizing society. People were taught to cultivate land and raise livestock according to seasonal and geographical conditions, with strict rules against cutting trees or fishing before the first lunar month, and prohibitions on harvesting immature plants, animals, or eggs to allow natural reproduction and abundant reserves. Scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants each specialized in their occupations, exchanging goods to meet needs without excessive taxation, as noted in the "Book of Changes" and "Guanzi," which emphasized that people content with their professions and customs would have few desires and ample property, guided by morality and ritual.

input_text: 此之谓也《管子》云古之四民不得杂处。 士相与言仁谊于闲宴，工相与议技巧于官府，商相与语财利于市井，农相与谋稼穑于田野，朝夕从事，不见异物而迁焉。 故其父兄之教不肃而成，子弟之学不劳而能，各安其居而乐其业，甘其食而美其服，虽见奇丽纷华，非其所习，辟犹戎翟之与于越，不相入矣。 是以欲寡而事节，财足而不争。 于是在民上者，道之以德，齐之以礼，故民有耻而且敬，贵谊而贱利。 此三代之所以直道而行，不严而治之大略也。 及周室衰，礼法堕，诸侯刻桷丹楹，大夫山节藻棁，八佾舞于庭，《雍》彻于堂。 其流至乎士庶人，莫不离制而弃本，稼穑之民少，商旅之民多，谷不足而货有余。陵夷至乎桓、文之后，礼谊大坏，上下相冒，国异政，家殊俗，嗜欲不制，僣差亡极。 于是商通难得之货，工作亡用之器，士设反道之行，以追时好而取世资。 伪民背实而要名，奸夫犯害而求利，篡弑取国者为王公，圉夺成家者为雄桀。 礼谊不足以拘君子，刑戮不足以威小人。 富者木土被文锦，犬马余肉粟，而贫者短褐不完，含菽饮水。 其为编户齐民，同列而以财力相君，虽为仆虏，犹亡愠色。
target_text: The decline began when the Zhou royal family weakened and etiquette collapsed, exemplified by Duke Zhuang of Lu violating Zhou rites by carving and painting his father's temple, and other officials like Zang Wenzhong and the three Huan families of Lu exceeding their ranks in music and sacrifices. This spread to commoners, who abandoned farming for commerce, leading to food shortages and luxury excess. After the reigns of Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin, ritual and righteousness were destroyed, superiors and subordinates offended each other, and deceitful, treacherous, and murderous individuals gained wealth and status. The rich decorated homes with silk and fed dogs and horses grain, while the poor wore coarse cloth and ate beans, yet the poor did not resent their status. Those who followed justice faced hunger, while the wicked prospered, all stemming from the destruction of the legal system.

input_text: 故夫饰变诈为奸轨者，自足乎一世之间；守道循理者，不免于饥寒之患。 其教自上兴，由法度之无限也。 故列其行事，以传世变云。 昔粤王勾践困于会稽之上，乃用荡蠡、计然。 计然曰： 知斗则修备，时用则知物，二者形则万货之情可得见矣。 故旱则资舟，水则资车，物之理也。 推此类而修之，十年国富，厚赂战士，遂报强吴，刷会稽之耻。 范蠡叹曰： 计然之策，十用其五而得意。 既以施国，吾欲施之家。 乃乘扁舟，浮江湖，变名姓，适齐为鸱夷子皮，之陶为朱公。
target_text: In response, King Gou Jian of Yue, besieged on Kuaiji Mountain, appointed Fan Li and Ji Ran to govern. Ji Ran advised buying ships during droughts and vehicles during floods to prepare for opposite conditions, understanding market cycles. Yue followed this policy, became wealthy, and avenged Wu. Fan Li later applied these principles to enrich his family, changing his name to Zhu Gong in Taoyi, a central trading hub. He hoarded goods, adapted to circumstances, and lent money wisely, amassing a fortune three times over 19 years, distributing wealth to the poor, and leaving a legacy that made "Duke Tao Zhu" synonymous with riches.

input_text: 当魏文侯时，李史务尽地力，而白圭乐观时变，故人弃我取，人取我予。 能薄饮食，忍嗜欲，节衣服，与用事僮仆同苦乐，趋时若猛兽挚鸟之发。 故曰： 吾治生犹伊尹、吕尚之谋，孙、吴用兵，商鞅行法是也。 故智不足与权变，勇不足以决断，仁不能以取予，强不能以有守，虽欲学吾术，终不告也。 盖天下言治生者祖白圭。 猗顿用盬盐起，邯郸郭纵以铸冶成业，与王者埒富。 乌氏蠃畜牧，及众，斥卖，求奇缯物，间献戎王。 戎王十倍其偿，予畜，畜至用谷量牛马。 秦始皇令蠃比封君，以时与列臣朝请。
target_text: Other wealthy figures included Zi Gong, a disciple of Confucius who traded between Cao and Wei, becoming richer than Yan Yuan, though Confucius praised Yan's wisdom. Bai Gui of Zhou, during Wei Wenhou's time, observed market price changes, advocating buying when others sold and vice versa. He lived frugally, shared hardships with servants, and seized opportunities swiftly, comparing his methods to Yi Yin, Sun Tzu, and Shang Yang. He taught only those who were intelligent, brave, benevolent, and strong. Yidun made a fortune from salt, Guo Zong from iron, and Wu Shiying from livestock, who bribed the Rong King and became so wealthy that Qin Shihuang honored him. The widow Qing of Ba preserved her family's cinnabar mine, and Qin Shihuang built a platform for her as a chaste woman.

input_text: 巴寡妇清，其先得丹穴，而擅其利数世，家亦不訾。 清寡妇能守其业，用财自卫，人不敢犯。 始皇以为贞妇而客之，为筑女怀清台。 秦汉之制，列侯封君食租税，岁率户二百。 千户之君则二十万，朝觐聘享出其中。 庶民农工商贾，率亦岁万息二千，百万之家即二十万，而更徭租赋出其中，衣食好美矣。 故曰陆地牧马二百蹄，牛千蹄角，千足羊，泽中千足彘，水居千石鱼波，山居千章之萩。 安邑千树枣；燕、秦千树栗；蜀、汉、江陵千树橘；淮北荥南河济之间千树萩；陈、夏千亩漆；齐、鲁千亩桑麻；渭川千亩竹；及名国万家之城，带郭千亩亩钟之田，若千亩卮茜，千畦姜韭：此其人皆与千户侯等。
target_text: Under Qin and Han systems, a prince with a thousand households earned 200,000 yuan annually from rents, while commoners with 10,000 yuan could earn 2,000 yuan in interest. Wealthy families raised livestock, planted trees, or cultivated crops like jujubes, chestnuts, oranges, lacquer, mulberries, bamboo, or ginger, matching the income of a thousand-household prince. The proverb said that for a poor man to get rich, commerce was better than farming or crafts. In a bustling city, annual sales of wine, vinegar, grain, livestock, timber, and other goods could yield profits comparable to a prince's income.

input_text: 齐俗贱奴虏，而刀间独爱贵之。 桀黠奴，人之所患，唯刀间收取，使之逐鱼盐商贾之利，或连车骑交守相，然愈益任之，终得其力，起数千万。 故曰 宁爵无刀 ，言能使豪奴自饶，而尽其力也。 刀间既衰，至成、哀间，临淄姓伟訾五千万。 周人既孅，而师史尤甚，转毂百数，贾郡国，无所不至。 雒阳街居在齐、秦、楚、赵之中，富家相矜以久贾，过邑不入门。 设用此等，故师史能致十千万。 师史既衰，至成、哀、王莽时，雒阳张长叔、薛子促訾亦十千万。 莽皆以为纳言士，欲法武帝，然不能得其利。 宣曲任氏，其先为督道仓吏。
target_text: The Zhuo family of Shu, exiled from Zhao, chose fertile land at Marriage Mountain, mined iron, and traded with Yunnan and Shu, amassing wealth with 800 servants. Cheng Zheng, a captive, also prospered in iron. Later, Luo Pei of Chengdu, trusted by the Shi family, made millions in Ba, Shu, and the capital, bribing nobles to monopolize well salt. The Kong family of Wan, exiled to Nanyang, combined iron smelting with farming and trade, earning a reputation for generosity. The Bing family of Lu, frugal and meticulous, made millions from iron, influencing many to abandon literature for commerce. Dao Xian of Qi valued cunning slaves, using them to trade fish and salt, accumulating tens of millions. After his decline, Wei of Linzi had 50 million. Shishi of Zhou, with hundreds of carts, traded across counties, making 100 million, followed by Zhang Changshu and Xue Zizhong under Wang Mang.

input_text: 秦之败也，豪桀争取金玉，任氏独窖仓粟。 楚、汉相距荥阳，民不得耕种，米石至万，而豪桀金玉尽归任氏，任氏以此起富。 富人奢侈，而任氏折节为力田畜。 人争取贱贾，任氏独取贵善，富者数世。 然任公家约，非田畜所生不衣食，公事不毕则不得饮酒食肉。 以此为闾里率，故富而主上重之。 塞之斥也，唯桥桃以致马千匹，牛倍之，羊万，粟以万钟计。 吴、楚兵之起，长安中列侯封君行从军旅，赍貣子钱家，子钱家以为关东成败未决，莫肯予。 唯毋盐氏出捐千金贷，其息十之。 三月，吴、楚平。 一岁之中，则毋盐氏息十倍，用此富关中。
target_text: The Ren family of Xuanqu stored grain during Qin's fall, profiting when war drove prices to 10,000 yuan per stone. They focused on farmland and livestock, eating only what they produced, and became a model village, respected by the emperor. During the Seven Kingdoms' rebellion, Wuyan family lent money at tenfold interest, earning a fortune in Guanzhong. Other wealthy families included the Tian clan, Fan Jia, Zhi Gang, and Wang Junfang, with Fan Jia having 50 million. Countless others gained wealth through patents, bribery, or illegal means like tomb robbing and gambling, corrupting society and leading to chaos.

input_text: 贾谊，雒阳人也，年十八，以能诵诗书属文称于郡中。 河南守吴公闻其秀材，召置门下，甚幸爱。 文帝初立，闻河南守吴公治平为天下第一，故与李斯同邑，而尝学事焉，征以为廷尉。 廷尉乃言谊年少，颇通诸家之书。 文帝召以为博士。 是时，谊年二十余，最为少。 每诏令议下，诸老先生未能言，谊尽为之对，人人各如其意所出。诸生于是以为能。 文帝说之，超迁，岁中至太中大夫。 谊以为汉兴二十余年，天下和洽，宜当改正朔，易服色制度，定官名，兴礼乐。 乃草具其仪法，色上黄，数用五，为官名悉更，奏之。 文帝廉让未皇也。 然诸法令所更定，及列侯就国，其说皆谊发之。 于是天子议以谊任公卿之位。 绛、灌、东阳侯、冯敬之属尽害之，乃毁谊曰： 雒阳之人年少初学，专欲擅权，纷乱诸事。 于是天子后亦疏之，不用其议，以谊为长沙王太傅。 谊既以適去，意不自得，及渡湘水，为赋以吊屈原。 屈原，楚贤臣也，被谗放逐，作《离骚赋》，其终篇曰： 已矣！
target_text: Jia Yi, a native of Luoyang, was renowned for his literary talents at eighteen. Governor Wu Gong of Henan summoned him after hearing of his abilities. When Emperor Wen of Han ascended the throne, he appointed Wu Gong as a court captain due to his excellent governance and connection to Li Si. Wu Gong recommended Jia Yi, who was then made a doctor at around twenty years old, the youngest among them. Jia Yi excelled in court discussions, impressing the emperor, who promoted him to Taizhong doctor within a year. Jia Yi proposed reforming the calendar, legal system, and rituals, drafting regulations with yellow as the noble color and a five-character seal. Emperor Wen hesitated to implement these changes, but many legal reforms and the relocation of princes were Jia Yi's ideas.

input_text: 贾谊，雒阳人也，年十八，以能诵诗书属文称于郡中。 河南守吴公闻其秀材，召置门下，甚幸爱。 文帝初立，闻河南守吴公治平为天下第一，故与李斯同邑，而尝学事焉，征以为廷尉。 廷尉乃言谊年少，颇通诸家之书。 文帝召以为博士。 是时，谊年二十余，最为少。 每诏令议下，诸老先生未能言，谊尽为之对，人人各如其意所出。诸生于是以为能。 文帝说之，超迁，岁中至太中大夫。 谊以为汉兴二十余年，天下和洽，宜当改正朔，易服色制度，定官名，兴礼乐。 乃草具其仪法，色上黄，数用五，为官名悉更，奏之。 文帝廉让未皇也。 然诸法令所更定，及列侯就国，其说皆谊发之。 于是天子议以谊任公卿之位。 绛、灌、东阳侯、冯敬之属尽害之，乃毁谊曰： 雒阳之人年少初学，专欲擅权，纷乱诸事。 于是天子后亦疏之，不用其议，以谊为长沙王太傅。 谊既以適去，意不自得，及渡湘水，为赋以吊屈原。 屈原，楚贤臣也，被谗放逐，作《离骚赋》，其终篇曰： 已矣！
target_text: Jealous officials slandered Jia Yi, leading to his demotion as Tutor to the Prince of Changsha. On his journey, he wrote a poem mourning Qu Yuan, comparing their fates. The poem lamented Qu Yuan's unjust exile and suicide, criticizing a world that values the worthless over the worthy. Jia Yi advised retreat and self-preservation, using metaphors of dragons and phoenixes to urge distancing from corruption. He argued that Qu Yuan should have sought a wise ruler rather than cling to Chu.

input_text: 凤缥缥其高逝兮，夫固自引而远去。 袭九渊之神龙兮，沕渊潜以自珍；偭蟂獭以隐处兮，夫岂从虾与蛭螾？ 所贵圣之神德兮，远浊世而自臧。 使骐骥可系而羁兮，岂云异夫犬羊？ 般纷纷其离此邮兮，亦夫子之故也！ 历九州而相其君兮，何必怀此都也？ 凤皇翔于千仞兮，览德煇而下之；见细德之险征兮，遥增击而去之。 彼寻常之污渎佤，岂容吞舟之鱼！ 横江湖之鳣鲸兮，固将制于蝼蚁。 谊为长沙傅三年，有服飞入谊舍，止于坐隅。 服似鸮，不祥鸟也。 谊既以適居长沙，长沙卑湿，谊自伤悼，以为寿不得长，乃为赋以自广。 其辞曰：
target_text: In his third year in Changsha, an owl, an unlucky bird, entered Jia Yi's room. He wrote a poem exploring fate and fortune, reflecting on the cyclical nature of life and the futility of human concerns. The poem discusses the interplay of fortune and misfortune, using examples like Li Si and Fu Yue to illustrate unpredictability. It advocates detachment from worldly desires, embracing the Dao, and accepting life's transience. Jia Yi concluded that the owl's omen was trivial.

input_text: 后岁余，文帝思谊，征之。 至，入见，上方受厘，坐宣室。 上因感鬼神事，而问鬼神之本。 谊具道所以然之故。 至夜半，文帝前席。 既罢，曰： 吾久不见贾生，自以为过之，今不及也。 乃拜谊为梁怀王太傅。 怀王，上少子，爱，而好书，故令谊傅之，数问以得失。 是时，匈奴强，侵边。 天下初定，制度疏阔。 诸侯王僣拟，地过古制，淮南、济北王皆为逆诛。 谊数上疏陈政事，多所欲匡建，其大略曰： 臣窃惟事势，可为痛哭者一，可为流涕者二，可为长太息者六，若其它背理而伤道者，难遍以疏举。
target_text: Emperor Wen later recalled Jia Yi, discussing ghosts and gods late into the night. Impressed, he appointed Jia Yi as Tutor to his favored son, King Huai of Liang. Jia Yi frequently advised on state affairs, highlighting crises: the Xiongnu threat, rebellious princes, and corrupt customs. He argued that the realm was not truly peaceful, comparing it to sleeping on a pyre. He proposed dividing large fiefdoms to weaken princes, using historical examples to show that power leads to rebellion. He urged the emperor to adopt a system of smaller states to ensure stability, warning that inaction would lead to disaster.

input_text: 后岁余，文帝思谊，征之。 至，入见，上方受厘，坐宣室。 上因感鬼神事，而问鬼神之本。 谊具道所以然之故。 至夜半，文帝前席。 既罢，曰： 吾久不见贾生，自以为过之，今不及也。 乃拜谊为梁怀王太傅。 怀王，上少子，爱，而好书，故令谊傅之，数问以得失。 是时，匈奴强，侵边。 天下初定，制度疏阔。 诸侯王僣拟，地过古制，淮南、济北王皆为逆诛。 谊数上疏陈政事，多所欲匡建，其大略曰： 臣窃惟事势，可为痛哭者一，可为流涕者二，可为长太息者六，若其它背理而伤道者，难遍以疏举。
target_text: Jia Yi criticized the Xiongnu policy of appeasement, calling it humiliating and ineffective. He offered to subdue them through strategy. He also condemned lavish dress among commoners, which drained resources and undermined social hierarchy. He lamented the decline of moral standards, tracing it to Qin's abandonment of propriety. He advocated for early education of the crown prince, citing the long reigns of Xia, Shang, and Zhou, which prioritized ritual and moral instruction, unlike Qin's harsh laws that led to rapid collapse.

input_text: 文帝于是从谊计，乃徙淮阳王武为梁王，北界泰山，西至高阳，得大县四十余城；徙城阳王喜为淮南王，抚其民。 时又封淮南厉王四子皆为列侯。 谊知上必将复王之也，上疏谏曰： 窃恐陛下接王淮南诸子，曾不与如臣者孰计之也。 淮南王之悖逆亡道，天下孰不知其罪？ 陛下幸而赦迁之，自疾而死，天下孰以王死之不当？ 今奉尊罪人之子，适足以负谤于天下耳。 此人少壮，岂能忘其父哉 白公胜所为父报仇者，大父与伯父、叔父也。 白公为乱，非欲取国代主也，发愤快志，剡手以冲仇人之匈，固为俱靡而已。 淮南虽小，黥布尝用之矣，汉存特幸耳。 夫擅仇人足以危汉之资，于策不便。 虽割而为四，四子一心也。 予之众，积之财，此非有子胥、白公报于广都之中，即疑有剸诸、荆轲起于两柱之间，所谓假贼兵为虎翼者也。 愿陛下少留计！
target_text: Jia Yi emphasized the importance of ritual over punishment, arguing that ritual prevents wrongdoing subtly, while punishment only reacts. He urged the emperor to respect ministers, using historical examples to show that honor fosters loyalty. He advised against humiliating officials, as it erodes their integrity. He used the case of Zhou Bo, falsely accused of treason, to argue for leniency. Emperor Wen heeded this, and thereafter, guilty ministers committed suicide rather than face execution.

input_text: 文帝于是从谊计，乃徙淮阳王武为梁王，北界泰山，西至高阳，得大县四十余城；徙城阳王喜为淮南王，抚其民。 时又封淮南厉王四子皆为列侯。 谊知上必将复王之也，上疏谏曰： 窃恐陛下接王淮南诸子，曾不与如臣者孰计之也。 淮南王之悖逆亡道，天下孰不知其罪？ 陛下幸而赦迁之，自疾而死，天下孰以王死之不当？ 今奉尊罪人之子，适足以负谤于天下耳。 此人少壮，岂能忘其父哉 白公胜所为父报仇者，大父与伯父、叔父也。 白公为乱，非欲取国代主也，发愤快志，剡手以冲仇人之匈，固为俱靡而已。 淮南虽小，黥布尝用之矣，汉存特幸耳。 夫擅仇人足以危汉之资，于策不便。 虽割而为四，四子一心也。 予之众，积之财，此非有子胥、白公报于广都之中，即疑有剸诸、荆轲起于两柱之间，所谓假贼兵为虎翼者也。 愿陛下少留计！
target_text: Jia Yi later proposed strengthening the kingdoms of Huaiyang and Liang to counter powerful princes like Huainan. He warned against granting titles to the sons of the rebellious King Li of Huainan, predicting they would seek revenge. Emperor Wen partially adopted his advice, appointing Liu Wu as King of Liang. After Jia Yi's death at thirty-three, his predictions came true: the Seven Kingdoms rebelled, but Liang's strength helped suppress them. Emperor Wu later executed some of King Li's sons for rebellion.

input_text: 梁王胜坠马死，谊自伤为傅无状，常哭泣，后岁余，亦死。 贾生之死，年三十三矣。 后四岁，齐文王薨，亡子。 文帝思贾生之言，乃分齐为六国，尽立悼惠王子六人为王；又迁淮南王喜于城阳，而分淮南为三国，尽立厉王三子以王之。 后十年，文帝崩，景帝立；三年而吴、楚、赵与四齐王合从举兵，西乡京师，梁王扞之，卒破七国。 至武帝时，淮南厉王子为王者两国亦反诛。 孝武初立，举贾生之孙二人至郡守。 贾嘉最好学，世其家。 赞曰：刘向称 贾谊言三代与秦治乱之意，其论甚美，通达国体，虽古之伊、管未能远过也。 使时见用，功化必盛。 为庸臣所害，甚可悼痛。
target_text: The historian praised Jia Yi's insights on governance, comparing him to Yi Yin and Guan Zhong. Though his ideas were only partially implemented, his writings on statecraft were influential. His early death prevented him from reaching high office, but his legacy endured through his fifty-eight essays.

input_text: 贾山，颍川人也。 祖父祛，故魏王时博士弟子也。 山受学祛，所言涉猎书记，不能为醇儒。 尝给事颍阴侯为骑。 孝文时，言治乱之道，借秦为谕，名曰《至言》。 其辞曰：臣闻为人臣者，尽忠竭愚，以直谏主，不避死亡之诛者，臣山是也。 臣不敢以久远谕，愿借秦以为谕，唯陛下少加意焉。 夫布衣韦带之士，修身于内，成名于外，而使后世不绝息。 至秦则不然。贵为天子，富有天下，赋敛重数，百姓任罢，赭衣半道，群盗满山，使天下之人戴目而视，倾耳而听。 一夫大呼，天下响应者，陈胜是也。 秦非徒如此也，起咸阳而西至雍，离宫三百，钟鼓帷帐，不移而具。
target_text: Jia Shan, from Yingchuan, studied under his grandfather Jia Qu and was known for his broad knowledge across various schools of thought, though he did not specialize in Confucianism. He served as a riding attendant under Marquis Yingyin. During Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Jia Shan used the Qin Dynasty as a cautionary example to discuss governance, titling his work "Zhi Yan." He criticized Qin's tyranny, excessive construction of palaces like Epang, extravagant roads, and the lavish Lishan Mausoleum, which drained resources and oppressed the people, leading to widespread rebellion. He emphasized the importance of loyal ministers and open communication, warning that rulers who suppress criticism and act tyrannically risk losing their realm. Jia Shan urged the emperor to adopt benevolent policies, listen to advice, and avoid Qin's mistakes.

input_text: 其后，文帝除铸钱令，山复上书谏，以为变先帝法，非是。 又讼淮南王无大罪，宜急令反国。 又言柴唐子为不善，足以戒。 章下诘责，对以为： 钱者，亡用器也，而可以易富贵。 富贵者，人主之操柄也，令民为之，是与人主共操柄，不可长也。 其言多激切，善指事意，然终不加罚，所以广谏争之路也。 其后复禁铸钱云。邹阳，齐人也。 汉兴，诸侯王皆自治民聘贤。 吴王濞招致四方游士，阳与吴严忌、枚乘等俱仕吴，皆以文辩著名。 久之，吴王以太子事怨望，称疾不朝，阴有邪谋，阳奏书谏。 为其事尚隐，恶指斥言，故先引秦为谕，因道胡、越、齐、赵、淮南之难，然后乃致其意。 其辞曰： 臣闻秦倚曲台之官，悬衡天下，画地而不犯，兵加胡、越；至其晚节末路，张耳、陈胜连从兵之据，以叩函谷，咸阳遂危。
target_text: Jia Shan also highlighted the Qin Dynasty's failure to maintain stability despite its vast power, contrasting it with the Zhou Dynasty's more moderate rule. He noted that Qin's harsh laws and exploitation led to its downfall, while wise rulers like King Wen of Zhou attracted talented ministers through benevolence. He advised the emperor to cultivate virtue, reduce punishments, and encourage honest counsel. Later, Jia Shan opposed Emperor Wen's decision to allow private coinage, arguing it would undermine imperial authority. Despite his urgent remonstrations, Emperor Wen did not punish him, aiming to keep open the path for advice.

input_text: 自立天子之后，使东牟朱虚东褒义父之后，深割婴儿王之。壤子王梁、代，益以淮阳。 卒仆济北，囚弟于雍者，岂非象新垣平等哉！ 今天子新据先帝之遗业，左规山东，右制关中，变权易势，大臣难知。 大王弗察，臣恐周鼎复起于汉，新垣过计于朝，则我吴遗嗣，不可期于世矣。 高皇帝烧栈道，水章邯，兵不留行，收弊民之倦，东驰函谷，西楚大破。 水攻则章邯以亡其城，陆击则荆王以失其地，此皆国家之不几者也。 愿大王孰察之。 吴王不内其言。 是时，景帝少弟梁孝王贵盛，亦待士。于是邹阳、枚乘、严忌知吴不可说，皆去之梁，从孝王游。 阳为人有智略，忼慨不苟合，介于羊胜、公孙诡之间。 胜等疾阳，恶之孝王。 孝王怒，下阳吏，将杀之。 阳客游以谗见禽，恐死而负累，乃从狱中上书曰：
target_text: Zou Yang, a native of Qi, served under King Wu Liu Bi of Wu. When the king harbored rebellious intentions after his son's death, Zou Yang wrote a letter advising against rebellion, using Qin's fall as a warning. He argued that unity and loyalty to the Han court were essential, warning that rebellion would lead to destruction. When King Wu ignored him, Zou Yang joined King Xiao of Liang. However, he was slandered and imprisoned. From prison, he wrote to King Liang, citing historical examples of loyal ministers who were misunderstood, such as Jing Ke and Bian He, and urged the king to trust his sincerity. King Liang eventually released him and made him a guest.

input_text: 乘久为大国上宾，与英俊并游，得其所好，不乐郡吏，以病去官。 复游梁，梁客皆善属辞赋，乘尤高。 孝王薨，乘归淮阴。 武帝自为太子闻乘名，及即位，乘年老，乃以安车蒲轮征乘，道死。 诏问乘子，无能为文者，后乃得其薛子皋。 皋字少孺，乘在梁时，取皋母为小妻。 乘之东归也，皋母不肯随乘，乘怒，分皋数千钱，留与母居。 年十七，上书梁共王，得召为郎。 三年，为王使，与冗从争，见谗恶遇罪，家室没入。 皋亡至长安。 会赦，上书北阙，自陈枚乘之子。
target_text: Mei Cheng, from Huaiyin, also served King Wu and advised him against rebellion, warning that the Han Dynasty's strength far exceeded Wu's. He used metaphors like a thread holding a heavy weight to illustrate the danger of rebellion. When King Wu persisted, Mei Cheng left for Liang. After Emperor Jing ascended, Chao Cuo's policies provoked the Seven Kingdoms' rebellion. Mei Cheng again advised King Wu to withdraw, but the king refused and was eventually killed. Mei Cheng later served King Xiao of Liang and became famous for his writings. Emperor Wu later summoned him, but he died en route.

input_text: 唯陛下除诽谤以招切言，开天下之口，广箴谏之路，扫亡秦之失，尊文、武之德，省法制，宽刑罚，以废治狱，则太平之风可兴于世，永履和乐，与天亡极，天下幸甚。 上善其言，迁广阳私府长。 内史举温舒文学高第，迁右扶风丞。 时，诏书令公卿选可使匈奴者。温舒上书，愿给厮养，暴骨方对，以尽臣节。事下度辽将军范明友、太仆杜延年问状，罢归故官。 久之，迁临淮太守，治有异迹，卒于官。 温舒从祖父受历数天文，以为汉厄三七之间，上封事以豫戒。 成帝时，谷永亦言如此。 及王莽篡位，欲章代汉之符，著其语焉。 温舒子及孙皆至牧守大官。
target_text: Lu Wenshu, from Julu, studied law and the Spring and Autumn Annals. During Emperor Xuan's reign, he wrote a memorial advocating benevolence and lighter punishments, criticizing the harsh legal system inherited from Qin. He argued that severe torture led to false confessions and injustice, undermining peace. He urged the emperor to follow the virtuous policies of King Wen and King Wu of Zhou, reduce penalties, and open channels for advice. Emperor Xuan appreciated his petition and promoted him. Lu Wenshu later served as prefect of Linhuai, where he performed excellently until his death. His descendants became high-ranking officials.

input_text: 赵充国字翁孙，陇西上邽人也，后徙金城令居。 始为骑士，以六郡良家子善骑射补羽林。 为人沉勇有大略，少好将帅之节，而学兵法，通知四夷事。 武帝时，以假司马从贰师将军击匈奴，大为虏所围。 汉军乏食数日，死伤者多，充国乃与壮士百余人溃围陷陈，贰师引兵随之，遂得解。 身被二十余创，贰师奏状，诏征充国诣行在所。武帝亲见视其创，嗟叹之，拜为中郎，迁连骑将军长史。 昭帝时，武都氐人反，充国以大将军、护军都尉将兵击定之，迁中郎将，将屯上谷，还为水衡都尉。 击匈奴，获西祁王，擢为后将军，兼水衡如故。 与大将军霍光定册尊立宣帝，封营平侯。 本始中，为蒲类将军征匈奴，斩虏数百级，还为后将军、少府。
target_text: Zhao Chongguo, styled Wengsun, was from Shangbang in Longxi and later moved to Jincheng Lingju. He began as a knight, was promoted to a guard of the feather forest for his skill in horseback riding and archery, and was known for his calm courage and strategic depth. He studied military strategy and became familiar with barbarian affairs. Under Emperor Wu, he served as a fake Sima under the Second Division General against the Xiongnu, breaking through an enemy siege with over 100 strong men despite heavy casualties and over 20 wounds. Emperor Wu personally honored him, appointing him Zhonglang and later General of Chariots and Cavalry. Under Emperor Zhao, he quelled a Di rebellion in Wudu, was promoted to Zhonglang General, and later captured Xiongnu King Xiqi, becoming a post-general. He supported Emperor Xuan’s ascension with Huo Guang and was named Yingpinghou. During the Benshi period, he led a campaign against the Xiongnu, killing hundreds, and was appointed Hou General and Shaofu.

input_text: 匈奴大发十余万骑，南旁塞，至符奚庐山，欲入为寇。 亡者题除渠堂降汉言之，遣充国将四万骑屯缘边九郡。 单于闻之，引去。 是时，光禄大夫义渠安国使行诸羌，先零豪言愿时渡湟水北，逐民所不田处畜牧。 安国以闻。 充国劾安国奉使不敬。 是后，羌人旁缘前言，抵冒渡湟水，郡县不能禁。 元康三年，先零遂与诸羌种豪二百余人解仇交质盟诅。 上闻之，以问充国，对曰： 羌人所以易制者，以其种自有豪，数相攻击，势不一也。 往三十余岁，西羌反时，亦先解仇合约攻令居，与汉相距，五六年乃定。 至征和五年，先零豪封煎等通使匈奴，匈奴使人至小月氏，传告诸羌曰： 汉贰师将军众十余万人降匈奴。 羌人为汉事苦。 张掖、酒泉本我地，地肥美，可共击居之。 以此观匈奴欲与羌合，非一世也。 间者匈奴困于西方，闻乌桓来保塞，恐兵复从东方起，数使使尉黎、危须诸国，设以子女貂裘，欲沮解之。
target_text: When the Xiongnu mobilized over 100,000 cavalry near the border, Zhao Chongguo led 40,000 cavalry to garrison nine counties, causing the Shanyu to retreat. He later impeached Yiqu Anguo for disrespect after Anguo mishandled Qiang affairs. In the third year of Yuankang, Qiang chief Xianling formed alliances, and Zhao Chongguo warned of potential rebellion, citing past Qiang uprisings and Xiongnu collusion. He advised preparations, but Anguo’s subsequent actions—killing over 30 Qiang leaders and attacking their tribes—provoked a widespread Qiang revolt. Zhao Chongguo, over 70, was tasked with leading the campaign. He insisted on personal command, saying “seeing once is better than hearing a hundred times,” and Emperor Xuan agreed.

input_text: 充国常以远斥候为务，行必为战务，止必坚营壁，尤能持重，爱士卒，先计而后战。 遂西至西部都尉府，日飨军士，士皆欲为用。 虏数挑战，充国坚守。 捕得生口，言羌豪相数责曰： 语汝亡反，今天子遣赵将军来，年八九十矣，善为兵。 今请欲一斗而死，可得邪！ 充国子右曹中郎将卬，将期门佽飞、羽林孤儿、胡越骑为支兵，至令居，虏并出绝转道，卬以闻。 有诏将八校尉与骁骑都尉、金城太守合疏捕山间虏，通转道津渡。 初，罕、开豪靡当儿使弟雕库来告都尉曰先零欲反，后数日果反。 雕库种人颇在先零中，都尉即留雕库为质。 充国以为亡罪，乃遣归告种豪： 大兵诛有罪者，明白自别，毋取并灭。 天子告诸羌人，犯法者能相捕斩，除罪。 斩大豪有罪者一人，赐钱四十万，中豪十五万，下豪二万，大男三千，女子及老小千钱，又以其所捕妻子财物尽与之。 充国计欲以威信招降罕、开及劫略者，解散虏谋，徼极乃击之。 时，上已发三辅、太常徒弛刑，三河、颍川、沛郡、淮阳、汝南材官，金城、陇西、天水、安定、北地、上郡骑士、羌骑，与武威、张掖、酒泉太守各屯其郡者，合六万人矣。
target_text: At Jincheng, Zhao Chongguo crossed the Yellow River cautiously, avoiding enemy traps. He prioritized reconnaissance, fortifications, and soldier welfare, refusing to engage in small skirmishes. His son Zhao Yin led reinforcements, but Zhao Chongguo advocated a strategy of kindness and power, recruiting Qiang tribes like Han and Kai to disrupt enemy plans. Emperor Xuan assembled 60,000 troops, but Zhao Chongguo opposed a proposed attack by Xin Wuxian, arguing it risked logistical failure and enemy ambush. He recommended a defensive approach, focusing on farming and waiting for the enemy to weaken. Despite imperial pressure, Zhao Chongguo submitted a memorial detailing a plan to withdraw cavalry and station 10,281 soldiers for farming, listing twelve benefits including cost savings, enemy attrition, and border security. Emperor Xuan eventually approved his strategy.

input_text: 主亡子，主教钦良人习诈有身，名它人子。 钦薨，子岑嗣侯，习为太夫人。 岑父母求钱财亡已，忿恨相告。 岑坐非子免，国除。 元始中，修功臣后，复封充国曾孙伋为营平侯。 初，充国以功德与霍光等列，画未央宫。 成帝时，西羌尝有警，上思将帅之臣，追美充国，乃召黄门郎杨雄即充国图画而颂之，曰： 明灵惟宣，戎有先零。 先零昌狂，侵汉西疆。 汉命虎臣，惟后将军，整我六师，是讨是震。 既临其域，谕以威德，有守矜功，谓之弗克。 请奋其旅，于罕之羌，天子命我，从之鲜阳。 营平守节，屡奏封章，料敌制胜，威谋靡亢。 遂克西戎，还师于京，鬼方宾服，罔有不庭。 昔周之宣，有方有虎，诗人歌功，乃列于《雅》。 在汉中兴，充国作武，赳赳桓桓，亦绍厥后。
target_text: Zhao Chongguo’s campaign succeeded: over 10,000 Qiang surrendered, and by the following year, only about 4,000 enemies remained. He was praised for his foresight, though his son Zhao Yin committed suicide after a dispute. Zhao Chongguo retired with honors and died at 86. His portrait was placed in Weiyang Palace, and a eulogy by Yang Xiong celebrated his achievements. The text also covers Xin Wuxian and his son Xin Qingji, noting their military roles and eventual decline under Wang Mang. The commentary reflects on the martial traditions of western regions like Tianshui and Longxi, attributing the prevalence of generals there to proximity to Qiang and Hu peoples.

input_text: 赵广汉字子都，涿郡蠡吾人也，故属河间。 少为郡吏、州从事，以廉洁通敏下士为名。 举茂材，平准令。 察廉为阳翟令。 以治行尤异，迁京辅都尉，守京兆尹。 会昭帝崩，而新丰杜建为京兆掾，护作平陵方上。 建素豪侠，宾客为奸利，广汉闻之，先风告。 建不改，于是收案致法。 中贵人豪长者为请无不至，终无所听。 宗族宾客谋欲篡取，广汉尽知其计议主名起居，使吏告曰： 若计如此，且并灭家。 令数吏将建弃市，莫敢近者。 京师称之。 是时，昌邑王征即位，行淫乱，大将军霍光与群臣共废王，尊立宣帝。 广汉以与议定策，赐爵关内侯。 迁颍川太守。
target_text: Zhao Guanghan, a native of Zhuo Commandery, began his career as a county and commandery official, known for his integrity and talent. He was elected as Maocai and served as a market price regulator before becoming the magistrate of Yangdi. His exceptional governance led to his promotion to Lieutenant of Jingfu and acting Jing Zhaoyin. After Emperor Zhao's death, he executed the corrupt Du Jian despite powerful intercessions, earning praise from the capital. He participated in deposing King Changyi and establishing Emperor Xuan, receiving the title of Marquis of Guannei. As Governor of Yingchuan, he suppressed the powerful Yuan and Chu clans and used innovative methods like the "snitch bucket" to break up local factions, restoring order. His reputation spread even to the Xiongnu.

input_text: 所举应法，得其罪辜，属县长吏虽中伤，莫有怨者。 举廉为缑氏尉，历守郡中，所居治理，迁补都内令，举廉为弘农都尉。 征拜东海太守，过辞廷尉于定国。 定国家在东海，欲属托邑子两人，令坐后堂待见。 定国与翁归语终日，不敢见其邑子。 既去，定国乃谓邑子曰： 此贤将，汝不任事也，又不可干以私。 翁归治东海明察，郡中吏民贤不肖，及奸邪罪名尽知之，县县各有记籍。 自听其政，有急名则少缓之，吏民小解，辄披籍。 县县收取黠吏豪民，案致其罪，高至于死。 收取人必于秋冬课吏大会中，及出行县，不以无事时。 其有所取也，以一警百，吏民皆服，恐惧改行自新。 东海大豪郯许仲孙为奸猾，乱吏治，郡中苦之。 二千石欲捕者，辄以力势变诈自解，终莫能制。 翁归至，论弃仲孙市，一郡怖栗，莫敢犯禁。 东海大治。 以高第入守右扶风，满岁为真。 选用廉平疾奸吏以为右职，接待以礼，好恶与同之；其负翁归，罚亦必行。 治如在东海故迹，奸邪罪名亦县县有名籍。 盗贼发其比伍中，翁归辄召其县长吏，晓告以奸黠主名，教使用类推迹盗贼所过抵，类常如翁归言，无有遗脱。 缓于小弱，急于豪强。 豪强有论罪，输掌畜官，使斫莝，责以员程，不得取代。 不中程，辄笞督，极者至以鈇自刭而死。 京师畏其威严，扶风大治，盗贼课常为三辅最。
target_text: As Jing Zhaoyin, Guanghan was diligent and generous, attributing successes to his subordinates. He was skilled in the "hook distance" method of investigation, uncovering crimes with precision. He once prevented a kidnapping by negotiating with the kidnappers and later treated them with dignity before their execution. He also exposed private affairs with uncanny accuracy, such as knowing a pavilion chief's message before it was delivered. He increased the salary of traveling wardens to prevent corruption, leading to a well-governed capital. However, after General Huo Guang's death, Guanghan raided his son's residence, offending the queen and powerful relatives. He eventually fell from favor after a series of conflicts, including a false accusation against the prime minister's wife. Despite his integrity and popularity among the people, he was executed by waist-cutting.

target_text: Yin Wenggui, from Hedong, lost his father early and worked as a prison clerk. As a market official, he curbed the violence of Huo Guang's retainers. Governor Tian Yannian recognized his talent and appointed him to oversee half of the commandery's counties. He later served as Governor of Donghai, where he maintained detailed records of officials' conduct and arrested criminals during official meetings, instilling fear. He executed the cunning Xu Zhongsun, pacifying the region. As You Fufeng, he continued his strict governance, targeting the powerful while being lenient with the weak. He was known for his integrity and modesty, dying in office with no surplus property. The emperor praised him and granted gold to his family.

input_text: 敞为人敏疾，赏罚分明，见恶辄取，时时越法纵舍，有足大者。 其治京兆，略循赵广汉之迹。 方略耳目，发伏禁奸，不如广汉，然敞本治《春秋》，以经术自辅，其政颇杂儒雅，往往表贤显善，不醇用诛罚，以此能自全，竟免于刑戮。 京兆典京师，长安中浩穰，于三辅尤为剧。 郡国二千石以高弟入守，及为真，久者不过二三年，近者数月一岁，辄毁伤失名，以罪过罢。 唯广汉及敞为久任职。 敞为京兆，朝廷每有大议，引古今，处便宜，公卿皆服，天子数从之。 然敞无威仪，时罢朝会，过走马章台街，使御吏驱，自以便面拊马。 又为妇画眉，长安中传张京兆眉怃。 有司以奏敞。 上问之，对曰： 臣闻闺房之内，夫妇之私，有过于画眉者。 上爱其能，弗备责也。 然终不得大位。
target_text: Han Yanshou, from Handi, was promoted after his father died admonishing King Yan. As Governor of Yingchuan, he replaced Zhao Guanghan's confrontational methods with education in rites, consulting local elders and standardizing ceremonies. The people followed his teachings, abandoning lavish funerals. He later governed Shujun, hiring local worthies and promoting filial piety. He treated officials with kindness, blaming himself for their failures. As Zuo Fengyi, he resolved a land dispute by blaming himself, leading to the brothers' reconciliation. However, he was impeached for exceeding his authority and executed, despite public mourning. His sons resigned from office as he advised.

input_text: 天子引见敞，拜为冀州刺史。 敞起亡命，复奉使典州。 既到部，而广川王国群辈不道，贼连发，不得。 敞以耳目发起贼主名区处，诛其渠帅。 广川王姬昆弟及王同族宗室刘调等通行为之囊橐，吏逐捕穷窘，踪迹皆入王宫。 敞自将郡国吏，车数百辆，围守王宫，搜索调等，果得之殿屋重轑中。 敞傅吏皆捕格断头，县其头王宫门外。因劾奏广川王。 天子不忍致法，削其户。 敞居部岁余，冀州盗贼禁止。 守太原太守，满岁为真，太原郡清。 顷之，宣帝崩。 元帝初即位，待诏郑朋荐敞先帝名臣，宜傅辅皇太子。 上以问前将军萧望之，望之以为敞能吏，任治烦乱，材轻，非师傅之器。 天子使使者征敞，欲以为左冯翊。 会病卒。 敞所诛杀太原吏，吏家怨敞，随至杜陵刺杀敞中子璜。 敞三子官皆至都尉。 初，敞为京兆尹，而敞弟武拜为梁相。 是时，梁王骄贵，民多豪强，号为难治。 敞问武： 欲何以治梁？ 武敬惮兄，谦不肯言。 敞使吏送至关，戒吏自问武。 武应曰： 驭黠马者利其衔策，梁国大都，吏民凋敝，且当以柱后惠文弹治之耳。 秦时狱法吏冠柱后惠文，武意欲以刑法治梁。 吏还道之，敞笑曰： 审如掾言，武必辨治梁矣。 武既到官，其治有迹，亦能吏也。 敞孙竦，王莽时至郡守，封侯，博学文雅过于敞，然政事不及也。 竦死，敞无后。
target_text: Zhang Chang, from Hedong, gained fame for admonishing King Changyi. He warned Emperor Xuan about the Huo family's power, advocating for their removal. As Governor of Shanyang, he requested to suppress bandits in Bohai, using rewards and amnesty to disperse them. He also advised the Empress Dowager to stop hunting. As Jing Zhaoyin, he recruited thief leaders to capture others, arresting hundreds in one day. He was known for his wit and leniency, but his frivolous behavior, like thrushing his wife's eyebrows, drew criticism. He served for nine years but was dismissed after killing a subordinate. He later governed Jizhou and Taiyuan, dying of illness. His brother Zhang Wu also governed Liang effectively.

target_text: Wang Zun, from Zhuo Commandery, began as a prison clerk and studied the classics. As magistrate of Guo County, he executed an unfilial son by shooting. As Governor of Anding, he issued strict notices and killed the corrupt Zhang Fu, shocking the commandery. He was dismissed for excessive killings but later served as Governor of Yizhou, famously scolding his horse at a dangerous pass. As Prime Minister of Dongping, he confronted the arrogant king, who eventually avoided him. He impeached Prime Minister Kuang Heng for misconduct but was demoted. As Jing Zhaoyin, he eliminated bandits in Nanshan and executed powerful criminals, but was dismissed again. He later prevented a Yellow River flood by personally staying on the embankment, earning a promotion. He died in office, remembered by the people.

input_text: 我君素刚，先死者必君。 明日问之，章果死。 妻子皆徙合浦。 大将军凤薨后，弟成都侯商复为大将军辅政，白上还章妻子故郡。 其家属皆完具，采珠致产数百万。时，萧育为泰山太守，皆令赎还故田宅。 章为京兆二岁，死不以其罪，众庶冤纪之，号为三王。 王骏自有传。骏即王阳子也。 赞曰：自孝武置左冯翊、右扶风、京兆尹，而吏民为之语曰： 前有赵、张，后有三王。 然刘向独序赵广汉、尹翁归、韩延寿，冯商传王尊，杨雄亦如之。 广汉聪明，下不能欺，延寿厉善，所居移风，然皆讦上不信，以失身堕功。 翁归抱公洁己，为近世表。
target_text: Wang Zhang, from Taishan, was a blunt admonisher who slandered Zhongshu Ling Shi Xian, leading to his dismissal. Recalled by Emperor Cheng, he became Sili Xiaowei and later Jing Zhaoyin. He accused General Wang Feng of monopolizing power, leading to his execution for treason despite his wife's warnings. His family was exiled but later returned. He served for two years and was mourned by the people. The text concludes that Zhao Guanghan, Han Yanshou, Yin Wenggui, Zhang Chang, Wang Zun, and Wang Zhang were notable officials, though some met tragic ends due to their integrity or conflicts with power.

input_text: 郦食其，陈留高阳人也。 好读书，家贫落魄，无衣食业。 为里监门，然吏县中贤豪不敢役，皆谓之狂生。 及陈胜、项梁等起，诸将徇地过高阳者数十人，食其闻其将皆握龊好荷礼自用，不能听大度之言，食其乃自匿。 后闻沛公略地陈留郊，沛公麾下骑士适食其里中子，沛公时时问邑中贤豪。 骑士归，食其见，谓曰： 吾闻沛公嫚易人，有大略，此真吾所愿从游，莫为我先。 若见沛公，谓曰 臣里中有郦生，年六十余，长八尺，人皆谓之狂生，自谓我非狂。 骑士曰： 沛公不喜儒，诸客冠儒冠来者，沛公辄解其冠，溺其中。 与人言，常大骂。未可以儒生说也。 食其曰： 第言之。 骑士从容言食其所戒者。
target_text: Li Shiqi of Gaoyang was a learned man from a poor family who worked as a village gatekeeper. When various rebel generals passed through Gaoyang during the uprisings against Qin, he hid from them, considering them narrow-minded. Upon hearing that Pei Gong (later Emperor Gaozu of Han) was far-sighted, Li Shiqi arranged an introduction through a fellow villager serving under Pei Gong. Despite Pei Gong's disdain for Confucian scholars, Li Shiqi boldly criticized him for washing his feet while receiving visitors. Pei Gong apologized, and Li Shiqi advised him to seize Chenliu County, which had abundant food stores. Li Shiqi persuaded the magistrate to surrender, and Pei Gong captured Chenliu, granting Li Shiqi the title of Lord of Guangye. Later, when the Han army was besieged, Li Shiqi urged the King of Han to seize Aocang's grain supplies and strategic positions. He then volunteered to persuade the King of Qi to submit to Han, successfully convincing Tian Guang to surrender. However, Han Xin attacked Qi anyway, and Tian Guang, believing Li Shiqi had deceived him, executed him.

input_text: 平用其计，乃以五百金为绛侯寿，厚县乐饮太尉，太尉亦报如之。 两人深相结，吕氏谋益坏。 陈平乃以奴婢百人，车马五十乘，钱五百万，遗贾为食饮费。 贾以此游汉廷公卿间，名声籍甚。 及诛吕氏，立孝文，贾颇有力。 孝文即位，欲使人之南越，丞相平乃言贾为太中大夫，往使尉佗，去黄屋称制，令比诸侯，皆如意指。 语在《南越传》。 陆生竟以寿终。 朱建，楚人也。故尝为淮南王黥布相，有罪去，后复事布。 布欲反时，问建，建谏止之。布不听，听梁父侯，遂反。 汉既诛布，闻建谏之，高祖赐建号平原君，家徙长安。 为人辩有口，刻廉刚直，行不苟合，义不取容。 辟阳侯行不正，得幸吕太后，欲知建，建不肯见。
target_text: Lu Jia of Chu was a skilled orator who served as an envoy for Emperor Gaozu. He was sent to South Vietnam to grant Wei Tuo the king's seal. When Wei Tuo received him disrespectfully, Lu Jia warned him that the Han emperor could easily destroy him. Wei Tuo apologized and acknowledged Han's superiority. Lu Jia successfully secured South Vietnam's submission. Later, when Emperor Gaozu dismissed the value of studying the classics, Lu Jia argued that while one could conquer the world on horseback, one could not govern it that way. He wrote twelve essays explaining why Qin fell and Han succeeded, which became known as the "New Speeches." During Empress Dowager Lu's regency, Lu Jia retired but later advised Chancellor Chen Ping to ally with General Zhou Bo to counter the Lu family's conspiracy. His strategy helped preserve the Liu imperial house.

input_text: 平用其计，乃以五百金为绛侯寿，厚县乐饮太尉，太尉亦报如之。 两人深相结，吕氏谋益坏。 陈平乃以奴婢百人，车马五十乘，钱五百万，遗贾为食饮费。 贾以此游汉廷公卿间，名声籍甚。 及诛吕氏，立孝文，贾颇有力。 孝文即位，欲使人之南越，丞相平乃言贾为太中大夫，往使尉佗，去黄屋称制，令比诸侯，皆如意指。 语在《南越传》。 陆生竟以寿终。 朱建，楚人也。故尝为淮南王黥布相，有罪去，后复事布。 布欲反时，问建，建谏止之。布不听，听梁父侯，遂反。 汉既诛布，闻建谏之，高祖赐建号平原君，家徙长安。 为人辩有口，刻廉刚直，行不苟合，义不取容。 辟阳侯行不正，得幸吕太后，欲知建，建不肯见。
target_text: Zhu Jian of Chu served as prime minister to Yingbu, King of Huainan, and advised against rebellion. After Yingbu rebelled and was suppressed, Zhu Jian was rewarded. He was known for his integrity and refused to associate with the corrupt Marquis of Piyang, who was favored by Empress Dowager Lu. When Zhu Jian's mother died, Lu Jia advised the Marquis of Piyang to offer generous funeral gifts, which led to reconciliation. Later, when the Marquis of Piyang was imprisoned, Zhu Jian secretly instructed the emperor's favorite minister to plead for his release, saving his life. After Empress Dowager Lu's death, Zhu Jian's earlier advice helped protect the Marquis of Piyang from execution. During Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Zhu Jian was implicated in a case involving the Marquis of Piyang and committed suicide to protect his family.

input_text: 今陛下起丰沛，收卒三千人，以之径往，卷蜀汉，定三秦，与项籍战荥阳，大战七十，小战四十，使天下之民肝脑涂地，父子暴骸中野，不可胜数，哭泣之声不绝，伤夷者未起，而欲比隆成、康之时，臣窃以为不侔矣。 且夫秦地被山带河，四塞以为固，卒然有急，百万之众可具。 因秦之故，资甚美膏腴之地，此所谓天府。 陛下入关而都之，山东虽乱，秦故地可全而有也。 夫与人斗，不搤其亢，拊其背，未能全胜。 今陛下入关而都，按秦之故，此亦搤天下之亢而拊其背也。 高帝问群臣，群臣皆山东人，争言周王数百年，秦二世则亡，不如都周。 上疑未能决。 及留侯明言入关便，即日驾西都关中。 于是上曰： 本言都秦地者娄敬，娄者刘也。 赐姓刘氏，拜为郎中，号曰奉春君。 汉七年，韩王信反，高帝自往击。
target_text: Lou Jing of Qi advised Emperor Gaozu to establish the capital in Guanzhong rather than Luoyang, arguing that Qin's former territory had natural defenses and abundant resources. Despite opposition from ministers from Shandong, Zhang Liang supported this plan, and the emperor adopted it, granting Lou Jing the surname Liu and the title of Feng Chunjun. Later, when the emperor planned to attack the Xiongnu, Lou Jing warned that the Xiongnu were deliberately showing weakness to ambush the Han army. The emperor ignored this advice, was besieged at Baideng, and later released Lou Jing, rewarding him. Lou Jing then proposed a marriage alliance with the Xiongnu, suggesting the emperor send his eldest princess to marry the Chanyu. Although Empress Lu objected, a substitute princess was sent. Lou Jing also recommended relocating powerful clans from various states to Guanzhong to strengthen the region.

input_text: 通前曰： 诸生言皆非。 夫天下为一家，毁郡县城，铄其兵，视天下弗复用。 且明主在上，法令具于下，吏人人奉职，四方辐辏，安有反者！ 此特群盗鼠窃狗盗，何足置齿牙间哉？ 郡守尉今捕诛，何足忧？ 二世喜，尽问诸生，诸生或言反，或言盗。于是二世令御史按诸生言反者下吏，非所宜言。 诸生言盗者皆罢之。 乃赐通帛二十匹，衣一袭，拜为博士，通已出，反舍，诸生曰： 生何言之谀也？ 通曰： 公不知，我几不免虎口！ 乃亡去之薛，薛已降楚矣。 及项梁之薛，通从之。 败定陶，从怀王。 怀王为义帝，徙长沙，通留事项王，汉二年，汉王从五诸侯入彭城，通降汉王。
target_text: Shusun Tong of Xue served under Qin II, cleverly avoiding punishment by calling rebels mere thieves. He later served Xiang Liang, King Huai, and finally surrendered to the King of Han. Noticing the disorderly behavior of ministers at court, he offered to create court rituals. Despite criticism from conservative Confucian scholars, he adapted ancient and Qin rituals to create a practical system. After the completion of Changle Palace, the new rituals were implemented, impressing Emperor Gaozu, who remarked, "Now I know the dignity of being emperor." Shusun Tong was appointed Fengchang and rewarded with gold, which he distributed to his disciples. He later served as Crown Prince Tutor and successfully dissuaded Emperor Gaozu from replacing the crown prince. Under Emperor Xiaohui, he continued to formulate rituals and established the practice of offering fruits at ancestral temples.

input_text: 孔子曰： 导之以政，齐之以刑，民免而无耻；导之以德，齐之以礼，有耻且格。 老氏称： 上德不德，是以有德；下德不失德，是以无德。 法令滋章，盗贼多有。 信哉是言也！ 法令者，治之具，而非制治清浊之原也。 昔天下之罔尝密矣，然奸轨愈起，其极也，上下相遁，至于不振。 当是之时，吏治若救火扬沸，非武健严酷，恶能胜其任而愉快乎？ 言道德者，溺于职矣。 故曰： 听讼吾犹人也，必也使无讼乎！ 下士闻道大笑之。 非虚言也。 汉兴，破觚而为圜，斫雕而为朴，号为罔漏吞舟之鱼。而吏治蒸蒸，不至于奸，黎民艾安。 由是观之，在彼不在此。
target_text: Confucius taught that governance through laws and punishments only temporarily prevents wrongdoing without instilling shame, while governance through morality and rituals creates both shame and willing compliance. Laozi similarly distinguished between superior virtue aligned with nature and inferior virtue that is subjectively created. The text observes that excessive laws breed cunning and increase thieves, noting that laws are merely tools of governance, not its source. During the Han Dynasty's rise, broad and sparse legal frameworks allowed officials to flourish and people to live peacefully, demonstrating that effective governance depends not on harsh laws.

input_text: 至则诛瞷氏首恶，余皆股栗。 居岁余，郡中不拾遗，旁十余郡守畏都如大府。 都为人，勇有气，公廉，不发私书，问遗无所受，请寄无所听。 常称曰： 已背亲而出身，固当奉职死节官下，终不顾妻子矣。 都迁为中尉，丞相条侯至贵居也，而都揖丞相。 是时，民朴，畏罪自重，而都独先严酷，致行法不避贵戚，列侯宗室见都侧目而视，号曰 苍鹰 。 临江王征诣中尉府对簿，临江王欲得刀笔为书谢上，而都禁吏弗与。 魏其侯使人间予临江王。 临江王既得，为书谢上，因自杀。 窦太后闻之，怒，以危法中都，都免归家。 景帝乃使使即拜都为雁门太守，便道之官，得以便宜从事。 匈奴素闻郅都节，举边为引兵去，竟都死不近雁门。 匈奴至为偶人象都，令骑驰射，莫能中，其见惮如此。 匈奴患之。乃中都以汉法。景帝曰： 都忠臣。 欲释之。 窦太后曰： 临江王独非忠臣乎？ 于是斩都也。
target_text: The text then chronicles several cruel officials. Zhidu served Emperors Wen and Jing, known for his bravery, integrity, and harsh enforcement. He once prevented Emperor Jing from risking his life to save a palace attendant from a wild boar. As governor of Jinan, he executed the chief culprit among powerful clans, causing such fear that the county became orderly. He declared his loyalty to duty over family. The Huns feared him so much they carved his likeness for target practice but could never hit it. Despite Emperor Jing recognizing him as a loyal minister, Empress Dowager Dou had him executed for his role in Prince Linjiang's suicide.

input_text: 上幸鼎湖，病久，已而卒起幸甘泉，道不治。 上怒曰： 纵以我为不行此道乎？ 衔之。 至冬，杨可方受告缗，纵以为此乱民，部吏捕其为可使者。 天子闻，使杜式治，以为废格沮事，弃纵市。 后一岁，张汤亦死。 王温舒，阳陵人也。 少时椎埋为奸。 已而试县亭长，数废。 数为吏，以治狱至廷尉史。 事张汤，迁为御史，督盗贼，杀伤甚多。 稍迁至广平都尉，择郡中豪敢往吏十余人为爪牙，皆把其阴重罪，而纵使督盗贼，快其意所欲得。 此人虽有百罪，弗法；即有避回，夷之，亦灭宗。 以故齐赵之郊盗不敢近广平，广平声为道不拾遗。 上闻，迁为河内太守。 素居广平时，皆知河内豪奸之家。 及往，以九月至，令郡具私马五十匹，为驿自河内至长安，部吏如居广平时方略，捕郡中豪猾，相连坐千余家。 上书请，大者至族，小者乃死，家尽没入偿臧。 奏行不过二日，得可，事论报，至流血十余里。 河内皆怪其奏，以为神速。 尽十二月，郡中无犬吠之盗。 其颇不得，失之旁郡，追求，会春，温舒顿足汉曰： 嗟乎，令冬月益展一月，足吾事矣！
target_text: Ningcheng succeeded Zhidu as governor of Jinan, known for aggression and cruelty. After Zhidu's death, he became lieutenant and terrorized nobles. Under Emperor Wu, he was sentenced to shaving and iron collar, but escaped, became wealthy through land leasing, and wielded power greater than county governors. Zhou Yangyou was known for bending laws according to personal feelings, eradicating tyrants, and competing with superiors for power, eventually executed for his conflicts.

input_text: 汲黯为忮，司马安之文恶，俱在二千石列，同车未尝敢均茵冯。 后由为河东都尉，与其守胜屠公争权，相告言，胜屠公当抵罪，义不受刑，自杀，而由弃市。 自甯成、周阳由之后，事益多，民巧法，大抵吏治类多成、由等矣。 赵禹，斄人也。 以佐史补中都官，用廉为令史，事太尉周亚夫。 亚夫为丞相，禹为丞相史，府中皆称其廉平。 然亚夫弗任，曰： 极知禹无害，然文深，不可以居大府。 武帝时，禹以刀笔吏积劳，迁为御史。 上以为能，至中大夫。 与张汤论定律令，作见知，吏传相监司以法，尽自此始。 禹为人廉裾，为吏以来，舍无食客。 公卿相造请，禹终不行报谢，务在绝知友宾客之请，孤立行一意而已。 见法辄取，亦不复案求官属阴罪。 尝中废，已为廷尉。 始条侯以禹贼深，及禹为少府九卿，酷急。 至晚节，事益多。吏务为严峻，而禹治加缓，名为平。 王温舒等后起，治峻禹。 禹以老，徙为燕相，数岁，悖乱有罪，免归。
target_text: Zhao Yu served under Zhou Yafu, who recognized his integrity but considered him too harsh for important positions. Under Emperor Wu, he helped formulate legal regulations and became known for honesty, refusing all social invitations. Yi Zong rose from banditry to become an official through his sister's connection to the Empress Dowager. He governed with daring severity, eradicating powerful families in Hanoi. As governor of Dingxiang, he executed over 400 prisoners in one day. He was eventually executed for his actions.

input_text: 上幸鼎湖，病久，已而卒起幸甘泉，道不治。 上怒曰： 纵以我为不行此道乎？ 衔之。 至冬，杨可方受告缗，纵以为此乱民，部吏捕其为可使者。 天子闻，使杜式治，以为废格沮事，弃纵市。 后一岁，张汤亦死。 王温舒，阳陵人也。 少时椎埋为奸。 已而试县亭长，数废。 数为吏，以治狱至廷尉史。 事张汤，迁为御史，督盗贼，杀伤甚多。 稍迁至广平都尉，择郡中豪敢往吏十余人为爪牙，皆把其阴重罪，而纵使督盗贼，快其意所欲得。 此人虽有百罪，弗法；即有避回，夷之，亦灭宗。 以故齐赵之郊盗不敢近广平，广平声为道不拾遗。 上闻，迁为河内太守。 素居广平时，皆知河内豪奸之家。 及往，以九月至，令郡具私马五十匹，为驿自河内至长安，部吏如居广平时方略，捕郡中豪猾，相连坐千余家。 上书请，大者至族，小者乃死，家尽没入偿臧。 奏行不过二日，得可，事论报，至流血十余里。 河内皆怪其奏，以为神速。 尽十二月，郡中无犬吠之盗。 其颇不得，失之旁郡，追求，会春，温舒顿足汉曰： 嗟乎，令冬月益展一月，足吾事矣！
target_text: Wang Wenshu began as a thief but became an official known for managing prisons. As governor of Guangping, he recruited brave men as informants, concealing their crimes while executing those who failed him. As governor of Hanoi, he arrested over a thousand people, executing the worst and confiscating property, with blood flowing for miles. He regretted that winter ended before he could eliminate all thieves. He became lieutenant but committed suicide when facing execution for his crimes, with his entire family executed.

input_text: 延年本尝与义俱为丞相史，实亲厚之，无意毁伤也，馈遗之甚厚。 义愈益恐，自筮得死卦，忽忽不乐，取告至长安，上书言延年罪名十事。 已拜奏，因饮药自杀，以明不欺。 事下御史丞按验，有此数事，以结延年，坐怨望非谤政治不道弃市。 初，延年母从东海来，欲从延年腊，到雒阳，适见报囚。 母大惊，便止都亭，不肯入府。 延年出至都亭谒母，母闭阁不见。 延年免冠顿首阁下，良久，母乃见之，因数责延年： 幸得备郡守，专治千里，不闻仁爱教化，有以全安愚民，顾乘刑罚多刑杀人，欲以立威，岂为民父母意哉！ 延年服罪，重顿首谢，因自为母御，归府舍。 母毕正腊，谓延年： 天道神明，人不可独杀。 我不意当老见壮子被刑戮也！ 行矣！去女东归，扫除墓地耳。
target_text: Yan Yannian served as governor of Zhuojun and Henan, known for suppressing powerful families while protecting the poor and weak. He executed dozens from powerful clans, earning the nickname "Butcher." His mother rebuked him for relying on killing rather than kindness, predicting retribution. She returned home to prepare his burial place, and indeed he was later executed for his crimes. Yin Shang, as magistrate of Chang'an, built "Tiger Caves" - deep pits where he threw hundreds of criminals to die. He warned his children that being dismissed for cruelty was preferable to being dismissed for weakness.

input_text: 赞曰： 自郅都以下皆以酷烈为声，然都抗直，引是非，争大体。 张汤以知阿邑人主，与俱上下，时辩当否，国家赖其便。 赵禹据法守正。 杜周从谀，以少言为重。 张汤死后，罔密事丛，浸以耗废，九卿奉职，救过不给，何暇论绳墨之外乎！ 自是以至哀、平，酷吏众多，然莫足数，此其知名见纪者也。 其廉者足以为仪表，其污者方略教道，一切禁奸，亦质有文武焉。 虽酷，称其位矣。 汤、周子孙贵盛，故别传。
target_text: The text concludes that while these officials were harsh, some were upright and understood principles, while others flattered monarchs and stirred trouble. Their descendants became prominent, recorded in separate biographies.

input_text: 居鄛人范增年七十，素好奇计，往说梁曰： 陈胜败固当。 夫秦灭六国，楚最亡罪，自怀王入秦不反，楚人怜之至今，故南以称曰 楚虽三户，亡秦必楚 。今陈胜首事，不立楚后，其势不长。 今君起江东，楚蜂起之将皆争附君者，以君世世楚将，为能复立楚之后也。 于是梁乃求楚怀王孙心，在民间为人牧羊，立以为楚怀王，从民望也。 陈婴为上柱国，封五县，与怀王都盱台。 梁自号武信君，引兵攻亢父。 初，章邯既杀齐王田儋于临菑，田假复自立为齐王。 儋弟荣走保东阿，章邯追围之。 梁引兵救东阿，大破秦军东阿。 田荣即引兵归，逐王假，假亡走楚，相田角亡走赵。 角弟駹，故将，居赵不敢归。 田荣立儋子市为齐王。 梁己破东阿下军，遂追秦军。 数使使趣齐兵俱西。荣曰： 楚杀田假，赵杀田角、田駹，乃发兵。 梁曰： 田假与国之王，穷来归我，不忍杀。 赵亦不杀角、駹以市于齐。 齐遂不肯发兵助楚。 染使羽与沛公别攻城阳，屠之。 西破秦军濮阳东，秦兵收入濮阳。 沛公、羽攻定陶，定陶未下，去，西略地至雍丘，大破秦军，斩李由。 还攻外黄，外黄未下。 梁起东阿，比至定陶，再破秦军，羽等又斩李由，益轻秦，有骄色。 宋义谏曰： 战胜而将骄卒惰者败。 今少惰矣，秦兵日益，臣为君畏之。 梁不听。乃使宋义于齐。 道遇齐使者高陵君显，曰： 公将见武信君乎？
target_text: Chen Sheng, courtesy name She, was from Yangcheng, and Wu Guang, courtesy name Shu, was from Yangxia. When Chen She was young, he worked as a hired farmhand. Once, while resting, he expressed frustration and told his fellow workers that if they became rich, they should not forget each other. They laughed at him, but Chen Sheng sighed, "How can a sparrow know the ambition of a swan?" In the autumn of the first year of Qin II, the government sent 900 people, including Chen Sheng and Wu Guang as village chiefs, to guard Yuyang. They encountered heavy rain in Qidaze Township, blocking the road and causing them to miss the deadline, which was punishable by beheading. Chen Sheng and Wu Guang discussed that escaping or rising up both led to death, so they decided to die for the state. Chen Sheng noted that the people had long suffered under Qin's harsh rule. He proposed pretending to be Fusu, the eldest son of the First Emperor, and Xiang Yan, a beloved Chu general, to gain support. Wu Guang agreed. They consulted a fortune teller who hinted at using ghosts and gods to gain prestige. They wrote "King Chen Sheng" on silk and hid it in a fish, which soldiers found. Chen Sheng also had Wu Guang imitate a fox's cry at night, shouting, "Great Chu is rising, King Chen Sheng." The soldiers were frightened and talked about it the next day. Chen Sheng and Wu Guang, known for their kindness, killed the two escorting generals after Wu Guang provoked them. Chen Sheng addressed the soldiers, saying that missing the deadline meant death, and that strong men should leave a great name. The soldiers agreed, and they staged an uprising, pretending to be Fusu and Xiang Yan. They attacked Daze Township, Qixian, and other counties, recruiting troops along the way. By the time they reached Chen County, they had six to seven hundred chariots, over a thousand cavalry, and tens of thousands of infantry. They captured Chen County, and the local elders declared Chen Sheng king, known as Zhang Chu. Many counties killed their Qin officials in response. Chen Sheng appointed Wu Guang as acting king to attack Rongyang, and sent others to capture Zhao, Jiujiang, and Wei. Ge Ying, sent to capture territory, established Xiang Qiang as King of Chu but later killed him upon hearing of Chen Sheng's kingship. Chen Sheng then killed Ge Ying. Wu Guang besieged Rongyang but could not capture it. Chen Sheng appointed Zhou Wen as general to attack Qin. Zhou Wen gathered troops and reached Hangu Pass, but Qin general Zhang Han defeated him. Zhou Wen committed suicide after several defeats. Wu Chen proclaimed himself King of Zhao, angering Chen Sheng, but Cai Ci advised against killing his family. Chen Sheng sent an envoy to congratulate Zhao and moved the family to the palace. Zhao decided not to march west but to expand north into Yan. Han Guang, sent to attack Yan, was advised to proclaim himself King of Yan, which he did. Tian Dan killed the magistrate of Di County and proclaimed himself King of Qi, attacking Zhou Shi. Zhou Shi returned to Wei and made Ningling Junjiu King of Wei. Tian Zang and others killed Wu Guang, claiming he was arrogant and incompetent. Chen Sheng made Tian Zang a general, but he was killed by Zhang Han. Deng Yue and Wu Feng fled to Chen County after defeats. Chen Sheng killed Deng Shuo. Qin Jia and others independently raised armies. Chen Sheng sent Wu Ping Junpan to oversee them, but Qin Jia killed him. Zhang Han attacked Chen County, and Chen Sheng personally led the battle but was defeated. In December, Chen Sheng's coachman Zhuangmai killed him and surrendered to Qin. Chen Sheng was buried in Ci County. His old minister Lu Chen raised a "Cangtou Army," killed Zhuangmai, and made Chen County the capital of Chu. Song Liu, sent to pacify Nanyang, surrendered to Qin after hearing of Chen Sheng's death. Qin Jia appointed Jing Ju as King of Chu. Chen Sheng reigned for six months. His old friends came to see him but were killed for speaking freely, causing others to leave. Chen Sheng appointed Zhu Fang and Hu Wu, who were harsh, leading to his failure. Despite his death, the generals he appointed eventually destroyed Qin. Emperor Gaozu arranged for sacrifices to Chen Sheng's tomb, which continued until Wang Mang's time. Xiang Ji, courtesy name Yu, was from Xiaxiang. His uncle was Xiang Liang, son of Xiang Yan, a famous Chu general. The Xiang family had been generals for generations. Xiang Ji learned writing and swordsmanship but gave up, wanting to learn to resist tens of thousands. Xiang Liang taught him the art of war, but Xiang Ji only learned a little. Xiang Liang killed someone and fled to Wuzhong with Xiang Ji. When Qin Shihuang traveled to Kuaiji, Xiang Ji said, "We can replace him," shocking Xiang Liang. Xiang Ji was eight feet two inches tall, could lift a cauldron, and was feared by the youth of Wuzhong. In the first year of Qin II, Yin Tong, the acting governor of Kuaiji, discussed rebellion with Xiang Liang. Xiang Liang had Xiang Ji kill Yin Tong, then took control of the county, raising 8,000 elite soldiers. Xiang Liang became general of Kuaiji, with Xiang Ji as deputy. In the second year, Xiang Liang led 8,000 men across the Yangtze River. Chen Ying, who had raised 20,000 men in Dongyang, joined him on his mother's advice. Xiang Liang crossed the Huai River, and Yingbu and others joined him, totaling 60,000-70,000 men. Xiang Liang attacked Qin Jia, who had betrayed Chen Sheng, and killed him. He then heard of Chen Sheng's death and summoned generals to Xue County. Fan Zeng advised Xiang Liang to support a descendant of King Huai of Chu. Xiang Liang found King Huai's grandson, who was tending sheep, and made him King Huai of Chu. Xiang Liang called himself Lord Wu Xin. He defeated Qin forces at Dong'a and Dingtao but became arrogant. Song Yi warned him, but Xiang Liang ignored him. Qin reinforced Zhang Han, who defeated and killed Xiang Liang at Dingtao. Xiang Yu and Pei Gong retreated. Zhang Han, thinking Chu was weak, crossed the Yellow River to attack Zhao, besieging Julu. King Huai of Chu appointed Song Yi as general, with Xiang Yu as second-in-command, to rescue Zhao. Song Yi stopped at Anyang, refusing to advance. Xiang Yu killed Song Yi, claiming he was a traitor, and became general. He led troops across the Zhang River, sinking ships and burning supplies, and defeated the Qin army at Julu, killing Su Jiao and capturing Wang Li. The Chu army became dominant among the princes. Zhang Han, fearing Zhao Gao, surrendered to Xiang Yu after negotiations. Xiang Yu made Zhang Han King Yong and placed him in the Chu army. He then killed over 200,000 surrendered Qin soldiers at night. Xiang Yu entered Hangu Pass and arrived at Hongmen. Pei Gong had captured Xianyang, and Xiang Yu was angry. Fan Zeng advised attacking Pei Gong, but Xiang Bo saved him. Xiang Yu sacked Xianyang, killed Qin's prince, and burned the palace. He killed Han Sheng for criticizing him. Xiang Yu betrayed the agreement that the first to enter Guanzhong would be king. He moved King Huai to Changsha and divided the world, making Pei Gong King of Han, and others kings. He proclaimed himself Overlord of Western Chu. Tian Rong rebelled, and Xiang Yu attacked Qi, killing many. The King of Han attacked Chu, but Xiang Yu defeated him at Pengcheng, killing over 100,000 Han soldiers. The King of Han escaped and gathered troops. Xiang Yu besieged Rongyang, but the King of Han escaped. Fan Zeng died after being suspected. Xiang Yu defeated Peng Yue but lost Chenggao. He made a pact with the King of Han to divide the world, but the King of Han broke it. Xiang Yu was besieged at Gaixia, hearing Chu songs from all sides. He sang a tragic song, then escaped with 800 cavalry. Only 28 remained. He killed many Han soldiers but was surrounded. He refused to cross the Wu River, saying he had no face to see his people. He killed himself, and his body was divided by five Han soldiers. The King of Han buried him and spared his family. The text concludes with a praise, discussing Qin's rise and fall, and criticizing Xiang Yu's arrogance and failure to learn from the past.

input_text: 上纳其言，下诏复太上皇寝庙园。 顷之，使行流民幽州。举奏刺史二千石劳徕有意者，言勃海盐池可且勿禁，以救民急。 所过见称，奉使者十一人，为最，迁丞相司直。 坐法，左迁逆方刺史，复征入为太中大夫给事中，累迁长信少府、大鸿胪、光禄勋。 先是，太后姊子卫尉淳于长白言昌陵不可成，下有司议。 当以为作治连年，可遂就。 上既罢昌陵，以长首建忠策，复下公卿议封长。 当又以为长虽有善言，不应封爵之科。 坐前议不正，左迁钜鹿太守。后上遂封上。 当以经明《禹贡》，使行河，为骑都尉，领河堤。 哀帝即位，征当为光禄大夫、诸吏、散骑，复为光禄勋、御史大夫，至丞相。
target_text: Biographies of several Han Dynasty officials, highlighting their careers, virtues, and interactions with authority.

input_text: 胜之开阁延请，望见不疑容貌尊严，衣冠甚伟，胜之躧履起迎。 登堂坐定，不疑据地曰： 窃伏海濒，闻暴公子威名旧矣，今乃承颜接辞。 凡为吏，太刚则折，太柔则废，威行施之以恩，然后树功扬名，永终天禄。 胜之知不疑非庸人，敬纳其戒，深接以礼意，问当世所施行。 门下诸从事皆州郡选吏，侧听不疑，莫不惊骇。 至昏夜，罢去。 胜之遂表荐不疑，征诣公车，拜为青州刺史。 久之，武帝崩，昭帝即位，而齐孝王孙刘泽交结郡国豪桀谋反，欲先杀青州刺史。 不疑发觉，收捕，皆伏其辜。 擢为京兆尹，赐钱百万。
target_text: Jun Buyi, a native of Bohai, was known for his strict adherence to etiquette and expertise in the "Spring and Autumn." During the late years of Emperor Wu, he was summoned by the imperial envoy Baoshengzhi, who was impressed by his virtue. Jun Buyi arrived in full ceremonial attire, refusing to remove his sword, which he deemed a gentleman's essential tool. Baoshengzhi received him with respect, and Jun Buyi advised him to balance firmness with leniency in governance. Baoshengzhi recommended him to the court, and he became Governor of Qingzhou. He later thwarted a rebellion by Liu Ze, a grandson of the King of Qi, and was promoted to Jing Zhaoyin. His mother’s influence ensured he was dignified but not cruel in office. In the fifth year of Emperor Zhao’s reign, a man claiming to be Prince Wei appeared. Jun Buyi immediately arrested him, citing the "Spring and Autumn" to justify his action, earning praise from Emperor Zhao and General Huo Guang. He refused Huo Guang’s offer of marriage and later retired due to illness, dying at home. The imposter was later executed.

input_text: 征为博士、太中大夫。 地节三年，立皇太子，选丙吉为太傅，广为少傅，数月，吉迁御史大夫，广徙为太傅。 广兄子受字公子，亦以贤良举为太子家令。 受好礼恭谨，敏而有辞。 宣帝幸太子宫，受迎谒应对，及置酒宴，奉觞上寿，辞礼闲雅，上甚欢说。 顷之，拜受为少傅。 太子外祖父特进平恩侯许伯以为太子少，白使其弟中郎将舜监护太子家。 上以问广，广对曰： 太子国储副君，师友必于天下英俊，不宜独亲外家许氏。且太子自有太傅、少傅。官属已备，今复使舜护太子家，视陋，非所以广太子德于天下也。 上善其言，以语丞相魏相，相免冠谢曰： 此非臣等所能及。 广由是见器重，数受赏赐。 太子每朝，因进见，太傅在前，少傅在后。 父子并为师傅，朝廷以为荣。 在位五岁，皇太子年十二，通《论语》、《孝经》。
target_text: Shu Guang and his nephew Shu Shou served as tutors to the crown prince. Shu Guang, a native of Lanling, was learned in the "Spring and Autumn." He advised Emperor Xuan against appointing the prince’s maternal relative Xu Shun as supervisor, arguing that the prince’s teachers should be chosen from the world’s best. After five years, when the prince was proficient in the "Analects" and "Classic of Filial Piety," Shu Guang urged his nephew to retire with him, citing the principle of knowing when to stop. They resigned, receiving generous gifts of gold. Shu Guang used the gold to host feasts for his clan, refusing to buy land for his descendants, fearing wealth would lead to laziness or faults. He believed the emperor’s gift was meant for sharing with his community.

input_text: 定国遂称笃，固辞。上乃赐安车驷马、黄金六十斤，罢就第。 数岁，七十余薨。谥曰安侯。 子永嗣。 少时，耆酒多过失，年且三十，乃折节修行，以父任为侍中中郎将、长水校尉。 定国死，居丧如礼，孝行闻。 由是以列侯为散骑、光禄勋，至御史大夫。 尚馆陶公主施。 施者，宣帝长女，成帝姑也，贤有行，永以选尚焉。 上方欲相之，会永薨。 子恬嗣。 恬不肖，薄于行。 始，定国父于公，其闾门坏，父老方共治之。于公谓曰： 少高大闾门，令容驷马高盖车。 我治狱多阴德，未尝有所冤，子孙必有兴者。 至定国为丞相，永为御史大夫，封侯传世云。 薛广德字长卿，沛郡相人也。 以《鲁诗》教授楚国，龚胜、舍师事焉。 萧望之为御史大夫，除广德为属，数与论议，器之，荐广德经行宜充本朝。 为博士，论石渠，迁谏大夫，代贡禹为长信少府、御史大夫。 广德为人温雅有酝藉。
target_text: Yu Dingguo, from Donghai, learned law from his father Yu Gong, a fair judge. Yu Gong had once protested the wrongful execution of a filial widow, which led to a three-year drought until her innocence was acknowledged. Yu Dingguo became a court official, studying the "Spring and Autumn" with humility. As Tingwei, he was known for leniency and fairness, earning praise that no one felt wronged under his jurisdiction. He served as imperial censor and later replaced Huang Ba as prime minister, being respected by Emperor Yuan. However, disasters in Guandong led to imperial reprimands. Yu Dingguo apologized and eventually retired, dying at over seventy. His son Yu Yong and grandson Yu Tian succeeded him, though Yu Tian lacked his ancestors’ virtues.

input_text: 及为三公，直言谏争。 始拜旬日间，上幸甘泉，郊泰时畤，礼毕，因留射猎。 广德上书曰： 窃见关东困极，人民流离。 陛下日撞亡秦之钟，听郑、卫之乐，臣诚悼之。 今士卒暴露，从官劳倦，愿队下亟反官，思与百姓同忧乐，天下幸甚。 上即日还。 其秋，上酎祭宗庙，出便门，欲御楼船，广德当乘舆车，免冠顿首曰： 宜从桥。 诏曰： 大夫冠。 广德曰： 陛下不听臣，臣自刎，以血污车轮，陛下不得入庙矣！ 上不说。 先驱光禄大夫张猛进曰： 臣闻主圣臣直。 乘船危，就桥安，圣主不乘危。 御史大夫言可听。 上曰： 晓人不当如是邪！ 乃从桥。 后月余，以岁恶民流，与丞相定国、大司马车骑将军史高俱乞骸骨，皆赐安车驷马、黄金六十斤，罢。 广德为御史大夫，凡十月免。
target_text: Xue Guangde, from Pei, taught the "Book of Songs" and served as imperial censor. He was known for his outspoken advice, once urging Emperor Yuan to return from a hunt due to poverty in Guandong. Another time, he threatened suicide to prevent the emperor from crossing a river by boat, leading to a safer bridge crossing. After ten months, he resigned due to disasters and was dismissed, returning home with honor.

input_text: 定国遂称笃，固辞。上乃赐安车驷马、黄金六十斤，罢就第。 数岁，七十余薨。谥曰安侯。 子永嗣。 少时，耆酒多过失，年且三十，乃折节修行，以父任为侍中中郎将、长水校尉。 定国死，居丧如礼，孝行闻。 由是以列侯为散骑、光禄勋，至御史大夫。 尚馆陶公主施。 施者，宣帝长女，成帝姑也，贤有行，永以选尚焉。 上方欲相之，会永薨。 子恬嗣。 恬不肖，薄于行。 始，定国父于公，其闾门坏，父老方共治之。于公谓曰： 少高大闾门，令容驷马高盖车。 我治狱多阴德，未尝有所冤，子孙必有兴者。 至定国为丞相，永为御史大夫，封侯传世云。 薛广德字长卿，沛郡相人也。 以《鲁诗》教授楚国，龚胜、舍师事焉。 萧望之为御史大夫，除广德为属，数与论议，器之，荐广德经行宜充本朝。 为博士，论石渠，迁谏大夫，代贡禹为长信少府、御史大夫。 广德为人温雅有酝藉。
target_text: Ping Dang, from Pingling, was proficient in classics and served as prime minister under Emperor Ai. He argued for maintaining the Supreme Emperor’s mausoleum and temple gardens, citing filial piety. He also recommended relief for refugees and opposed granting a marquisate to Chunyu Chang, leading to his demotion. Later, he was recalled but fell ill, refusing to accept a marquisate under duress, and died after a month.

input_text: 治《易》，事张禹，举为博士，迁东平太傅。 禹以帝师见尊信，荐宣经明有威重，可任政事，繇是入为右扶风，迁廷尉，以王国人出为太原太守。 数年，复入为大司农、光禄勋、右将军。 哀帝即位，徙为左将军。 岁余，上欲令丁、傅处爪牙官，乃策宣曰： 有司数奏言诸侯国人不得宿卫，将军不宜典兵马，处大位。 朕唯将军任汉将之重，而子又前取淮阳王女，婚姻不绝，非国之制。 使光禄大夫曼赐将军黄金五十斤、安车驷马，其上左将军印绶，以关内侯归家。 宣罢数岁，谏大夫鲍宣数荐宣。 会元寿元年正月朔日蚀，鲍宣复言，上乃召宣为光禄大夫，迁御史大夫，转为大司空，封长平侯。 会哀帝崩，新都侯王莽为大司马，秉政专权。
target_text: Peng Xuan, from Huaiyang, studied the "Book of Changes" and served as a general. Emperor Ai dismissed him due to his kingdom origins, but he was later recalled. After Emperor Ai’s death, Wang Mang took power, and Peng Xuan resigned, citing old age. Wang Mang, resenting his resignation, denied him customary gifts. Peng Xuan died in his fief, and his title was later abolished.

input_text: 宣上书言： 三公鼎足承君，一足不任，则覆乱美实。 臣资性浅薄，年齿老眊，数伏疾病，昏乱遗忘，愿上大司空、长平侯印绶，乞骸骨归乡里，俟置沟壑。 莽白太后，策宣曰： 惟君视事日寡，功德未效，迫于老眊昏乱，非所以辅国家、绥海内也。 使光禄勋丰册诏君，其上大司空印绶，便就国。 莽恨宣求退，故不赐黄金、安车驷马。 宣居国数年，薨，谥曰顷侯。 传子至孙，王莽败，乃绝。 赞曰：隽不疑学以从政，临事不惑，遂立名迹，终始可述。 疏广行止足之计，免辱殆之累，亦其次也。 于安国父子哀鳏哲狱，为任职臣。 薛广德保县车之荣，平当逡遁有耻，彭宣见险而止，异乎 苟患失之 者矣。
target_text: The text concludes with praise for these officials: Jun Buyi for his wisdom and achievements, Shu Guang for timely retirement, Yu Dingguo for his fairness, and Xue Guangde, Ping Dang, and Peng Xuan for their integrity, contrasting them with those who cling to power.

input_text: 霍光字子孟，票骑将军去病弟也。 父中孺，河东平阳人也，以县吏给事平阳侯家，与侍者卫少皃私通而生去病。 中孺吏毕归家，娶妇生光，因绝不相闻。 久之，少皃女弟子夫得幸于武帝，立为皇后，去病以皇后姊子贵幸。 既壮大，乃自知父为霍中孺，未及求问。 会为票骑将军击匈奴，道出河东，河东太守郊迎，负弩矢先驱，至平阳传舍，遣吏迎霍中孺。 中孺趋入拜谒，将军迎拜，因跪曰： 去病不早自知为大人遗体也。 中孺扶报叩头，曰： 老臣得托命将军，此天力也。 去病大为中孺买田宅、奴婢而去。 还，复过焉，乃将光西至长安，时年十余岁，任光为郎，稍迁诸曹、侍中。
target_text: Huo Guang, courtesy name Zimeng, was the younger half-brother of the renowned general Huo Qubing. Their father Zhongru served as a county official in the Pingyang Hou family and had an affair with the maid Wei Shaoer, fathering Huo Qubing. After completing his duties, Zhongru returned home, married, and fathered Huo Guang, severing all ties with Wei Shaoer. When Huo Qubing later learned of his father's identity while serving as a hussar general attacking the Xiongnu, he visited Zhongru in Hedong, purchased lands and slaves for him, and took ten-year-old Huo Guang to Chang'an. Huo Guang was appointed as Lang and later promoted to various positions. After Huo Qubing's death, Huo Guang served as Guanglu and Commander-in-Chief, accompanying Emperor Wu for over twenty years with cautious conduct, earning the emperor's complete trust.
